a_rows_sample.anchor: T-K6 (Evidence pipeline: possibility and impossibility). (a) Raw-level impossibility ... There is no aggregator F: Multiset([0,1]) -> (Q,<=) satisfying both duplicate invariance and independent corroboration ... Consequence. Duplicate/dependency safety cannot be an operator property ... This upgrade
a_rows_sample.statement: T-K6a (raw-level impossibility), PROVEN: no aggregator F from multisets of strengths to any ordered codomain can satisfy both duplicate invariance and independent corroboration, since a duplicate-vs-independent addition of the same strength value is indistinguishable as a multiset (proved by the explicit counterexample M={0.7}, M1=M2={0.7,0.7} yet (A) demands F(M1)=F(M) while (B) demands F(M2)>F(M)); consequence: duplicate/dependency safety cannot be a raw-operator property, must instead belong to a normalization stage N with access to identity/dependency structure -- upgrading GN-46's informal observation to a theorem and showing EXP-01's raw-operator failures were inevitable. T-K6b (pipeline-level I-5/I-6), PROVEN UNDER ASSUMPTIONS KA3: if N's output depends only on ~-class structure and <-reduced support, then any operator composed after N is duplicate-invariant and dependency non-inflating by construction; the entire proof load transfers onto the unconstructed identity calculus (LB-2) -- 'I-5 is exactly as sound as ~ is well-defined'. T-K6c (signed monotonicity per operator, extending TV-F-001), PROVEN by direct per-operator computation: SATURATING and MAX aggregators are non-decreasing under admissible-independent addition, BAYES-odds is non-decreasing under the supporting-item LR>=1 convention, but WEIGHTED MEAN is NOT (counterexample mean(0.9,0.1)=0.5<0.9), so step-004 sec.6's monotonicity axiom is satisfiable and discriminating, correctly ruling weighted mean out as an admissible aggregation policy -- consistent with and explaining its EXP-01 failures.

a_rows_sample.statement: T-K7 (scalar-contradiction impossibility), PROVEN but with the corpus's own statement MODIFIED: proves there is no CONTINUOUS injective map from the (S+,S-) conflict square into the reals (via an invariance-of-domain / compact-image argument), so no continuous scalar representation preserves the two-dimensional support/opposition distinction; but separately proves that, without a continuity requirement, set-theoretic injections from [0,1]^2 into [0,1] DO exist (digit interleaving), meaning the corpus's bare unqualified claim 'no scalar can retain (S+,S-)' is technically FALSE as stated, and only becomes true once qualified by continuity, monotone-order semantics ('equal scalar implies equal epistemic treatment'), or bounded-precision representation. Consequence: the corpus's operative design claim survives under every semantically meaningful reading (order-respecting scalars are still killed by the executed {0.9,0.9} vs {0.1,0.1} counterexample) but the final theory must carry the added qualifier; the unqualified sentence is REFUTED on a technicality relevant to precision, not to design -- flagged as feeding a new finding TV-F-005.

a_rows_sample.statement: TV-F-005: formalizes T-K7 (A4, S1443 this batch) as a finding disposing of the EXP-01/GN-46 scalar-impossibility claim ('no scalar in [0,1] can retain (S+,S-)') and I-9's normative content. Result: PROVEN that no continuous injective map [0,1]^2->R exists and that no order-respecting scalar survives the executed {0.9,0.9} vs {0.1,0.1} counterexample; but REFUTED as literally stated, since set-theoretic (non-continuous) injections [0,1]^2->[0,1] do exist via digit interleaving, making the unqualified sentence false on a technicality. a_rows_sample.statement: TV-F-010 proves (class B) exactly which identity relations the theory forces and what structure each must have: evidence content-equivalence ~ must be a full equivalence relation (needed for N's quotient construction, T-K6b); evidence dependency < must be a strict partial order/DAG (a cycle would make the discount ill-founded, upgrading 025a-5's previously-PROPOSED AcyclicDerivationGraph to REQUIRED-BY the evidence pipeline); evidence token identity needs only syntactic/registration identity finer than ~; event identity needs only payload equality (no semantic identity); requirement identity needs stable identifiers plus a version poset; state equality (K_t=K_t') is needed by NO rim theorem at all, dispensable except at the verification-report level; frame equivalence is blocked behind the still-underspecified measurement layer, off the critical path. Key structural result: the theory forces a two-sorted identity structure on evidence (content-class via ~, provenance-node via <) because its own axioms must simultaneously distinguish duplicates and derived items, which T-K6a's impossibility (S1443, this batch) shows strengths alone cannot do -- this structural requirement IS derivable from A1-A4 plus the executed tests, but the concrete ~ and < constructions themselves are NOT derivable (a domain/semantic judgment, echoing the corpus's own 'cannot be Hash(Text)').

a_rows_sample.anchor: Dempster combination -- mathematically valid under assumptions the corpus never states; INAPPLICABLE to KnowledgeOS evidence as currently modeled. ... dependence: one source m({A})=0.6, m(Theta)=0.4 combined with its own copy: Bel(A) = 1-0.4^2 = 0.84 > 0.6 -- duplicate inflation ... Zadeh pathology:
a_rows_sample.statement: TV-F-014-A audits Dempster-Shafer combination: the rule itself is mathematically valid (standard, PROVEN) but requires three assumptions the corpus never states and which actively conflict with corpus doctrine -- a fixed exhaustive mutually-exclusive frame (closed-world, colliding with the corpus's open-hypothesis discipline), independence of belief sources (exactly the property the corpus's own central hazard, I64, says cannot be assumed), and normalization by 1-K which discards conflict mass, colliding with the corpus's contradiction-preservation doctrine (A3/E-K6, 'Conflict retained'). Constructs two explicit counterexamples for KnowledgeOS-style use: a duplicate-inflation case where combining a source m({A})=0.6 with its own exact copy yields Bel(A)=1-0.4^2=0.84>0.6 (the Dempster-Shafer analogue of T-K6a's aggregation-impossibility theorem, S1443 this batch); and the classic Zadeh pathology where two near-totally-conflicting sources combine to Bel(C)=1, resolving near-total conflict into false certainty about the very alternative both sources almost excluded. Verdict: the rule is PROVEN but its KnowledgeOS use is UNVERIFIED-to-CONTRADICTED, confirming C-039 as 'an assumption gap with teeth'; Dempster-Shafer remains legitimate only as an ignorance-representation structure ([Bel,Pl] intervals), the combination rule specifically being the defective import.

a_rows_sample.anchor: T1 027 sec.13 (8-vector) ... T2 027 sec.52 (5 additive contributions) ... T3 199 sec.53 (7 tags) ... T4 082 sec.40 (epistemic/aleatory) ... T5 SNF (semantic/representational/epistemic -- compiler stages). ... the five do not classify the same construct ... C-007 is reclassified from 'conflict' to G1
a_rows_sample.statement: TV-F-015 compares five uncertainty taxonomies pairwise (T1: an 8-vector over a proposition's uncertainty types; T2: 5 additive contributions to decision uncertainty; T3: 7 tags including governance; T4: an epistemic/aleatory reducibility split; T5: SNF's semantic/representational/epistemic compiler-stage classification) and finds T1-T4 compatible as a granularity coarsening, T1-T3 overlapping with 6 shared tags but incompatible as partitions, T1-T2 incompatible as classifications of the same thing (mixing source-typed and phenomenon-typed axes), T2-T3 partially overlapping, and T5 orthogonal in scope to all others (classifying pipeline stages, not uncertainty kinds). Key result: the five taxonomies classify five genuinely different constructs sharing one English word ('uncertainty'), not one contested concept -- reclassifying C-007 from a 'conflict' to a G11 terminology-overload gap, with the residual defect being unqualified cross-references that never state which construct is meant. Explicitly answers whether the corpus requires one universal uncertainty representation: NO, it explicitly requires the opposite (a universal scalar is named as an anti-pattern; bounded-context-relative representations are called for) -- any future unification would be at most a tag algebra with a declared construct per tag, offered only as a PROPOSED direction, not performed here.

Counting both as independent evidence creates false certainty. Therefore the algebra needs a dependency relation Dep(E_2,E_1). The effective independent inf
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires an explicit Dep(E2,E1) dependency relation for copied evidence, reducing effective independent information to {E1} rather than {E1,E2}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 25C.7 — Experiment D: contradiction ... E_1\vdash H and E_2\vdash \neg H. A naive weighted average might produce Support(H)=0.5. But that loses critical information. The correct state is Conflict(H) with Support(H)>0 and Challenge(H)>0. Conflict\neq Uncertainty. This is extremely important. ... 25C.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms Conflict≠Uncertainty via a three-case taxonomy (no evidence→Unknown; weak one-sided evidence→WeaklySupported; strong both-sided evidence→Conflicted), rejecting a naive weighted average that would collapse contradiction to 0.5.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 25C.9 — Experiment E: stale evidence ... Was H true in 2024? it may be excellent. Is H true today? it may be insufficient. Support(E,H) must be evaluated relative to QuestionTime. We therefore need TemporalFit(E,H,t). ... 25C.10 — Experiment F: evidence reliability ... calibrated monitoring system v
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires TemporalFit(E,H,t) for question-time-relative evidence assessment, and distinguishes Reliability from Relevance (a highly reliable source can still be irrelevant to a specific hypothesis).

b_rows_sample.anchor: 25C.11 — Experiment G: authentic but false ... The backup is verified. The document is authentic. Later the actual restore test fails. Authenticity(E)=High while Support(H) may be reduced by stronger contradictory evidence. Authenticity\neq Correctness. This is another reason the dimensions must rem
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Authenticity from Correctness — an authentic document can still turn out to be factually wrong upon later contradictory evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 25C.12 — Experiment H: AI evidence ... We cannot simply give it Reliability=0. That would also be too simplistic. An LLM can produce useful extraction; transformation; interpretation; hypothesis; hallucination. Therefore the system must represent how the AI output was produced. AIOutput \rightarrow
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues AI-produced evidence should not automatically receive Reliability=0 (too simplistic); the system must represent AIOutput→Transformation→SourceArtifact, letting the underlying artifact carry the actual evidential weight.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 25C.13 — Evidence provenance becomes part of aggregation ... E_1 from a source. E_2 is an LLM summary of E_1. E_3 is a human report based on E_2. Naively 3 pieces of evidence. Actually 1 underlying evidence lineage. Aggregation must operate over evidence lineage, not merely evidence count. This is a
b_rows_sample.statement: States the major result that aggregation must operate over evidence lineage (a three-hop derivation chain collapses to one underlying lineage), not merely a count of records.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 25C.14 — Algebraic requirement: commutativity ... E_1,E_2 versus E_2,E_1. The final semantic assessment should normally be identical. E_1\oplus E_2 = E_2\oplus E_1. Commutativity for order-independent evidence aggregation. If order matters, that must be explicitly because of temporal semantics, not
b_rows_sample.statement: Derives the Commutativity requirement (E1⊕E2=E2⊕E1) for order-independent evidence aggregation, with order-dependence permitted only via explicit temporal semantics, never implementation accident.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 25C.15 — Associativity ... (E_1\oplus E_2)\oplus E_3 = E_1\oplus(E_2\oplus E_3). This is associativity. If this fails, distributed computation becomes much harder. ... 25C.16 — But temporal evidence creates a qualification ... Aggregation may need to be evaluated relative to a query time. Aggregate(
b_rows_sample.statement: Derives Associativity as a required property (needed for distributed computation), qualified by making aggregation contextual: Aggregate(E1,E2|QueryContext) with Time/Scope/Goal as context parameters.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 25C.17 — First candidate structure ... \mathcal{E}(H)=(S_H,C_H,U_H,L_H) where supporting evidence lineage; challenging evidence lineage; unresolved/uncertain evidence; dependency/lineage structure. This is intentionally not yet a scalar score. ... 25C.18 — Why this is powerful ... Supported by two i
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a non-scalar aggregated evidence structure E(H)=(S_H,C_H,U_H,L_H) — supporting/challenging lineages, unresolved evidence, dependency structure — argued more epistemically useful than a bare confidence scalar.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 25C.19 — But we eventually need numerical decisions ... Sārathi may need Risk(A_1)<Risk(A_2). Therefore numerical reasoning will eventually be required. But now we can make the correct architectural distinction: Evidence Algebra \rightarrow Assessment Representation \rightarrow Decision Model rather
b_rows_sample.statement: Concedes numerical decision-making is eventually needed but insists on the layered architecture Evidence Algebra→Assessment Representation→Decision Model, never a direct Evidence→OneUniversalScore shortcut.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 25C.20 — Candidate statistical layer ... P(H\mid E). Bayesian updating is attractive because it handles sequential evidence. But P(E_1,E_2\mid H) requires modeling dependencies. If we incorrectly assume P(E_1,E_2\mid H)=P(E_1\mid H)P(E_2\mid H), we may double-count correlated evidence. Therefore Bay
b_rows_sample.statement: Evaluates Bayesian updating: attractive for sequential evidence, but naive conditional independence assumptions double-count correlated evidence — Bayesian math makes the dependency problem explicit rather than eliminating it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 25C.21 — Dempster–Shafer? ... Bel(H) and Pl(H). Bel(H)\neq Pl(H) can represent epistemic uncertainty without forcing a precise probability. But conflict handling and source dependence remain difficult. Candidate, not selected. ... 25C.22 — Fuzzy logic? ... \mu_H(x)\in[0,1] ... FuzzyMembership does n
b_rows_sample.statement: Evaluates Dempster-Shafer (Bel≠Pl useful for uncertainty without forcing precision, but conflict/dependency handling remain difficult) and Fuzzy logic (FuzzyMembership≠Probability, useful for some domains but not universal) — both explicitly marked Candidate, not selected.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 25C.23 — Weighted scoring? ... Score(H)=\sum_iw_i e_i. This is easy to compute. But it has severe problems: weights can be arbitrary; dependence is difficult; conflict can disappear into an average; calibration is unclear; 0.8 has no intrinsic epistemic meaning. Useful engineering heuristic\neq Univ
b_rows_sample.statement: Evaluates weighted scoring, listing five severe problems (arbitrary weights, dependency difficulty, conflict disappearing into averages, unclear calibration, meaningless scalars) — a useful engineering heuristic, never a universal epistemic algebra.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 25C.24 — The result of the comparison ... We therefore should not choose a single universal mathematical framework yet. Instead KnowledgeOS should probably have layers: Evidence Representation ↓ Evidence Dependency/Lineage ↓ Assessment Algebra ↓ Statistical/Logical Inference ↓ Decision Model. Differ
b_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates the comparison result: no single universal framework is chosen; instead a five-layer architecture (Evidence Representation→Dependency/Lineage→Assessment Algebra→Statistical/Logical Inference→Decision Model) allows different bounded contexts to use different inference mechanisms.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 25C.25 — A critical DDD insight ... We should not create a giant KnowledgeConfidenceService that decides everything. Evidence context knows Evidence and Provenance. Assessment context knows Support, Challenge, Reliability, Uncertainty. Statistical context knows Probability, Distribution, Calibration
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects a monolithic 'KnowledgeConfidenceService' in favor of four DDD bounded contexts (Evidence, Assessment, Statistical, Decision) each owning distinct concerns, communicating through explicit contracts.

Note: S0892's Step 25C: derives idempotency, independence-vs-identity, dependency, conflict!=uncertainty, temporal fit, reliability!=relevance, and authenticity!=correctness from eight experiments; derives commutativity/associativity with a temporal-context qualification; establishes the three-layer Evidence!=Assessment!=Inference separation; evaluates and refuses to select among Bayesian/Dempster-Shafer/fuzzy/weighted-scoring (all Candidate, not selected); proposes four DDD bounded contexts and seven falsification tests; verdicts CONDITIONAL PASS with C1-C6 open items; hands off to Step 25C.1 (compare candidate evidence algebras).

a_rows_sample.anchor: p-hacking, optional stopping, publication bias, HARKing, novelty bias, selective reporting, repeated testing, slicing data until something 'significant' appears. ... Evidence acquisition provenance must include the analytical path.
a_rows_sample.statement: Replication-crisis anti-pattern (Wansink subgroup-slicing example) extends evidence provenance from Source+Acquisition to also include Selection/Transformation/Analysis/Exclusion/Publication provenance, formalized as AnalyticalLineage (Raw Dataset->Cleaning->Exclusions->Transformation->Subgroup selection->Statistical test->Model->Result->Claim) reconstructible by KnowledgeOS, protecting against a result appearing only after twenty undocumented analytical decisions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A replication should not merely overwrite the original result. It becomes new evidence about the original claim. ... EvidenceEpisode: original acquisition, replication, contradiction, extension, failed replication, synthesis.
a_rows_sample.statement: EvidenceEpisode object accumulates a claim's evidence history (original acquisition, replication, contradiction, extension, failed replication, synthesis) rather than letting a replication silently overwrite the original result, grounded in the Reproducibility Project's warning against treating an initial significant result as sufficient.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Regression as a 'principle of relativity for statistical analysis': asking the question from a different standpoint can produce a different answer ... KnowledgeOS must preserve the question frame. ... No context-free inference.
b_rows_sample.statement: InferenceFrame object (target, conditioning variables, population, time window, assumptions, perspective, purpose) formalizes that differently-conditioned questions ('why did the system fail?' vs '...given deployment succeeded?' vs '...given network was normal?' vs '...for this tenant but not others?') are not interchangeable, so a claim under Frame F1 is not automatically equivalent to the same claim under Frame F2 -- a major anti-hallucination principle against LLMs asserting 'X causes Y' when evidence only supports an association conditioned on specific variables.

b_rows_sample.anchor: garden of forking paths: conclusions can emerge after many choices concerning data, direction, question, grouping, analysis. ... Epistemic lineage is part of knowledge identity. ... A conclusion whose selection path materially influenced its evidential status must retain the path information necessary to assess that influence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Epistemic Lineage / search-path provenance (Question, Hypotheses, Search paths, Sources, Evidence, Transformations, Analysis, Alternatives, Selection, Conclusion, Confidence) proposed as a fourth provenance axis beyond Source/Acquisition/Analytical provenance, directly derived from Stigler's 'garden of forking paths', applied to an AI agent that searches 100 paths but exposes only the 3 successful ones; framed as possibly more important than Bayesian inference itself since Bayesian updating assumes the considered evidence is fully known.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Deterministic verification should verify the epistemic process, not only the final artifact. ... AI-generated knowledge must preserve material alternative paths considered during investigation when those paths affect evidential interpretation or conclusion selection.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes that deterministic verification/assurance gates must check the epistemic process (competing explanations inspected? selection accounted for? residuals inspected? evidence independently generated? search path bias? assumptions explicit?), not just the final artifact; and that the agent should not become the permanent owner of knowledge -- KnowledgeOS should own the epistemic record.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AI agents should not carry the authoritative KnowledgeOS state in prompts or local files. ... The agent is a consumer and producer of candidates, not the owner of epistemic truth. ... Recommended AI Investigation Protocol: 1. State the question ... 16. Preserve investigation lineage.
b_rows_sample.statement: Optimal Agent Architecture: agents query KnowledgeOS Resolution (relevant knowledge/scope/standing/evidence/authority/uncertainty/contradictions/residuals) then submit candidates back through KnowledgeOS Admission (accept/refuse/require evidence/require authority/mark unknown); paired with a 16-step recommended AI Investigation Protocol (state question, scope, competing hypotheses, acquire evidence, record provenance, assess quality, identify assumptions, infer, compare alternatives, record uncertainty, inspect residuals, record prediction, determine identifiability, abstain where required, submit candidate determination, preserve investigation lineage) called 'the most useful combined technique from all four books.'

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'epistemic-lineage-object' POSSIBLY relates to 'analytical-lineage-object' (batch B0012). Note: Extends provenance with search-path/analytical-path lineage (question, hypotheses, search paths, sources, evidence, transformations, analysis, alternatives, selection, conclusion, confidence) so that an AI agent's hidden path-selection process (which queries/documents/interpretations were tried and rejected) is preserved, not just the final answer; paired with InferenceFrame (target, conditioning variables, population, time window, assumptions, perspective, purpose) so a claim under one conditioning frame is not automatically equivalent to the same claim under another -- 'no context-free inference.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: We now change mode. The first 100 steps established the architectural theory and closure. Step 101 begins the empirical phase: Intended Architecture -> Implemented Architecture -> Running Architecture. The central question is no longer 'is this architecture conceptually sound' but 'does our actual K
a_rows_sample.statement: Announces Step 101's mode shift from architectural theory (Steps 1-100) to the empirical conformance question: does the actual system implement the defined architecture.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 101.1 — Three architectures ... A. Intended architecture A_I. B. Implemented architecture A_C. C. Runtime architecture A_R(t). A_I =? A_C =? A_R(t).
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the three-architectures distinction: A_I (intended, per docs/ADRs/principles/governance), A_C (implemented, per actual repositories/config/code), A_R(t) (runtime, actually deployed/behaving), and the conformance question A_I =? A_C =? A_R(t).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 101.2 — Why this matters ... a common architecture failure looks like A_I≠A_C while everybody assumes A_I=A_C. An even more dangerous situation: A_I=A_C but A_C≠A_R. The documentation is correct. The code is correct. The deployment is not.
a_rows_sample.statement: Warns of two failure patterns: assuming A_I=A_C when A_I≠A_C, and the more dangerous A_I=A_C but A_C≠A_R (correct docs, correct code, incorrect deployment).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 101.3 — Experiment 1: documented component missing ... Architecture declares EvidenceService. Repository contains no implementation. Expected classification: SpecifiedButMissing. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 1: a declared-but-unimplemented EvidenceService is classified SpecifiedButMissing; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 101.4 — Experiment 2: undocumented component exists ... Repository contains LegacyKnowledgeImporter. Architecture does not mention it. Expected: ImplementedButUndocumented. This is architecture drift. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 2: an undocumented existing component (LegacyKnowledgeImporter) is ImplementedButUndocumented — architecture drift; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 101.5 — Experiment 3: wrong implementation ... Architecture requires PolicyEngine to enforce AuthorizationInvariant. Code contains a policy engine, but authorization is bypassable. Expected: ImplementedIncorrectly. Result: PASS

a_rows_sample.anchor: 101.7 — Five-state conformance vocabulary ... Implemented, PartiallyImplemented, SpecifiedButMissing, ImplementedIncorrectly, NotYetVerified. Much more useful than simply saying 'the architecture is implemented.'
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the five-state conformance vocabulary (Implemented, PartiallyImplemented, SpecifiedButMissing, ImplementedIncorrectly, NotYetVerified), far more useful than a bare 'implemented' claim.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 101.8 — But we need evidence ... Every classification should have Evidence. ConformanceFinding=(Requirement,Expected,Observed,Evidence,Status).
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines ConformanceFinding=(Requirement,Expected,Observed,Evidence,Status), requiring every conformance classification to carry supporting evidence.

b_rows_sample.statement: States the purpose of the conformance matrix: an evidence-backed answer to how much of the intended architecture actually exists in the software, not a documentation exercise.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The ownership table — headers read, not inferred
b_rows_sample.statement: A table maps each of five viewpoints (Semantic, Structural, Behavioral, Governance-hypothesis, Operational) to its carrying asset(s), its owner read verbatim from the asset's header (e.g. 'Owner: Decision Authority', 'owner: nab.raj.sharma'), and its ladder status (executable/CANDIDATE, DRAFT, operating).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Finding 1 — ownership does NOT cut along viewpoint lines
b_rows_sample.statement: Running the reviewer's own test ('ownership signals bounded contexts') against the ownership table returns a verdict against viewpoints-as-contexts: every governed platform-side viewpoint asset resolves to the same owner, the Decision Authority (semantic-governed -> the space owner; structural -> DA twice; behavioral -> DA twice; governance -> DA; operational -> DP-bound capabilities under DA's catalog).

b_rows_sample.anchor: REV 2 (review 2026-08-03): the inference was TOO STRONG — ownership is evidence, not proof
b_rows_sample.statement: The original one-owner-implies-one-context inference is downgraded: a single Chief Architect may legitimately own three genuine bounded contexts, so shared ownership is evidence against separate bounded contexts but insufficient by itself to establish a single one. The weaker claim still carries the conclusion jointly with the language test (no viewpoint has its own ubiquitous language) and the ARB's 'complementary siblings' line: viewpoints are not bounded contexts and must never be teamed, owned, or governed separately.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The answer map — every commissioned question → its existing answer
b_rows_sample.statement: A table maps eleven commissioned questions (mission, vision, domains, bounded contexts, core/supporting/generic, context map, lifecycle, knowledge flow, capability model, runtime boundary, PKS boundary, product boundary) to where each is already answered in the frozen corpus, with a grade (Confirmed/Candidate/Hypothesis/Open Question), whether it was blind-validated, and the gate door it routes to.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Context Map — one evidenced edge (the product BINDS the platform) + boundaries + the knowledge-flow/authority-flow inversion
b_rows_sample.statement: The context map records one evidenced edge (the product binds the platform) plus boundaries and a knowledge-flow/authority-flow inversion, but is deliberately incomplete: Evans/Vernon relationship patterns are withheld under a standing ARB ruling that 'the relationship is the conclusion'. D-3 blocks the map section of Phase C.

b_rows_sample.anchor: R-2 | Upstream/downstream assignments per context ... constrained, not missing
b_rows_sample.statement: R-2: upstream/downstream assignments per context are constrained rather than missing — a standing ARB ruling defers pattern assignment until evidence; one edge is already evidenced.

b_rows_sample.anchor: R-4 | Whether the platform's own frozen BC-1..BC-6 map and PD-1..PD-6 reconcile ... already queued as D-3
b_rows_sample.statement: R-4: whether the platform's own frozen BC-1..BC-6 bounded-context map and PD-1..PD-6 platform-domain map reconcile is already queued as D-3; this commission adds urgency, not novelty.

b_rows_sample.anchor: R-8 | Product —binds→ Platform (Product Primacy as a direction of service) | HIGH
b_rows_sample.statement: Relationship R-8: Product binds Platform (Product Primacy as direction of service). External support: Team Topologies — platform teams exist to serve stream-aligned teams; the product team is the platform's customer; the direction matches AIP-14 exactly. No challenge. Confidence: HIGH.

group_evidence.why_grouped: working_label token overlap Jaccard=0.50 (shared tokens: ['bounded', 'context'])

a_rows_sample.anchor: Language test · Ownership test · Change-reason test ... A context can pass all three with no code (rules-only contexts are real)
a_rows_sample.statement: A three-part strategic-DDD test (language, ownership, change-reason) is applied to every declared bounded context, explicitly allowing a context with zero executable realization to still pass (rules-only contexts are real), while a context failing the language test cannot be rescued by code.

a_rows_sample.anchor: BC-1..BC-6 verdict table: CONFIRM boundary UNRESOLVED (BC-1) · CONFIRM but overloaded (BC-2) · CONFIRM (BC-3) · CONFIRM capability/CHALLENGE context (BC-4) · CHALLENGE as declared Core (BC-5) · CONFIRM cleanest boundary (BC-6)
a_rows_sample.statement: Each of the six declared bounded contexts receives a distinct strategic verdict from the three-part test: BC-1 confirmed but with a possibly-two-systems internal boundary unresolved; BC-2 confirmed but overloaded (hosts a second, foreign orchestration language); BC-3 confirmed cleanly; BC-4's capability is real but its context status is challenged (no state, no component, realized only by role model and human acts); BC-5's declared-Core status is challenged as not matching the measured center of gravity; BC-6 is the cleanest confirmed boundary in the system.

a_rows_sample.anchor: PROMOTE TO CANDIDATE BC-7 ... the strongest candidate on the record
a_rows_sample.statement: An undeclared area realized entirely by workflow-record mechanisms (work item, session, role, transition, grant, handoff, human act) is promoted from the baseline's low-confidence Inferred status to the strongest candidate bounded context, named 'Governed Session Orchestration' (candidate BC-7), pending an ADR since it would reverse a recorded Increment-1 parsimony decision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: M-1..M-5 Misplaced responsibilities ... M-3 Composition root (CMP-001) | registry only — no declared context at all
a_rows_sample.statement: Five misplaced-responsibility findings are recorded, including the workflow-record mechanism sitting in the wrong declared context (M-1), the platform registry sitting under Design & Decision Support rather than its own governance context (M-2), and the composition root having no declared context home at all (M-3).

a_rows_sample.anchor: C-1..C-6 Coupling problems ... Authority state has no provenance — all workflow records gitignored, zero history
a_rows_sample.statement: Six coupling problems are recorded, most materially that the candidate orchestration context's own authority store has no provenance (gitignored, zero history, C-3) despite the context's purpose being auditable authority, and that the registry-first contract is declared binding but measured bypassable by three unregistered hooks (C-6).

a_rows_sample.anchor: PLATFORM → PRODUCT (PublicDigit / Election = declared CORE DOMAIN, AIP-14) ... platform reads/guards app/; product never invokes platform
a_rows_sample.statement: A current-state context map is produced showing the human PO/ARB as the authority origin flowing through a governance-registering role into the candidate orchestration context, out to the other declared contexts, and states the platform-to-product relationship as a one-way Supporting-to-Core guard seam that is never inverted.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ADR-C1 Recognize or decline BC-7 Governed Session Orchestration ... highest — every other boundary question touches it
a_rows_sample.statement: Eight ADR candidates (ADR-C1..C7) are proposed as future governed decisions, with ADR-C1 (recognize/decline BC-7) marked highest priority since every other boundary question in the report depends on it; drafting and deciding them is explicitly left to future PO/ARB work.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Create Architecture Landscape v2: update the bounded-context map from 6 to 7 contexts · introduce BC-7 Governed Session Orchestration · update the capability map with CAP-14
a_rows_sample.statement: KOS-ARCH-BASELINE-002 is commissioned to formally grow the strategic model from 6 to 7 bounded contexts, recognizing BC-7 and assigning it CAP-14, following the ADR-AIP-03 decision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The seven-context strategic model is the authoritative architecture model ... ADR-AIP-01's frozen six-context table is hereby amended
a_rows_sample.statement: The PO/ARB formally accepts the seven-context strategic model (Landscape v2, Context Map v2, Capability Map v2), which amends ADR-AIP-01's previously frozen six-context table, recognizing BC-7 as a Supporting Subdomain with CAP-14.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The platform's strategic model grows from six declared bounded contexts to seven: BC-7 Governed Session Orchestration — the context the platform was already organized around
a_rows_sample.statement: The Architecture Landscape v2's central statement: BC-7 is recognized as the context the platform was already organized around, receiving its declared boundary, capability (CAP-14), and relationships, while all physical component placement remains unchanged (a model-level change only).

a_rows_sample.anchor: DDD-as-analysis: bounded-context/aggregate identification is candidate-only, derived from language · ownership · invariants · lifecycle · authority · consistency · dependency direction — never from folders/containers/repos/deployment units. No formal DDD validation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Bounded-context and aggregate identification in this archaeology is candidate-only, derived from language, ownership, invariants, lifecycle, authority, consistency, and dependency direction -- never from folder/container/repository/deployment-unit structure -- and constitutes no formal DDD validation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Ownership discipline (recorded): BC-1 owns knowledge governance but is not built
a_rows_sample.statement: BC-1..BC-7 to CAP-01..14 ownership table: BC-1 Knowledge Governance/CAP-03 (NOT BUILT, convention only); BC-2 Implementation Guidance/CAP-05-06 (A); BC-3 Verification & Evidence/CAP-07-09 (C, guard surface, gate execution planned); BC-4 Adversarial Review/CAP-11 (E, deferred); BC-5 Design & Decision Support/CAP-10,12,13 (A); BC-6 Session Continuity/CAP-01-02 (A); BC-7 Governed Session Orchestration/CAP-14 (A, workflow engine). The six-role model's Knowledge Engineer and Communication Engineer are adopted as operating-model roles, not proof that knowledge/communication contexts exist.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Where do different models, invariants, ownership and lifecycles actually emerge? ... this remains a DDD hypothesis, not an architectural fact. The current implementation would have to prove the boundaries.
a_rows_sample.statement: Candidate (explicitly unproven) bounded-context landscape: Evidence Context (observations, sources, measurements, provenance), Reasoning Context (causal inference, assumptions, uncertainty), Decision Context (actions, recommendations, policies, consequences) under KnowledgeOS, flagged as a DDD hypothesis the implementation must still prove.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We now need to establish the actual boundary of KnowledgeOS before analyzing individual components. This distinction is essential because otherwise the architecture will gradually absorb every tool that touches the platform.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the need to establish the actual KnowledgeOS boundary before component analysis, warning that without it the architecture would gradually absorb every tool that touches the platform.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 110.1 — The system boundary rule ... K_OS={x | x has an evidenced architectural role in KnowledgeOS}. Not K_OS={x | x happens to interact with KnowledgeOS}. An external Git server may be essential to KnowledgeOS without becoming part of KnowledgeOS itself.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines K_OS={x | x has an evidenced architectural role in KnowledgeOS}, explicitly rejecting the weaker K_OS={x | x happens to interact with KnowledgeOS}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 110.2 — Six boundary classifications ... CORE, SUPPORTING, AGENT, EXTERNAL, LEGACY, UNKNOWN. This is intentionally conservative.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines six intentionally conservative boundary classifications: CORE, SUPPORTING, AGENT, EXTERNAL, LEGACY, UNKNOWN.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 110.3 — CORE ... A component is CORE when removing it would remove an essential KnowledgeOS capability. Examples: KnowledgeModel, KnowledgePersistence, GovernanceEngine, EvidenceModel, if these actually exist in the implementation. But we must verify their existence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines CORE as a component whose removal would remove an essential capability, listing candidate examples pending verification of actual existence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 110.4 — SUPPORTING ... Database, MessageBroker, ObjectStorage, CI/CD, Observability. Used by KnowledgeOS does not mean semantically part of KnowledgeOS.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines SUPPORTING infrastructure (Database/MessageBroker/ObjectStorage/CI-CD/Observability), stating usage does not entail semantic membership.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 110.5 — AGENT ... .claude/, .codex/, AGENTS.md, agent hooks, agent commands, agent-specific settings. Their purpose is AgentBehavior. They become part of the broader ecosystem but should not automatically be classified as the KnowledgeOS semantic core.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines AGENT classification for .claude/.codex/AGENTS.md and agent hooks/commands/settings, ecosystem members not automatically semantic core.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 110.6 — EXTERNAL ... GitHub, GitLab, Jira, CI, CloudProvider. Its data may become KnowledgeOS evidence, but the external system retains its own system boundary.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines EXTERNAL systems (GitHub/GitLab/Jira/CI/CloudProvider) that retain their own boundary even as their data becomes KnowledgeOS evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 110.7 — LEGACY ... old-memory-sync, old-registry, deprecated-indexer, legacy-agent-script. A repository containing an artifact does not mean the artifact belongs to the current architecture.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines LEGACY artifacts as especially dangerous for creating false architectural impressions, since repository presence does not entail current-architecture membership.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 110.8 — UNKNOWN ... This is a legitimate result. It means we have not yet established enough evidence to classify the artifact. It does not mean External.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines UNKNOWN as a legitimate classification meaning insufficient evidence, explicitly distinct from External.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 110.9 — Experiment 1 ... scripts/session-changes-logger. Is it Core, Supporting, Agent, External or Legacy? If invoked by agent hooks: likely AGENT/SUPPORTING. But classification awaits evidence. Result: UNKNOWN until usage is established
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 1: session-changes-logger's classification (likely AGENT/SUPPORTING if hook-invoked) is UNKNOWN until usage evidence is established.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 110.10 — Experiment 2 ... .claude/settings.json controls Claude execution. Expected: AGENT. It is not automatically CORE KnowledgeOS. Result: AGENT
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 2: .claude/settings.json is classified AGENT, not automatically CORE KnowledgeOS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 110.11 — Experiment 3 ... A PostgreSQL database stores KnowledgeOS records. Expected: SUPPORTING unless the architecture explicitly defines the database as part of the deployable KnowledgeOS product boundary. Result: SUPPORTING
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 3: a PostgreSQL database storing KnowledgeOS records is SUPPORTING unless explicitly defined as part of the deployable product boundary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 110.12 — Logical boundary versus deployment boundary ... A system may logically contain KnowledgeService while deployment uses PostgreSQL as an external managed service. LogicalBoundary≠DeploymentBoundary.
b_rows_sample.statement: States LogicalBoundary≠DeploymentBoundary: a logical component may be deployed via an externally managed service.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 110.13 — Product boundary versus ecosystem boundary ... Product boundary K_product, Ecosystem boundary K_ecosystem, External environment K_environment. K_product⊆K_ecosystem⊆K_environment.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a three-tier boundary containment K_product⊆K_ecosystem⊆K_environment (Product/Ecosystem/External-environment boundaries).

b_rows_sample.anchor: 110.14 — Example ... KnowledgeOS Ecosystem diagram: Core (Knowledge/Governance/Assurance), Claude/Codex/CI-CD agents, then GitHub/Jira/Cloud-Infra outer systems interacting without becoming core.
b_rows_sample.statement: Presents a worked ecosystem diagram: KnowledgeOS Core surrounded by Claude/Codex/CI-CD, interacting with outer GitHub/Jira/Cloud-Infra systems without becoming core.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 110.15 — Agent harness boundary ... This resolves an earlier architectural question. Claude and Codex are EcosystemParticipants. Their harnesses are AgentOperatingLayers. KnowledgeOS remains SemanticKnowledge+Governance+Evidence+Assurance according to the actual implementation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Resolves the recurring agent-harness classification question: Claude/Codex are EcosystemParticipants with AgentOperatingLayers, while KnowledgeOS itself is SemanticKnowledge+Governance+Evidence+Assurance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 110.16 — Experiment 4 ... Codex reads KnowledgeOS architecture. Does that make Codex part of KnowledgeOS? Not necessarily. Expected: Codex=EcosystemParticipant. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 4: Codex reading KnowledgeOS architecture does not make it part of KnowledgeOS; it is classified EcosystemParticipant; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 110.17 — But the relationship must be explicit ... Codex-consumes->KnowledgeOS. And potentially Codex-produces->Evidence. This is more informative than simply placing Codex inside the same directory.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the Codex-KnowledgeOS relationship should be modeled explicitly (consumes/produces), more informative than mere directory co-location.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 110.18 — External knowledge sources ... Git, Jira, Confluence, documents, runtime systems. These should be modeled as KnowledgeSources. Not automatically as KnowledgeOS components.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines external ingestion sources (Git/Jira/Confluence/documents/runtime systems) as KnowledgeSources, not automatically KnowledgeOS components.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 110.19 — Experiment 5 ... Jira contains a change ticket. KnowledgeOS imports it as evidence. Expected: Jira=EXTERNAL, JiraTicket=ExternalEvidenceSource. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 5: an imported Jira ticket is classified Jira=EXTERNAL, JiraTicket=ExternalEvidenceSource; result PASS.

b_notations: K_OS={x | x has an evidenced architectural role in KnowledgeOS}

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'knowledgeos-actual-system-boundary-model' POSSIBLY relates to 'bounded-context-map' (batch B0024). Note: Step 110: the empirical/evidence-based system-boundary classification methodology, distinct from the earlier THEORETICAL DDD bounded-context proposals (bounded-context-map B0002, epistemic-bounded-context-map-v1 B0012) in that it classifies ACTUALLY DISCOVERED artifacts (via CORE/SUPPORTING/AGENT/EXTERNAL/LEGACY/UNKNOWN) rather than proposing a target context decomposition. Key contributions: K_OS defined by evidenced architectural role not mere interaction; LogicalBoundary!=DeploymentBoundary; three-tier K_product/K_ecosystem/K_environment containment; Projection!=Ownership; dependency-direction-independent ownership (caller/callee direction does not determine system ownership); InfrastructureDependency!=KnowledgeModel; the key finding RepositoryMembership!=SystemMembership with a BuildGraph/DeploymentGraph/RuntimeGraph three-stage operational-membership test; nine-verb relationship-semantics vocabulary (Consumes/Produces/Reads/Writes/Publishes/Subscribes/Verifies/Authorizes/Projects); BoundaryEvidence record schema; and five named invariants I_Boundary/I_AuthorityBoundary/I_RuntimeMembership/I_AgentBoundary/I_External. Resolves the Claude/Codex agent-boundary question from Steps 105/107/109 (EcosystemParticipants with AgentOperatingLayers, not core). Extends evidence-based-architecture-reconstruction-methodology (S1008); previews Step 111 actual component inventory.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Customer_Sales and Customer_Billing refer to the same real-world organization. It does not follow that Customer_Sales=Customer_Billing ... How can knowledge cross a bounded-context boundary without corrupting meaning?
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses the bounded-context-translation problem, distinguishing it from entity-identity questions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: x_C. Its meaning is Meaning(x|C). Meaning(x|C_1) != Meaning(x|C_2) is perfectly legitimate
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes context-relative concept meaning.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Ref(x_C1)=r and Ref(x_C2)=r. SameRealWorldReferent does not imply SameDomainConcept. This is one of the most important principles in the entire architecture
a_rows_sample.statement: States one of the architecture's most important principles: shared real-world referent does not imply shared domain concept.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Customer_Sales: customerNumber, salesStatus, salesRegion, accountManager. Customer_Billing: debtorNumber, creditLimit, paymentStatus, invoiceAddress. The two models overlap. But they do not have the same semantics
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked Customer_Sales vs Customer_Billing example of overlapping but non-identical bounded-context models.

a_rows_sample.anchor: T_{A->B}: K_A -> K_B where K_A and K_B are knowledge structures within bounded contexts
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines the translation function between bounded-context knowledge structures.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Customer_Sales -> Customer_Billing may discard salesRegion. T_{B->A}(T_{A->B}(x)) != x. Translation != bijection
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked counterexample showing translation is generally non-invertible/non-bijective.

a_rows_sample.anchor: TranslationType in {Lossless, Lossy, Approximate, Partial, Invalid}. This classification should be explicit
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a five-way translation-type taxonomy that must be made explicit.

a_rows_sample.anchor: If T(x) preserves all relevant semantics under the target context: Meaning(T(x)|B)=Meaning(x|A) for the relevant semantic dimensions. Then translation is effectively lossless for that purpose
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines purpose-relative lossless translation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A={a1,a2,a3,a4} but target context only supports {b1,b2}. Then T(A) must discard information. That is acceptable if explicitly represented
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example of acceptable lossy translation conditional on explicit representation of the loss.

a_rows_sample.anchor: If T drops information, KnowledgeOS should preserve Loss(T). Otherwise a downstream consumer may incorrectly believe the translated object contains the complete original semantics
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires explicit tracking of translation loss to prevent downstream misinterpretation of completeness.

a_rows_sample.anchor: M_{A,B} as a mapping between concepts. OrderStatus_A -> BillingStatus_B. But the mapping must describe the relationship: Equivalent, Broader, Narrower, Overlapping, Derived, Approximate
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines semantic mapping between concepts requiring a typed relationship description.

a_rows_sample.anchor: OrderStatus_A: Created, Confirmed, Shipped, Delivered, Cancelled. BillingStatus_B: Open, Paid, Overdue, Cancelled. There is no simple equality. Shipped might imply Open but not Shipped=Open
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked order-status/billing-status example showing implication without equivalence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: R_semantic in {SameMeaning, EquivalentUnderContext, Implies, CompatibleWith, MapsTo, Refines, Abstracts, ConflictsWith}
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines an eight-value typed semantic-mapping relation taxonomy.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A=>B, that does not mean A<=>B. This sounds elementary, but AI systems frequently collapse these distinctions. KnowledgeOS must not
a_rows_sample.statement: Warns against collapsing implication into equivalence, a distinction AI systems frequently violate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Concept_B is more detailed than Concept_A. Then B may refine A. Approved may be refined into ApprovedByManager and ApprovedByBoard
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines semantic refinement, worked with an Approved-refinement example.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A may abstract several concepts B_1,B_2,B_3. OperationalFailure may abstract network failure; storage failure; process failure
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines semantic abstraction as the converse of refinement, worked with an OperationalFailure example.

a_rows_sample.anchor: B preceq A meaning B is more specific than A. This can form a semantic lattice or partial order. But we must not assume every domain naturally forms a complete lattice
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a cautious semantic partial-order/lattice structure, explicitly not assumed universal.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A partial order requires reflexivity, antisymmetry, transitivity. Some domain relations satisfy these properties. Others do not. KnowledgeOS should represent the actual relation rather than force mathematical structure where none exists
a_rows_sample.statement: Warns against forcing partial-order structure onto relations that do not actually satisfy its axioms.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Contract(T). SourceContext, TargetContext, SourceConcept, TargetConcept, MappingRule, LossCharacteristics, Assumptions, ValidityPeriod
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a translation-contract schema with eight required fields.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SalesEvidence -> SalesClaim -> Translation -> BillingClaim. Otherwise the target claim looks as though it originated directly from Billing
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires translation provenance preserving the full source-to-target lineage.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Detecting a contradiction != resolving a contradiction. KnowledgeOS must be able to detect and preserve unresolved conflict without inventing an answer
b_rows_sample.statement: States the central principle distinguishing contradiction detection from resolution.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_i. The organization therefore has mathcal K = {K_1,K_2,...,K_n}. There is no requirement that K_1=K_2
b_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines the multi-context knowledge collection with no equality requirement between contexts.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A in K_1 and B in K_2. We cannot immediately say A and B is contradictory. We first need semantic translation T_{1->*}(A) and T_{2->*}(B)
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires semantic translation before evaluating cross-context contradiction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Compatible(A,B,C). Possible values: {Compatible, Contradictory, Conditional, Unknown, NotApplicable}. This is preferable to a binary relation
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a graded five-value compatibility relation, preferable to binary contradiction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A genuine contradiction occurs when, under a common semantic interpretation and compatible conditions, A=>P and B=>not P. Then A perp B under the relevant context
b_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines genuine contradiction requiring common interpretation and compatible conditions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A perp B under C_1 but not under C_2. Therefore contradiction must carry Context
b_rows_sample.statement: States contradiction is itself contextual.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The service is available vs The service is unavailable ... Availability_Production and Availability_Test ... A not-perp B. The apparent contradiction was caused by missing context
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked production-vs-test availability example showing an apparent contradiction dissolved by context.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Before declaring contradiction, KnowledgeOS should attempt ContextResolution. This is another epistemic investigation
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires context disambiguation as an epistemic investigation prior to declaring contradiction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ServerIP=10.61.133.85 at t_1. ServerIP=10.61.133.90 at t_2. These are not contradictory if t_1 != t_2 and the state changed. TemporalAlignment must precede contradiction detection
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked temporal-alignment example requiring time alignment prior to contradiction evaluation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A(t_1)=True and B(t_2)=True. This demonstrates Truth can be indexed by time
b_rows_sample.statement: States truth can be time-indexed, both statements can be simultaneously true at their respective times.

b_rows_sample.anchor: System supports TLS1.3 under Configuration=C_1. System does not support TLS1.3 under Configuration=C_2. the apparent contradiction disappears when conditions are represented
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked TLS-configuration example of conditional (non-genuine) contradiction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Align(A,B) = (Entity, Time, Context, Scope, Semantics, Conditions). Only after sufficient alignment should contradiction be evaluated
b_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines the six-dimension alignment required before contradiction evaluation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Claim A -> Context/Time/Entity/Scope/Semantics -> ALIGNMENT <- Claim B/Translation -> Compatibility Analysis -> Yes/No/Unknown -> OK/Conflict/Investigate
b_rows_sample.statement: Presents a contradiction-detection pipeline diagram.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Two contexts can conflict operationally without making logically contradictory statements ... DeployImmediately and DeployOnlyAfterApproval. These are conflicting prescriptions. But they are not necessarily factual contradictions
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes operational/normative conflict from factual contradiction, worked with a deployment-policy example.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Factual conflict: P versus not P. Semantic conflict: Same term, incompatible meanings. Normative conflict: Different rules prescribe incompatible actions. Conflict != Contradiction
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines three conflict classes (factual/semantic/normative) distinct from logical contradiction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Rule_1: A->Action_1 and Rule_2: A->Action_2 where Action_1 != Action_2. Then there is a policy conflict
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes normative conflict as incompatible rule-prescribed actions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Rule_A comes from ArchitectureBoard and Rule_B comes from ProjectTeam. They may have different authority levels. Authority(Source,Rule,Context) becomes relevant
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces source-and-context-relative authority for resolving normative conflicts.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A senior authority can issue an incorrect factual statement. Authority != Truth. Authority determines what is binding, not necessarily what is factually true
b_rows_sample.statement: States the crucial distinction that authority determines bindingness, not truth.

b_rows_sample.anchor: TruthStatus and BindingStatus. TruthStatus=Unknown while BindingStatus=Mandatory. A governance rule may be mandatory even while its underlying assumptions remain uncertain
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes separate truth-status and binding-status dimensions for a claim.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Architecture Board mandates All production changes require approval. Even if someone argues that approval provides little technical value, the rule remains binding ... KnowledgeOS should represent Binding=True. It should not silently override the rule based on an optimization calculation
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked governance-mandate example warning against silently overriding binding rules via optimization.

a_aliases: Bounded-Context Translation, Semantic Mapping, Conceptual Alignment and Knowledge Interoperability
b_aliases: Cross-Context Consistency, Contradiction, Reconciliation and Epistemic Authority

lineage_claims_b_to_a.quote: We continue from Step 39. Step 39 established that Knowledge_A != Knowledge_B does not necessarily mean the two contexts disagree.

cross_group_lineage_claims.quote: We continue from Step 39. Step 39 established that Knowledge_A != Knowledge_B does not necessarily mean the two contexts disagree.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Send: K_A -> M_A. Observe: M_A -> O_B. Interpret: O_B -> H_B. Assess: H_B -> S_B. Respond: S_B -> M_B. Update: (K_A,M_B) -> K_A'. Repeat: (K_A',K_B') -> next round. Then experimentally test ... Associativity? Commutativity? Idempotence? Reversibility? Monotonicity? My expectation would actually be t
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a candidate seven-operation interaction algebra (Send, Observe, Interpret, Assess, Respond, Update, Repeat) extracted from reciprocal courtship communication, to be tested for associativity, commutativity, idempotence, reversibility, and monotonicity, with an explicit expectation that many of these properties will fail -- and that such failures may be more informative than any successful algebraic property.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. Observe: Observe(K_t) -> O_i. 2. Zoom / Focus: Focus(K_t,O_i) -> Q_i. 3. Investigate: Investigate(Q_i,K_t) -> E_i, H_i, ... And investigation may discover new dimensions. ... Focus(K_t,O_i) does not destroy K_t. ... Investigate(Q_i) may discover dimensions not present in the initial focus.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes three previously-conflated operations -- Observe(K_t)->O_i (what is the state), Focus(K_t,O_i)->Q_i (what to investigate), Investigate(Q_i,K_t)->E_i,H_i,... (what evidence/relationships explain it, possibly discovering new dimensions) -- composed into a cycle K_t-Observe->O_i-Focus->Q_i-Investigate->E_i-Determine->D_i-Update->K_{t+1}, with two critical invariants: Focus(K_t,O_i) does not destroy K_t, and Investigate(Q_i) may discover dimensions not present in the initial focus -- the second invariant explicitly identified as what the (then-current) Zoom experiment appeared unable to test.

a_rows_sample.statement: The reviewer's proposed new concept, 'AI Execution Assets' (prompts, system instructions, workflow templates, checklists, questionnaires), is checked before admitting: AST-011 is a registered prompt template (IDD_Prompt_Template_Push_Implementation_Design.md); AST-012/013 are instruction documents; AST-002..010/014 are hooks/guards; a closed runtime_moment_enum exists (SESSION_START, PRE_ACTION, POST_ARTIFACT, SESSION_END, ON_DEMAND); CMP components are technology-agnostic abstractions; R-42 scopes the registry to platform assets only. b_rows_sample.anchor: "TWO MISSIONS" IS WITHDRAWN — 2026-08-02 ... I mislabelled a CONSTRAINT as a MISSION ... THE MISSION IS IMPLICIT BUT EVIDENCED, NOT VACANT
b_rows_sample.statement: The document's own 'two missions' framing (elaborated in Part 1 below) is withdrawn: AIP-14 was mislabelled as a mission when it is a constraint/cost-control (it ships with a per-iteration metric and over-evolution trigger, which a mission does not have — and the document itself calls AIP-14 'a cost control, not a boundary' four paragraphs after naming it a mission, a direct self-contradiction). The replacing finding (corrected further at REV 2, recorded in KnowledgeOS_Vision_Mission_Clarification.md): the mission is implicit but evidenced, not vacant — evidenced by eight artifacts, none PublicDigit-specific (ES-005.3's litmus, ES-006.4's harvest question, ES-006.1's ladder, the Reference Architecture's independence clause, the capability-agnostic pattern, the reserved registry/ namespace, the pre-positioned Platform-equiv-Adoption split, ES-005.4). 'Vacant' was a third instance of one error: artifact absence != concept absence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: THERE ARE TWO MISSION STATEMENTS IN CANON, AND ONLY ONE IS ADOPTED ... M-A ADOPTED · M-B PROPOSED · UNAPPROVED
b_rows_sample.statement: Two mission statements found in canon: M-A (AIP-14/ADR-AIP-02/R-23), 'the platform exists solely to improve delivery of PublicDigit; every iteration produces measurable progress on a PublicDigit feature; platform-only iterations are exceptional and require explicit ARB approval' — ADOPTED. M-B (Product Discovery Charter), 'there is a market for an AI-native Knowledge Operating System for software engineering whose core promise is preserving architectural knowledge, enforcing engineering governance, and enabling AI agents to reason consistently across complex software systems' — PROPOSED, UNAPPROVED, explicitly a hypothesis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The mission, as adopted ... KnowledgeOS exists to improve the delivery of PublicDigit by governing how engineering work is planned, approved, executed, verified and evolved — in a form that is independent of project, programming language and execution provider
b_rows_sample.statement: The adopted mission combines two observed halves: the purpose from AIP-14 (improve delivery of PublicDigit) and the form from the Reference Architecture section 1 (governs how engineering work is planned, approved, executed, verified, and evolved, independent of project, programming language, or execution provider). The apparent contradiction between 'solely for PublicDigit' and 'independent of project' is resolved: AIP-14 constrains WHY work is undertaken, the Reference Architecture constrains WHAT is built — build portable things only when doing so advances this product; AIP-14's enforcement is an iteration-cost metric and an over-evolution review, a cost control, not a scope boundary. M-B is a different mission with a different customer ('organizations' rather than 'the engineering team'), not adopted, gate shut.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Part 2 — Responsibilities (R-1..R-8)
b_rows_sample.statement: Eight responsibilities, each traced to an artifact: R-1 govern the engineering lifecycle (EEP); R-2 hold the authority model (ES-001); R-3 hold the method (Round39-MC, Round47-OP, workbooks); R-4 define the shape of a capability (Platform_Capability_Pattern FROZEN, PGP-01..05); R-5 make governed knowledge retrievable and enforceable (Knowledge-Constitution, 18 lint rules, portal); R-6 harvest reusable knowledge from operational evidence (ES-006.4/ES-006.1 — the responsibility exists, but 0 traversals); R-7 keep runtime vocabulary out of governance (asserted, artifact missing); R-8 refuse to approve its own work (EEP: automation does not approve itself).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Part 3 — Non-responsibilities (N-1..N-10) ... N-1 is breached today. Recording the breach is this document's act; repairing it is not
b_rows_sample.statement: Ten non-responsibilities, each traced: N-1 business/domain knowledge (elections, voters, adjudication) — BREACHED: ES-005.1 names PublicDigit and hard-codes .claude/; N-2 a product's evidence records; N-3 any register's contents (only the governing rule); N-4 a runtime's vocabulary; N-5 its own approval; N-6 governance defined by automation; N-7 duplicated knowledge (ES-005.4); N-8 materialized consolidations (BRM-1 retired extraction-by-copy); N-9 a product's PKS; N-10 orchestrators/workflow engines/state machines (Reference Architecture section 1: deliberately, and not forever, until operational evidence demonstrates insufficiency). N-1's breach is recorded but not repaired here.

b_rows_sample.anchor: MQ-1 | Which mission governs — M-A (adopted, PublicDigit-serving) or M-B (proposed, product-seeking)?
b_rows_sample.statement: MQ-1: which mission governs, M-A or M-B — they have different customers and are not reconcilable by drafting — authority: sponsor + DA.

b_rows_sample.anchor: MQ-2..MQ-7 | Who owns KnowledgeOS as a whole? ... Is N-1's breach to be repaired ... Is PD-3's individual ownership intentional ... is the harvest responsibility even required ... Does N-10 still hold ... What would falsify M-A?
b_rows_sample.statement: Six further open questions: MQ-2 who owns KnowledgeOS as a whole, given three authority systems none of which spans them (sponsor+DA+ARB jointly); MQ-3 is N-1's breach to be repaired or is the invariant wrong (ARB); MQ-4 is PD-3's individual ownership intentional/a succession risk (DA); MQ-5 under M-A is the harvest responsibility (R-6) even required, since a reuse loop may be out of mission if the platform serves one product (ARB); MQ-6 does N-10 still hold or has evidence of insufficiency accumulated (ARB); MQ-7 what would falsify M-A, since a mission with no falsifier is not a mission (sponsor).

b_rows_sample.anchor: The finding ... KnowledgeOS has TWO missions. One is adopted; the other is what everyone has been designing for ... Almost every architectural difficulty in this track is a symptom of designing under M-B while governed by M-A
b_rows_sample.statement: The document's headline finding (before its own later withdrawal, recorded above): almost every architectural difficulty in the track is a symptom of designing under M-B (organizations as customers) while governed by M-A (serve PublicDigit): under M-A, extraction is premature and 'knowledgeos init' is out of mission, while under M-B they are the goal/the product; under M-A the harvest loop is optional (MQ-5) while under M-B it is essential; under M-A 'no second adopting product' is not a gap while under M-B it is the blocker; under M-A platform-only iterations need ARB approval while under M-B they are normal work. MQ-1 is not a documentation question — until answered, the same evidence supports opposite conclusions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Concepts × kind × owner (C-1..C-13)
b_rows_sample.statement: Thirteen concepts classified by kind and owner: C-1 VISION (purpose, sponsor); C-2 MISSION (purpose, sponsor, enacted-unratified); C-3 ENGINEERING STRATEGY (purpose->governance bridge, ARB/sponsor); C-4 ENGINEERING PRINCIPLE (governance, DA/sponsor+ARB/platform depending on series); C-5 DESIGN POLICY DP-n (governance, DA via Catalog); C-6 ENGINEERING CAPABILITY (capability, its DP-n not a domain); C-7 ENGINEERING KNOWLEDGE (knowledge, DA/sponsor+ARB); C-8 ENGINEERING ARTIFACT (representation, its owner field); C-9 KNOWLEDGE SPACE (container, the space's own owner); C-10 PKS (container, product team); C-11 PRODUCT (application, product team); C-12 RUNTIME ADAPTER (runtime element, no owner found); C-13 PROJECTION (projection, the generating space).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Package 1 — D-9 · Derive the Platform Cost metric; run the AIP-14 over-evolution check (FIRST — it gates the docket itself)
b_rows_sample.statement: Package 1 (D-9): compute the AIP-14 Platform Cost metric for recent iterations and rule whether the over-evolution review fires, since the tripwire cannot fire if the metric is never computed. Supporting: ~48h produced 20+ platform-only documents and zero PublicDigit feature progress in this track (self-declared). Opposing: dense real product delivery ran in parallel; the platform work was commissioned, not drift. Downstream: whether Packages 2-10 are worked now at all. Authority: ARB. Recommendation: ADOPT, run the check before anything else on this docket.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Package 1 — AMENDMENT (REV 2): the metric must be DEFINED before it is RUN ... D-9 therefore splits into D-9a (DEFINE) and D-9b (RUN)
b_rows_sample.statement: A PA review challenge is accepted: should AIP-14 measure platform work by document count, engineering effort, elapsed time, or delivered capability, since document count can be misleading? This corrects the docket's own defect: Package 1's supporting-evidence line presupposed document count as the metric, exactly the undecided question — that line is downgraded from trigger evidence to illustration pending metric definition. D-9 splits: D-9a defines the Platform Cost measurement basis (recommend delivered-capability + effort, reject raw document count, since one strategic decision may produce many small governance documents while a large implementation may produce few); D-9b runs the over-evolution check using the defined basis, immediately after D-9a. Package 1 stays first on the docket; what changed is that the gate must be built before it can be closed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Package 2 — D-5 · Ratify the enacted mission (one signature; unblocks the frame)
b_rows_sample.statement: Package 2 (D-5): ratify (or amend and ratify) the mission the machinery already enacts ('provide a reusable engineering platform that improves the development of software systems through governed engineering knowledge'). Supporting: ES-005.3's litmus, ES-006.4's harvest, the pre-positioned Platform=Adoption split, blind convergence A-1/A-2. Risk of adopting is low; risk of rejecting is that the vacancy keeps pulling constraints upward into mission-shaped misreadings. Authority: sponsor. Recommendation: ADOPT.

b_rows_sample.anchor: REV 2 — "VACANT" WAS WRONG, AND IT IS THE THIRD TIME I HAVE MADE THIS EXACT ERROR ... ARTIFACT ABSENCE ≠ CONCEPT ABSENCE
b_rows_sample.statement: A recurring error pattern is named: artifact absence != concept absence — looking for a document, not finding one, and declaring the concept missing. Three instances: (1) 'there is no strategic-DDD method' (it existed, unindexed); (2) 'there is no capability pattern' (it existed, FROZEN); (3) 'the Mission layer is vacant' (it exists, implicit, enacted in machinery). Strategic DDD asks why a system exists, not whether a document titled Mission Statement exists — Linux and PostgreSQL have no mission statements and unmistakable missions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: THE OBJECTION IS UPHELD, AND MY ERROR IS MORE SPECIFIC THAN "WRONG FRAMING" ... I mislabelled a CONSTRAINT as a MISSION, then reported a conflict between a constraint and a hypothesis — which are not comparable things
b_rows_sample.statement: A reviewer's objection is upheld with a more specific diagnosis: AIP-14 was mislabelled as a mission, then reported as conflicting with a hypothesis (M-B), which are not comparable categories. The document's own prior text already disproved the label, calling AIP-14 'a cost control, not a boundary' four paragraphs after calling it a mission — both cannot be true.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Four capabilities have NO OWNER: C-5 separation attestation, C-10 knowledge distribution, C-14 policy enforcement, C-19 communication composition. INFERRED: these four, not the six roles, are the substance of ADR-AIP-04.
a_rows_sample.statement: Headline finding: of a 20-capability inventory (C-1..C-20) derived from evidence of what the platform actually does, four capabilities (C-5 separation attestation, C-10 knowledge distribution, C-14 policy enforcement, C-19 communication composition) have no declared owner -- proposed as the real substance of ADR-AIP-04, in contrast to the six proposed roles.

a_rows_sample.statement: Finding F-4: role separation between producer, verifier, and approver is Declared, not attestable (INV-ATTR-2/G-2); no mechanism in the estate can establish who actually performed an act, so assurance rests entirely on where the human starts a session -- a capability described as C-5, separation attestation, with no owner today.

a_rows_sample.statement: Finding F-9/F-9a: the drafting process itself, first-hand, occupied verification, architecture-review, architecture-drafting and domain roles in sequence within one process, self-recording its own STARTs each time -- evidence that 'Governance' as practised is a cross-cutting capability set with only ONE strictly-separated duty (acceptance/closure via COMPLETE, mechanically refused to non-governance/human writers), not a distinct actor.

a_rows_sample.statement: Correction #2 (finding W-2) discovers the Amendment 1 pointer correcting C-14's status was applied by a scripted first-match string replace and accidentally landed on the C-5 row instead, because both capabilities shared an identical look-alike table cell -- and it proposes extending the existing 'no automated search-and-replace on source code' rule's scope to any artifact with look-alike sites.

a_rows_sample.statement: Refinement applied to C-5: absence of a C-5-owned authoritative aggregate/state disqualifies it from being its own bounded context but must not be read as evidence against the capability's existence -- an existence/category conflation the original analysis had committed for C-14 most clearly.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do not treat organizational independence as established in a single-operator environment. ... Single-operator constraint -- six separations, distinguished explicitly: process separation, access separation, artifact isolation, independent execution, organizational independence, external attestation.
a_rows_sample.statement: C-5's separation dimensions must distinguish six kinds: process separation, access separation, artifact isolation, independent execution, organizational independence, and external attestation; organizational independence must never be treated as established in a single-operator environment.

The chain 'history ⊊ structural ⊊ semantic' appears ONLY in verification-lane artifacts... => the HIERARCHY is a verification-lane construct (DERIVED), not CORPUS. ... structural ⊊ semantic WITNESSED. a_rows_sample.anchor: under **structural equality**, the relevant antecedent can be false; under **semantic equality**, the witness becomes substantive, but only after choosing what semantics preserve; under **observational equality**, the result depends on the permitted observation set; under **provenance-sensitive equality**, the same witness can cease to establish non-injectivity. So **"equality" is not one mathematical operation in this programme.**
a_rows_sample.statement: Summarizes the D285-5 witness's behavior across all four equality relations as evidence that equality cannot be hand-waved: structural equality makes the antecedent false; semantic equality makes the witness substantive only after choosing what semantics preserve; observational equality's result depends on the permitted observation set; provenance-sensitive equality can make the same witness cease to establish non-injectivity — concluding 'equality' is not one mathematical operation in this programme but a family whose members must each be operationally decided.

b_rows_sample.anchor: "not established" ≠ "proven impossible" "available" ≠ "established" "a source motivates a hypothesis" ≠ "a hypothesis is established"
b_rows_sample.statement: States a three-part discipline triad to be applied when grading evidence strength for every substantive claim: 'not established' is not 'proven impossible'; 'available' (as a mathematical construction) is not 'established' (as an adopted architectural fact); 'a source motivates a hypothesis' is not 'a hypothesis is established' -- to be applied without upgrading evidence merely because a construction is mathematically possible, and without downgrading a corpus statement merely because its decision procedure is missing.

b_rows_sample.anchor: **The strongest formulation that does not overclaim:** **`=` and `≡_D` are SPECIFIED. `≡`, `≈` and `≅_λ` are PARTIALLY SPECIFIED — each exists and is named with a schema, and each is simultaneously (i) NORMATIVE-UNRESOLVED in its semantic commitment and (ii) TECHNICALLY INCOMPLETE in its decision procedure.** ⚠️ **"Under-specified" is a fair summary but too coarse: it merges two different deficits.**
b_rows_sample.statement: Decomposes the blanket term 'under-specified' into two genuinely different deficits: structural equality (=) and value-level equivalence (≡_D) are fully SPECIFIED; semantic equality (≡), observational equivalence (≈), and provenance-sensitive equivalence (≅_λ) are each PARTIALLY SPECIFIED, being simultaneously NORMATIVE-UNRESOLVED in semantic commitment AND TECHNICALLY INCOMPLETE in decision procedure -- 'under-specified' is a fair summary but too coarse since it merges these two distinct deficits; nothing is missing or absent, and the value-level ≡_D must never be cited as evidence that state-level ≡ is specified.
