a_rows_sample.anchor: How do we ensure that a KnowledgeOS decision gate can never authorize a state that violates a mandatory invariant?
a_rows_sample.statement: Three distinct questions must be separated: Question 1 (Epistemic) 'Do we have sufficient knowledge?'; Question 2 (Logical) 'Are the decision conditions internally consistent?'; Question 3 (Governance/safety) 'Is the resulting action permitted?'. Therefore SufficientKnowledge != ValidDecision != AuthorizedAction. This distinction is stated as fundamental, moving the investigation from 'do we know enough' to 'is the decision formally admissible'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DC(d)=(Pre,Inv,Auth,Post,Temporal,Evidence)
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a first-version Decision Contract DC(d) = (Pre, Inv, Auth, Post, Temporal, Evidence): preconditions (what must already be true, e.g. IdentityConfirmed=True), invariants (what must never be violated, e.g. ProductionChange=>Approved, VoteCount<=MaximumAllowed, explicitly a domain constraint not merely evidence), authorization requirements, required postconditions, timing constraints, and assurance requirements. Preconditions and invariants are kept strictly separate: a precondition asks whether the world is ready for the operation; an invariant asks whether the operation is allowed to produce a state violating a protected property.

a_rows_sample.anchor: {Pre(d)} d {Post(d)}
a_rows_sample.statement: Borrows Hoare-logic style {P} d {Q} (if precondition P holds, execution of d should produce a state satisfying Q) and applies it as {Pre(d)} d {Post(d)}. Immediately argues ordinary Hoare logic is insufficient for KnowledgeOS because it additionally needs Evidence, Uncertainty, Authority, TemporalValidity and Provenance -- so the KnowledgeOS decision contract must extend the classical Hoare form.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Admissible = Pre and Invariant and Assurance and Authorization
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Admissible(d,K,t) iff Pre(d,K,t) and Invariant(d,K,t) and Assurance(d,K,t) and Authorization(d,K,t) -- a strict conjunction. Worked example: if Pre=True, Assurance=True, Authorization=True but Invariant=False, then Admissible=False regardless; 'there must be no averaging' across the conjuncts (i.e. no compensable weighted-sum scoring of admissibility conditions).

a_rows_sample.anchor: DC(d)=<P,I,A,E,Q,T,O>; Admissible as six-way conjunction
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates and extends the Decision Contract as DC(d) = <P,I,A,E,Q,T,O> where P=preconditions, I=invariants, A=authorization, E=evidence requirements, Q=epistemic sufficiency, T=temporal constraints, O=postconditions; and Admissible(d,K,t) iff P(K,t) and I(K,t) and A(K,t) and E(K,t) and Q(K,t) and T(K,t), with Execute(d) only then permitted.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Decision evaluation != decision execution; dry-run capability
a_rows_sample.statement: States that KnowledgeOS should conceptually perform Evaluate(d) before Execute(d), so Decision evaluation != Decision execution. The architecture should support Evaluate(d,K) without actually executing d, enabling simulation, review, what-if analysis, governance checks and AI planning; extends to a counterfactual decision WhatIf(Execute(d)) with estimated PostState(d), flagged as important for the later causal-reasoning formalization.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Safety gate pipeline: Plan->Evaluate->Validate->Authorize->Safety Gate->Execute->Observe Outcome
a_rows_sample.statement: For consequential operations, depicts a pipeline Plan -> Evaluate -> Validate -> Authorize -> Safety Gate -> Execute -> Observe Outcome, with the rule that the side effect must occur after the gate. Applies this to bound AI agents: an AI agent may propose d but should not automatically bypass Admissibility, so AIProposal -> DecisionEvaluation -> PolicyGate; states the architecture rule 'AI may propose; the governed system decides whether the proposal is admissible', and explicitly rejects Trust(AI)=True in favor of Capability(AI) constrained by Policy -- an AI agent's authority is explicitly bounded.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Twelve falsification experiments for Step 42 (all PASS)
a_rows_sample.statement: Runs twelve falsification tests against the Step 42 model, all recorded PASS: (1) epistemic requirements pass but authorization fails => Admissible=False; (2) authorization passes but a hard invariant fails => Block; (3) all conditions known except a safety-critical invariant => Block/Unknown per policy, never automatic authorization; (4) a valid transition from a valid state preserves the invariant; (5) a transition that would violate a domain invariant is rejected; (6) a required approval expires before execution => decision becomes inadmissible; (7) evidence used by a decision is revoked => dependency closure identifies affected assurance and decisions; (8) an AI proposes an action violating a governance rule => proposal may be recorded but execution is blocked; (9) new evidence disproves an earlier assumption => existing assurance can be downgraded/revoked; (10) a decision is evaluated without execution => dry-run result has no side effect; (11) an invariant belongs to bounded context BC_A => KnowledgeOS does not silently redefine it from BC_B; (12) a decision passes technical assurance but lacks governance authorization => TechnicallySupported=True, Authorized=False, therefore Execute=False.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 42 verdict and seven closing principles
a_rows_sample.statement: Declares STEP 42 -- PASS and restates seven principles as the step's headline results: (1) Sufficient Knowledge != Valid Decision; (2) Valid Decision != Authorized Action; (3) Unknown safety state must not silently become safe; (4) Hard invariants are non-negotiable; (5) AI proposal != authorized execution; (6) Every consequential decision should have an explicit contract; (7) Evidence invalidation must propagate through decision dependencies.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Second-order decision contract DC(d)=(Pre,Inv,Auth,Evidence,Post,Effects); horizon-dependent reachability safety; delayed effects
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends the Step 42 decision contract to DC(d) = (Pre, Inv, Auth, Evidence, Post, Effects), where Effects(A) = {E_1,...,E_n} covers both ExpectedEffect and PotentialSideEffects, so the system should evaluate not only the immediate postcondition but what important downstream states an action could create. Defines horizon-dependent reachability safety: an action A is safe only if Reach_H(S,A) intersect S_unsafe = empty for horizon H -- safety cannot usually be proven for t->infinity, so a finite horizon (e.g. 24h or 30 days) must be chosen, making Safety(d,H) horizon-specific (an action safe for H=1 day may be unsafe for H=2 years). Some actions have Lag(A,Y)>0 (e.g. ArchitectureChange -> MaintenanceCost manifesting months later); represents delayed causality as Y_{t+tau}=f(A_t,...) with delay tau as part of the causal model; warns that a controller reacting before a previous action's effects become visible (A_t -> S_{t+tau} -> Decision_{t+tau+1}) can overcorrect, producing oscillation (Increase->Decrease->Increase->Decrease) even when each local decision appears rational -- 'the problem lies in the dynamic system', so the decision engine should consider EffectDelay, not merely EffectExists.

b_rows_sample.statement: Extends the Step 42 decision contract to DC(d) = (Pre, Inv, Auth, Evidence, Post, Effects), where Effects(A) = {E_1,...,E_n} covers both ExpectedEffect and PotentialSideEffects, so the system should evaluate not only the immediate postcondition but what important downstream states an action could create. Defines horizon-dependent reachability safety: an action A is safe only if Reach_H(S,A) intersect S_unsafe = empty for horizon H -- safety cannot usually be proven for t->infinity, so a finite horizon (e.g. 24h or 30 days) must be chosen, making Safety(d,H) horizon-specific (an action safe for H=1 day may be unsafe for H=2 years). Some actions have Lag(A,Y)>0 (e.g. ArchitectureChange -> MaintenanceCost manifesting months later); represents delayed causality as Y_{t+tau}=f(A_t,...) with delay tau as part of the causal model; warns that a controller reacting before a previous action's effects become visible (A_t -> S_{t+tau} -> Decision_{t+tau+1}) can overcorrect, producing oscillation (Increase->Decrease->Increase->Decrease) even when each local decision appears rational -- 'the problem lies in the dynamic system', so the decision engine should consider EffectDelay, not merely EffectExists.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Twelve falsification experiments for Step 44 dynamic-causal model (all PASS)
b_rows_sample.statement: Runs twelve falsification tests, all PASS: (1) an action changes state and future available actions => future action space recomputed; (2) a feedback loop amplifies errors => potential instability detected; (3) a feedback loop dampens errors => stabilizing behavior recognized; (4) an action has a delayed effect => causal model preserves the delay; (5) a causal cascade contains multiple paths => direct/indirect effects remain distinguishable; (6) two failures share a common cause => not treated as independent failures; (7) an action is safe immediately but unsafe over a longer horizon => safety evaluation depends on horizon; (8) an action creates an unsafe reachable state => decision gate blocks it under the relevant safety policy; (9) an intervention produces an unexpected second-order effect => outcome recorded and causal model updated, original history unchanged; (10) a hidden state is inferred from observations => state estimate retains uncertainty; (11) two causal models produce different long-term predictions => model uncertainty remains explicit; (12) a delayed feedback controller repeatedly overreacts => oscillation/instability detected as a system-level phenomenon rather than attributed to isolated decisions.

a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the naive assumption that the best action is the one that maximally reduces discrepancy: actions carry cost, risk, reversibility, authority requirements, information value, and consequences.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The fundamental problem ... a^*=\arg\min_a Distance(K_{t+1},I). Why? Because some actions are dangerous; expensive; irreversible; unauthorized; unnecessary; poorly understood. action selection is a decision problem under uncertainty and constraints.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects a1*=argmin_a Distance(K_{t+1},I) as insufficient given actions can be dangerous/expensive/irreversible/unauthorized/unnecessary/poorly understood — action selection is a decision problem under uncertainty and constraints.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Action is not knowledge ... Knowledge\neq Action and Recommendation\neq Execution. "Changing the firewall rule is likely to solve the discrepancy." That does not mean "Change the firewall rule." There is a governance boundary between those two statements.
a_rows_sample.statement: States Knowledge ≠ Action and Recommendation ≠ Execution as a governance boundary between a diagnostic statement and a directive.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Define an Action ... a=(Intent,Preconditions,Effects,Cost,Risk,Reversibility,Authority,EvidenceRequirements,Context). An action is therefore a structured domain object.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Action as a structured domain object a=(Intent,Preconditions,Effects,Cost,Risk,Reversibility,Authority,EvidenceRequirements,Context).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Action Preconditions ... Migrate Nexus may require q_1=Backup verified, q_2=Rollback available, q_3=Dependencies identified. Preconditions(a) must be evaluated against K_t. If a critical precondition is unknown Executable(a)=False unless an explicit governance policy permits otherwise.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Preconditions(a) evaluated against K_t (worked with three migration preconditions), with Executable(a)=False by default when a critical precondition is unknown, absent explicit governance override.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Action effects ... Transition_a(X_t)\rightarrow X_{t+1} where X is the domain state. But we may not know the exact outcome. X_{t+1} may be probabilistic or uncertain.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines action effects as a (possibly probabilistic/uncertain) domain-state transition Transition_a(X_t)→X_{t+1}.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Expected outcome ... o_1,o_2,\ldots,o_m with probabilities P(o_i\mid a,K_t). EU(a) = \sum_i P(o_i\mid a,K_t)U(o_i) where U is the utility function. This is standard expected-utility reasoning.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines standard expected utility EU(a)=Σ_i P(o_i|a,K_t)U(o_i) over possible action outcomes.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Information has value ... inspect firewall logs. Its direct operational effect may be \Delta_{operational}=0. But it may greatly reduce uncertainty. Information itself has decision value.
a_rows_sample.statement: States Information itself has decision value, illustrated by an inspection action with zero direct operational effect but high uncertainty reduction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Value of Information ... EVSI(q) = \mathbb E_r[\max_a EU(a\mid K_{t+1}(r))] - \max_a EU(a\mid K_t) where EVSI is the Expected Value of Sample Information. This is a very useful formalization for Lord.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Expected Value of Sample Information EVSI(q)=E_r[max_a EU(a|K_{t+1}(r))]-max_a EU(a|K_t), a formal decision-theoretic value-of-information measure for Lord.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Simpler KnowledgeOS formulation ... VOI(q) = ExpectedDecisionImprovement(q) - Cost(q) as a policy-level approximation. q^* = \arg\max_q VOI(q). Subject to Risk(q)\leq RiskLimit.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a simpler policy-level VOI(q)=ExpectedDecisionImprovement(q)-Cost(q), with q*=argmax_q VOI(q) subject to a risk limit.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This changes the role of Lord ... Generate candidate actions and investigations that have high expected value for reducing relevant uncertainty, discrepancy, or decision risk. Lord: (K_t,I_t,\Delta_t) \rightarrow \mathcal A_t with each candidate annotated by ExpectedBenefit, Cost, Risk, VOI, Reversi
a_rows_sample.statement: Redefines Lord: (K_t,I_t,Δ_t)→A_t, with each candidate action annotated by ExpectedBenefit, Cost, Risk, VOI, and Reversibility.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sārathi is the decision function ... Sārathi: (K_t,I_t,\Delta_t,\mathcal A_t,\rho) \rightarrow Decision ... Decision\in\{Execute,Investigate,Defer,Reject,Escalate,RequestApproval\}. This is important.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines Sārathi:(K_t,I_t,Δ_t,A_t,ρ)→Decision, with Decision∈{Execute,Investigate,Defer,Reject,Escalate,RequestApproval}.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sārathi does not have unlimited authority ... production firewall change. Authority(a)=ArchitectureBoard. Therefore Sārathi should produce RequestApproval(a). Not Execute(a). Decision capability\neq Execution authority.
a_rows_sample.statement: States Decision capability ≠ Execution authority, illustrated by a production firewall change requiring Sārathi to produce RequestApproval rather than Execute even when it is the best-evaluated action.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Decision feasibility ... Feasible(a,K_t,\rho) = Preconditions \land Authority \land Constraints \land Safety. Only feasible actions enter the final decision set. \mathcal A^{feasible} \subseteq \mathcal A.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Feasible(a,K_t,ρ)=Preconditions∧Authority∧Constraints∧Safety, filtering the candidate set to A^feasible⊆A before decision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Constrained optimization ... a^* = \arg\max_{a\in\mathcal A^{feasible}} EU(a) subject to Risk(a)\leq R_{max} and Cost(a)\leq C_{max}. This is already a computationally well-defined problem when the relevant quantities are available.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes constrained action optimization a*=argmax_{a∈A^feasible} EU(a) subject to Risk(a)≤R_max and Cost(a)≤C_max.

a_rows_sample.anchor: But utility is not universal ... There is no universal U(a). For one organization Cost may dominate. For another Safety may dominate. For an incident TimeToRecovery may dominate. UtilityFunction is policy/purpose dependent.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues there is no universal utility function U(a); it is policy/purpose dependent (cost-dominant vs safety-dominant vs recovery-time-dominant organizations).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Multi-objective decision making ... Objectives=\{Cost,Risk,Time,Quality,Compliance,Security,Availability\}. There may be no single naturally correct ordering. \mathbf U(a)=(u_1(a),\ldots,u_n(a)). U_\rho(a) = F_\rho(\mathbf U(a)).
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a multi-objective utility vector U(a)=(u1(a),...,un(a)) over seven named objectives (Cost/Risk/Time/Quality/Compliance/Security/Availability), aggregated by a policy-specific function F_ρ.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Pareto optimality ... Action a_1 dominates a_2 if u_i(a_1)\geq u_i(a_2) for every criterion i, and strictly better for at least one. The Pareto frontier is \mathcal P = \{a\mid \nexists b:b\succ a\}. Sārathi can present the Pareto-optimal choices to the human decision-maker. This is often better tha
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Pareto dominance and the Pareto frontier P={a|∄b:b≻a}, recommending Sārathi present the Pareto set to a human decision-maker rather than pretend to know exact utility weights.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Example ... Inspect logs Low Very Low High Yes ... Change firewall Medium High Low Partly ... Do nothing Zero High None Yes. A naive optimizer might choose DoNothing because Cost=0. A purely discrepancy-driven system might choose ChangeFirewall. A proper decision system may choose InspectLogs becaus
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked five-action decision table (inspect logs/ask owner/run test/change firewall/do nothing) showing a naive cost-minimizer picks DoNothing and a naive discrepancy-minimizer picks ChangeFirewall, while the intended system correctly picks InspectLogs for its high information value at low risk.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Exploration versus exploitation ... Exploration Acquire information a_{explore} ... Exploitation Act on current knowledge a_{exploit} ... Sārathi must balance InformationGain vs ImmediateBenefit. This is closely related to sequential decision theory.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces the exploration (acquire information) vs exploitation (act on current knowledge) tradeoff Sārathi must balance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Lord = selects the next useful action ... Sarathi = determines what decision should be made
b_rows_sample.statement: Opens by distinguishing Lord ('selects the next useful action,' e.g. 'perform a restore test') from Sarathi ('determines what decision should be made,' e.g. migrate/postpone/change plan/stop given resulting knowledge).

b_rows_sample.anchor: D=\{Migrate,Postpone,ChangePlan,Reject\} ... Decision\neq Action
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the decision set D (e.g. {Migrate, Postpone, ChangePlan, Reject}) as distinct from the executable action set A (e.g. a single decision d=Migrate may require several actions {Backup, RestoreTest, FirewallValidation, Approval, Migration}) — Decision ≠ Action.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Lord: (K,Z,G,C)\rightarrow A ... Sarathi: (K,G,D,C,P)\rightarrow d
b_rows_sample.statement: States the precise operator distinction: Lord: (K,Z,G,C)->A (chooses what to do next to advance the process); Sarathi: (K,G,D,C,P)->d (chooses which decision is justified given current knowledge and decision model P).

type_signature.domain: KnowledgeState x Goal x DecisionSet x Constraints x Policy

b_rows_sample.anchor: Consequences(d_1) ... OutcomeModel(d,K)
b_rows_sample.statement: Decision reasoning requires knowing Consequences(d) (e.g. for d1=Migrate: Success, Failure, DataLoss, Downtime, Rollback), formalized as requiring an OutcomeModel(d,K).

b_rows_sample.anchor: U(Success)=+100, U(Failure)=-50, U(DataLoss)=-1000 ... illustrative only ... must never be invented by the AI and presented as organizational truth
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a utility function U(o) over outcomes with illustrative example values, explicitly warning these numbers 'must never be invented by the AI and presented as organizational truth.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: EU(d\mid K)=\sum_o P(o\mid d,K)U(o) ... d^*=\arg\max_d EU(d\mid K) subject to governance and safety constraints
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines expected utility EU(d|K)=sum_o P(o|d,K)U(o) and d*=argmax_d EU(d|K), explicitly subject to governance and safety constraints — 'a mathematically well-defined decision mechanism.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: P(o\mid d,K) cannot reasonably be established. We must not invent it ... Preference(d_1,d_2) or Dominates(d_1,d_2)
b_rows_sample.statement: When probability cannot reasonably be established, prohibits inventing it and instead allows qualitative Preference(d1,d2) or Dominates(d1,d2) (e.g. 'if migration is unauthorized, postponement dominates migration' — no probability necessary).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Feasible(d,K,C) ... Migrate requires RollbackVerified=True ... Feasible(Migrate)=False ... should not matter how attractive migration appears economically
b_rows_sample.statement: Before utility calculation, Sarathi must determine Feasible(d,K,C); e.g. Migrate requiring RollbackVerified=True is Feasible=False when RollbackVerified=Unknown, regardless of economic attractiveness.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Hard constraint C(d)=True ... Preference d_1\succ d_2 ... Constraints filter; Utility/preferences select
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes hard constraints (must hold, e.g. ProductionChangeAuthorized) from preferences among permissible decisions (e.g. prefer lower expected downtime): 'Constraints filter; Utility/preferences select.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: EU(Migrate)=95 ... EU(Postpone)=60 ... Authorized(Migrate)=False ... Migrate is eliminated before utility optimization ... Utility cannot override governance
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example showing higher expected utility (Migrate=95 vs Postpone=60) does not matter once Authorized(Migrate)=False eliminates it before optimization — 'Utility cannot override governance.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: DecisionModel=(Outcomes,Constraints,Preferences,Utilities,Uncertainty,Policy) ... Sarathi(K,D,DecisionModel)\rightarrow DecisionResult
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a six-component DecisionModel=(Outcomes, Constraints, Preferences, Utilities, Uncertainty, Policy) and Sarathi(K,D,DecisionModel)->DecisionResult.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Decision: POSTPONE ... Reason: rollback capability not established ... Blocking requirements: RollbackVerified ... Evidence basis: E17,E22,E31 ... Now the decision is auditable
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked full auditable DecisionResult record for a POSTPONE decision containing reason, blocking requirements, alternative feasibility, evidence basis, decision model version, and authorization status — contrasted with returning a bare 'MIGRATE' label.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DecisionProvenance(d) ... K_t+Contract+Policy+Model+Evidence\rightarrow d ... Decision must be reproducible
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires DecisionProvenance(d) tracing K_t+Contract+Policy+Model+Evidence -> d, so 'Decision must be reproducible.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Decision_t remains associated with K_t ... Decision_{t+1} is calculated from K_{t+1} ... Decision is time-indexed
b_rows_sample.statement: A historical decision (e.g. today's Postpone) must not be rewritten when tomorrow's new evidence would produce Migrate; Decision_t stays tied to K_t, and Decision_{t+1} is separately computed from K_{t+1} — 'Decision is time-indexed.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Stability(d,K) as sensitivity to plausible changes in the knowledge state
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines decision Stability(d,K) conceptually as sensitivity to plausible changes in the knowledge state, motivated by the concern that small evidence changes flipping Migrate<->Postpone indicate an unstable decision.

b_rows_sample.anchor: P(Success)=0.91 ... threshold 0.90 ... Migrate ... if a small uncertainty could make P(Success)=0.88 ... DecisionFragility=High
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example: a decision that barely clears its threshold (P(Success)=0.91 vs threshold 0.90) but could plausibly drop to 0.88 under small uncertainty should be reported as DecisionFragility=High rather than simply 'Migrate.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: P(Success)\ge\theta ... \theta must come from governance/domain policy. The AI cannot invent it
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes threshold decisions P(Success)>=theta (e.g. theta=0.95: P=0.97=>Migrate, P=0.72=>Postpone), explicitly requiring theta to come from governance/domain policy — 'the AI cannot invent it.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Probability=Unknown ... We should not substitute P=0.5 ... Unknown+CriticalRisk\rightarrow Postpone
b_rows_sample.statement: When P(Success) cannot be estimated, prohibits substituting an arbitrary P=0.5 as 'unjustified'; instead records Probability=Unknown and lets the decision policy handle uncertainty (e.g. Unknown+CriticalRisk -> Postpone).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Absence of evidence \neq evidence of failure ... Required evidence absent \Rightarrow decision may be blocked
b_rows_sample.statement: States a named KnowledgeOS principle: Absence of evidence ≠ evidence of failure, distinct from Required evidence absent => decision may be blocked — 'these are different.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Risk(d)=P(Loss\mid d,K)\times Impact(Loss) ... only appropriate where the probabilistic model is justified
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Risk (consequences under uncertainty) from Uncertainty (what we do not know), giving a common quantitative formalization Risk(d)=P(Loss|d,K) x Impact(Loss), qualified as appropriate only where the probabilistic model is justified.

a_notations: Sarathi: Lord's selected action -> actual behavior
a_aliases: Step 15: Decision Theory, Value of Information, Action Selection, and Sārathi

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'formal-sarathi-decision-algebra' POSSIBLY relates to 'decision-theory-action-selection-sarathi' (batch B0022). Note: S0900's Step 25H: the first fully formal, falsification-tested treatment of Sarathi specifically as a governed decision operator distinct from Lord, contrasted in an explicit Lord-vs-Sarathi comparison table; extends B0021's broader decision-theory-action-selection-sarathi (S0871/Step 15) object.

explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'decision-theory-action-selection-sarathi' POSSIBLY relates to 'formal-sarathi-decision-algebra' (batch B0022). Note: Recurring label across S0898/S0899 for the Lord (action-selection) / Sarathi (action-execution/conversion of selected action into actual behavior) architecture and its end-to-end diagram; closely related to, and possibly identical with, the already-registered formal-lord-action-selection-algebra and formal-sarathi-decision-algebra labels. Added here to satisfy the batch's own label-registration requirement; a future merge review should determine whether this collapses into those two existing objects.
labels share the alias 'Formal Sarathi Algebra'

a_rows_sample.anchor: PHASE 1 CORPUS DISCOVERY ... STOP adding theory. ... PHASE 2 GLOBAL RECONSTRUCTION ... PHASE 3 CONVERGENCE ... PHASE 4 KnowledgeOS Kernel. ... If we keep injecting our current hypotheses during the corpus pass, we risk confirmation bias.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues for completing the corpus reading pass (Phase 1) before Phase 2 (per-lineage reconstruction of Engineering/EKS-PKS, Gita/Vedanta, and Mathematical lines), Phase 3 (convergence analysis), and Phase 4 (kernel synthesis), explicitly to avoid confirmation bias from injecting current hypotheses mid-pass; specifies two invariants to monitor throughout (Evidence!=Interpretation!=Hypothesis!=CanonicalModel; no merging merely because concepts look similar) and a required deliverable set (corpus statistics, classification ledger, model-candidate registries, unresolved-equivalence/gap registers) before any final synthesis attempt.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DEFINED != CANONICALLY CONSOLIDATED. That is the key distinction. ... The real problem isn't lack of concepts. It is composition and canonicalization.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the entire research problem: rather than many concepts being missing, most of the needed conceptual stack (Knowledge Space Omega, K_t subset-of Omega, a Sigma_t dimension layer, an operator chain, six protected kernel dimensions, an operator-discovery contract) already has candidate definitions scattered across the corpus at different times and epistemic-status levels -- the actual unsolved problem is composing and canonicalizing already-scattered definitions, not discovering new ones.

a_rows_sample.anchor: For every major concept: | Concept | First definition | Later definitions | Conflicts | Final canonical definition |. ... establish the lineage D1->D2->D3->...->Dn and determine whether each transition is: refinement | extension | correction | replacement | contradiction.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a definition-reconciliation methodology as the correct next step (rather than further discovery): for every major concept (Knowledge, K_t, Dimension, Value, Operator, Invariant, Evidence, Purification, Moksha) trace its definition lineage across the corpus and classify each transition as refinement, extension, correction, replacement, or contradiction, producing a canonical definition graph.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sigma_t != K_t and a change in Sigma_t != a KnowledgeOS state transition. This is explicitly identified as the major conceptual correction.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports a later, more rigorous corpus generation's major correction: Sigma_t (the measurable epistemic-dimension layer) is not identical to K_t, and a change in Sigma_t does not automatically constitute a KnowledgeOS state transition -- correcting an earlier tendency to treat Sigma_t and K_t interchangeably.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t --pi--> X_t --mu--> (Omega,F,P) ... whether the knowledge element is: an outcome, a random variable, an event, a measurable function, a probability distribution, which is exactly the unresolved question.
a_rows_sample.statement: Refines the earlier candidate axiom K_t subset-of (Omega,F,P) into a two-stage construction K_t -pi-> X_t -mu-> (Omega,F,P), where pi is a semantic/measurement representation and mu a separately mathematically-justified construction, leaving open exactly which probabilistic object type a knowledge element should be (outcome/random-variable/event/measurable-function/distribution).

a_rows_sample.anchor: A. Knowledge-state operations O_K: K->K' ... B. Epistemic-analysis operations O_E: (K,X)->Y ... C. World/action operations O_W: (K,D)->W'. This three-way separation is something I strongly recommend we preserve.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports a three-class operation taxonomy recommended for preservation: knowledge-state operations O_K:K->K' (Create/Revise/Retract/Supersede/Merge/Split/Qualify); epistemic-analysis operations O_E:(K,X)->Y that need not modify K (Compare/Classify/DetectContradiction/EvaluateEvidence/DetermineIdentity/CheckConsistency); and world/action operations O_W:(K,D)->W' that cross the KnowledgeOS/world boundary (Authorize/Execute/Notify/Publish/Apply).

a_rows_sample.anchor: operation identity != operation semantics != operation execution. ... o=(name,input,pre,post,effect,authority,policy,provenance) and then [[o]](K)=K' or [[o]](K,I)=(K',E).
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports a semantic operation contract o=(name,input,pre,post,effect,authority,policy,provenance) with an explicit denotational-semantics function [[o]](K)=K' (or [[o]](K,I)=(K',E)), separating operation identity, operation semantics, and operation execution as three non-collapsing concerns -- called a major foundation for eventually defining the KnowledgeOS kernel computationally.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Purification = research hypothesis, because neither the component ordering of Sigma nor the relationship between Sigma-order and K-order has been established.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports the corpus's own conservative downgrading of Buddhi, Guna, and especially Purification (P:Sigma_t->Sigma_{t+1}) from candidate canonical kernel operators to research hypotheses, since neither Sigma's internal component ordering nor the relationship between Sigma-ordering and K-ordering has been established -- consistent with this batch's other findings that Sigma-order != K-order.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EpistemicState = Acquisition x Support x Resolution x Validity ... 'dimensions of knowledge' may actually need to be understood as a typed family of state coordinates, rather than merely a vector of numerical values.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports a pre-existing four-axis epistemic-state factorization (Acquisition x Support x Resolution x Validity, with axis values like Observed/Reported/Inferred/Calculated) as a candidate bridge suggesting knowledge dimensions should be modelled as a typed family of state coordinates rather than a plain numeric vector, chaining DDD Knowledge State -> epistemic dimensions -> measure-theoretic representation -> infinite-dimensional mathematical space as a stronger direction than directly declaring K_t a probability space.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Can the existing definitions be composed into one coherent mathematical KnowledgeOS Kernel? rather than 'What concepts are still missing?'
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the file's central reframed research question as whether the corpus's already-scattered candidate definitions (Omega, F, K_t, Sigma_t, O, I, B, G, H) can be composed into one coherent mathematical kernel under an operator O that simultaneously respects state, dimension, measure/probability, topological, and invariant structure -- rather than continuing to search for missing concepts.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero != Lord != Sarathi != Transition ... K_t -Zero-> Z_t -Lord-> L_t -Sarathi-> a_t -Commit-> e_t -delta-> K_{t+1} ... Zero, Lord, and Sarathi do not change K
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the initial Zero/Lord/Sarathi/Commit/Transition pipeline as a linear sequence culminating in a state change, with explicit invariants that Zero, Lord and Sarathi are each analytical (never transformational) and none of their outputs alone entail K_{t+1}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sarathi should not 'recommend Commit'... Commitment is not an epistemic action. It is an authorization/governance action... a_t -Authorize-> c_t -Execute-> e_t. Guidance != Authorization != Execution != Transition.
b_rows_sample.statement: Removes 'Commit' from Sarathi's action vocabulary and inserts an explicit Authorization boundary between recommendation and execution: Sarathi produces a recommendation a_t, Authorize(Knower,a_t,Policy) produces a command c_t, Execute(c_t) produces an event e_t, and only then does delta(K_t,e_t) fire -- Guidance != Authorization != Execution != Transition, with the missing Authorize function explicitly making the Knower's authority mathematically visible.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Execute: C -> E is too deterministic. Execution can fail... Execute(c_t) -> ExecutionResult in {Success(e),Failure(f),Partial(e,f)} ... ExecutionResult != DomainEvent.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects Execute from a total deterministic function C->E to one returning a structured ExecutionResult (Success/Failure/Partial), and similarly Authorize to return an AuthorizationResult (Authorized/Rejected/Deferred/Modified) rather than assuming every recommendation becomes a command; ExecutionResult is explicitly distinguished from the DomainEvent that actually triggers a transition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the epistemic cycle is actually not always a cycle... External observation -> Event -> Transition can update the state directly... Guidance is optional; Transition is fundamental. G5 - Guidance is not a prerequisite for transition.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the closing theorem G5: Guidance (Zero/Lord/Sarathi) is not a prerequisite for every Knowledge-State transition -- a raw external observation event or a scheduled validity check can trigger delta(K_t,e_t) directly, so the lenses must never be modelled as mandatory middleware sitting between every event and the transition function; renames the pipeline from 'Epistemic Cycle' to 'Epistemic Guidance-and-Transition Cycle' to reflect this.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I strongly recommend introducing: I-hat_t = Candidate Ideal State and I_t = Approved Ideal State ... KnowledgeOS -> I-hat_{t+1} (proposal); Authorize(I-hat_{t+1}) -> I_{t+1}.
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a Candidate Ideal State (I-hat) vs Approved Ideal State (I) split mirroring the Q17 recommendation/authorization boundary: KnowledgeOS may only ever produce a candidate revision proposal, and only an explicit Authorize step (by the Knower/governance authority under applicable norms) produces the actually approved I_{t+1}; KnowledgeOS != I_{t+1} but KnowledgeOS -> I-hat_{t+1}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sārathi \rightarrow DecisionPosture
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects Sarathi's output from a binary Stop/Continue decision to a richer DecisionPosture ∈ {Proceed, Investigate, ProceedWithCaveats, Defer, Escalate, UnableToDecide}, argued to be closer to Sarathi's actual role.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Recommendation \neq Assertion
b_rows_sample.statement: Strict boundary: Recommendation ≠ Assertion, Recommendation ≠ Fact, Recommendation ≠ Decision. Sārathi may say 'Investigate the moral obligation dimension' but KnowledgeOS must not silently convert that into 'Therefore Arjuna should fight' — the Knower remains the decision authority unless the domain explicitly delegates that authority. Marked as extremely important for the DDD model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate \neq Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Lord needs a stronger boundary too: Candidate ≠ Knowledge, Candidate ≠ Evidence, Candidate ≠ Assertion. A presentation should visually distinguish KNOWN / INFERRED / UNKNOWN / CANDIDATE / RECOMMENDED to prevent semantic contamination.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero(S_t) \rightarrow EpistemicFindings
b_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms Zero's role as boundary-finder, not belief-decider: Zero(S_t) -> EpistemicFindings, Presentation ⊇ DecisionRelevant(EpistemicFindings); 'Zero does not decide what the Knower should believe. Zero says: Here is where the state has a boundary.' Also strengthens provenance: EveryDecisionRelevantClaim -> Provenance, with a worked claim-level provenance record example (Acquisition/Evidence/Observed-at/Validity/Conflict/Source).

b_rows_sample.anchor:
Unknown 
eq Absent 
eq NotApplicable 
eq NotObserved 
eq NotYetInvestigated
b_rows_sample.statement: Elevates 'unknown' to a fundamental principle already implicit in Zero: Unknown ≠ Absent ≠ NotApplicable ≠ NotObserved ≠ NotYetInvestigated, illustrated by Version=UNKNOWN not meaning Version=ABSENT, and SecurityStatus=NOT_ASSESSED not meaning SecurityStatus=SAFE.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero \neq UniversalValidator
b_rows_sample.statement: DDD warning that Zero risks becoming a 'god object' by owning detection of gaps, conflicts, type problems, temporal problems and epistemic boundaries all at once: Zero ≠ UniversalValidator. Zero is redefined narrowly as detecting epistemic boundaries/deficiencies relevant to current state and purpose, aggregating epistemic consequences of findings from separate domain validators (schema, type, policy, security violations).

b_rows_sample.anchor: LordCandidate \neq Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: LordCandidate ≠ Knowledge and LordCandidate ≠ Evidence: Lord can propose 'there may be a moral-obligation dimension' but it becomes knowledge only after investigation; critical to prevent AI-generated hypotheses entering the Knowledge State as facts.

b_rows_sample.anchor: S\bar{a}rathiRecommendation \neq Decision
b_rows_sample.statement: Sārathi needs a constitutional policy boundary: SārathiRecommendation ≠ Decision, SārathiAction ≠ HumanAuthorization — Sārathi may determine the next best investigation, but the Knower decides whether to accept it unless the system has explicitly delegated authority.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sārathi: (K,U,N,\Delta,P,Role) \rightarrow Guidance
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects Sārathi(K,I,Δ)->Action as too simplistic: Sārathi:(K,U,N,Δ,P,Role) -> Guidance, which may then produce Decision, which may then authorize Action, giving Guidance ≠ Decision ≠ Action (confirming an earlier DDD warning). Also reframes Zero/Lord/Sārathi as three functions/lenses over the state rather than three sequential stages: Zero=Diagnose, Lord=Reason/Synthesize/Orient, Sārathi=Guide, with Decision->Action occurring outside those lenses; explicitly an architectural abstraction, not a literal theological equivalence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sārathi: (State, Norms, Role, Context, Discrepancies) \rightarrow Guidance
b_rows_sample.statement: Revises Sārathi(K,I,Δ)->Action (too direct) to Sārathi:(State,Norms,Role,Context,Discrepancies)->Guidance -> CandidateActions -> Decision -> Action, giving proper separation of concerns. Reaffirms Zero as a pure DiagnosticFunction that must not itself decide ('therefore do X'). Corrects Lord from 'merely a reasoning engine/LLM reasoning' to AuthoritativeKnowledge+NormativeOrientation+InterpretiveResolution, since Krishna in the text functions as an authoritative source of teaching, not just an inference engine — called crucial for KnowledgeOS governance. Confirms Sārathi = ContextualGuidance, distinguishing Lord ('what is authoritative/true/normative') from Sārathi ('how does that apply here') from Decision ('what will I choose') from Action ('what will I actually do').

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero(K,I,C,P) \rightarrow \text{Epistemic Boundaries}
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes Zero/Lord/Sārathi as product capabilities rather than domain entities: Zero(K,I,C,P)->Epistemic Boundaries acts as an 'epistemic diagnostic engine' (missing dimensions, unknown values, missing/weak/conflicting evidence, logical contradictions, stale knowledge, contextual mismatches, unresolved questions, unsupported assumptions, Ideal-State discrepancies); Lord asks 'what else might matter?' enabling 'horizon expansion' beyond gap-checking; Sārathi:(K,I,Z,L,Q,C)->NextAction performs 'epistemic navigation', worked through a Bhīṣma-relationship example (Zero flags unknown relationship, Lord flags kinship as material, Sārathi recommends investigating it before evaluating the decision).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Can we migrate this Nexus installation?
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example: asked 'Can we migrate this Nexus installation?', a conventional AI answers directly, while KnowledgeOS first constructs required dimensions (version, repository inventory, blob stores, storage, network, DNS, firewall, certificates, backup, dependencies, authentication, operational constraints), runs Zero to find missing items (backup verification, firewall confirmation, certificate ownership, dependency inventory), and has Sārathi respond 'Do not decide migration readiness yet. Investigate these four items.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: perform justified action given epistemic state
b_rows_sample.statement: Contrasts a conventional agent optimizing 'complete task' against KnowledgeOS optimizing 'perform justified action given epistemic state', worked through a deploy-approval example: required knowledge checklist (code reviewed✓, tests passed✓, architecture approved✓, security assessment✗, production configuration✗, rollback strategy✗) yields Zero='3 critical gaps' and Sārathi='DO NOT DEPLOY. Investigate security, configuration and rollback.' Also frames the agent loop as Understand Intent->Construct Knowledge State->Discover Dimensions->Zero->Identify Gaps/Conflicts->Lord->Expand Possible Investigation->Sārathi->Select Next Epistemic Action->Agent/Tool->Observation->Update Knowledge State->Repeat, called 'an epistemically governed autonomous agent architecture'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Retrieve(Q,K_t,I_t,C) \rightarrow EvidenceCandidates
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects plain Retrieve(Query)->Documents to a goal-directed Retrieve(Q,K_t,I_t,C)->EvidenceCandidates: the retrieval system 'knows why it is retrieving', discovering relevant dimensions (e.g. version, repository topology, blob stores, firewall, certificates for a migration decision) before retrieving. Zero can drive retrieval: given a partially-filled knowledge-state checklist, Zero reports specific gaps (backup verification, firewall rules, certificate ownership) and Sārathi generates a concrete investigation plan (search infrastructure docs for backup configuration, etc.), giving Zero -> Gap -> Sārathi -> Retrieval as part of the investigation loop, not a one-shot lookup.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'defined-not-canonically-consolidated-reconciliation-programme' POSSIBLY relates to 'zero-lord-sarathi-guidance-cycle' (batch B0056). Note: A four-phase corpus-reading discipline (Phase 1 Corpus Discovery: read sequentially, classify, record evidence, STOP adding theory; Phase 2 Global Reconstruction of three lineages -- Engineering/EKS-PKS, Gita/Vedanta, Mathematical; Phase 3 Convergence: common/different structures, contradictions, unresolved equivalences, missing bridges; Phase 4 KnowledgeOS Kernel only after the prior three) argued as the correct sequencing to avoid confirmation bias, with an explicit two-invariant monitoring rule (Evidence != Interpretation != Hypothesis != Canonical model; no merging merely because two concepts look similar) and a required deliverable set (corpus statistics, classification ledger, model-candidate registries, unresolved-equivalence/gap registers) before any final synthesis is attempted. On review of retrieved prior corpus material, reframes the standing problem via the key distinction DEFINED != CANONICALLY CONSOLIDATED: the corpus already contains many candidate definitions for nearly the full conceptual stack (Knowledge Space Omega with sigma-algebra F; K_t subset-of Omega; a temporal operator T:Omega->Omega; a Sigma_t measurable-epistemic-dimension layer explicitly allowed to have Sigma_t != Sigma_{t+1}; a Zero/Lord/Sarathi/Application operator chain; an operator-discovery contract requiring Input->Preconditions->Transformation->Output->Evidence->Provenance->Invariants with closure/determinism/idempotence/compositionality/reversibility/monotonicity tests; six protected kernel dimensions plus a Structural-Enforcement mechanism; a candidate complete kernel script-K=(script-K,K_t,Sigma_t,O,I,B,G,H) with B=Buddhi and G=Guna as an operating-mode hypothesis; and the Gita-term->philosophical-interpretation->KnowledgeOS-construct three-level translation discipline) -- so the real problem is not missing concepts but composition/canonicalization of already-scattered definitions with different epistemic status. Proposes a definition-reconciliation methodology: for every major concept, trace its definition lineage D1->D2->...->Dn and classify each transition as refinement, extension, correction, replacement, or contradiction, producing a canonical definition graph, rather than accepting whichever document is most recent. Reports a LATER, more rigorous corpus generation correcting the earlier candidate kernel into a layered research structure script-K_research=(K_t,R,I,E,O,T,G,H) (state/relations/invariants/equality-system/operations/transformation-semantics/governance/history) with equality/operations/transformation-semantics/implementation-contract explicitly still OPEN, and explicitly separates the ratified state K_t from a derived measurement/projection Sigma_t=mu(K_t,...) (Sigma_t != K_t; a change in Sigma_t != a KnowledgeOS state transition), refining the earlier proposal that K_t IS a probability space into a two-stage construction K_t --pi--> X_t --mu--> (Omega,F,P) where pi is a semantic/measurement representation and mu a separately-justified mathematical construction, raising the unresolved typing question of whether a knowledge element is an outcome/random-variable/event/measurable-function/distribution. Reports a three-way operation-class separation preserved as strongly recommended: O_K: K->K' (knowledge-state operations: Create/Revise/Retract/Supersede/Merge/Split/Qualify), O_E: (K,X)->Y (epistemic-analysis operations that need not modify K: Compare/Classify/DetectContradiction/EvaluateEvidence/DetermineIdentity/CheckConsistency), and O_W: (K,D)->W' (world/action operations crossing the KnowledgeOS/world boundary: Authorize/Execute/Notify/Publish/Apply) -- together with a semantic operation contract o=(name,input,pre,post,effect,authority,policy,provenance) and the non-collapse operation identity != operation semantics != operation execution. Treats Buddhi, Guna, and Purification as conservatively downgraded to research hypotheses rather than canonical kernel components (Purification P:Sigma_t->Sigma_{t+1} explicitly NOT canonical because neither Sigma's component ordering nor the Sigma-order-vs-K-order relationship is established). Reports a pre-existing four-axis EpistemicState=Acquisition x Support x Resolution x Validity factorization (Observed/Reported/Inferred/Calculated axis values) as a candidate bridge suggesting 'dimensions of knowledge' should be understood as a typed family of state coordinates rather than a plain numeric vector, chaining DDD-Knowledge-State -> epistemic-dimensions -> measure-theoretic-representation -> infinite-dimensional mathematical space as a stronger direction than directly declaring K_t a probability space.

b_rows_sample.anchor: MISSION: SAT-END-TO-END-CLOSURE-TEST-v1
b_rows_sample.statement: Full commissioning mission text for SAT-END-TO-END-CLOSURE-TEST-v1: test whether Sat(K,r,Gamma)=Det_r(EvalReq(K,r,EC,Gamma),EC) can be executed for ONE concrete corpus-grounded requirement, treating the boxed baseline definitions as given and explicitly forbidding reopening the historical Sat-existence question or another corpus-wide Sat survey. A strict non-design rule list bans inventing EvalReq/Det_r semantics, introducing Accept_r, assuming Sigma=(A,S,R,V,C) or V7, inventing component projections/thresholds/semantic adapters, silently completing missing arguments, or replacing an undefined operation with an intuitive implementation. Task: select one requirement r and its K/EC/Gamma only where corpus-grounded, execute the existing Eval/EvalReq/Det_r chain, record every intermediate value and its source citation, and stop at the first point requiring uninvented semantics. Output is a full execution trace with each step classified DERIVED/RECONSTRUCTABLE/ASSUMED/HYPOTHESIS/NOT ESTABLISHED/RESEARCH REQUIRED, and a final verdict of exactly one of COMPUTED/PARTIALLY COMPUTED/BLOCKED (with the first missing semantic dependency identified if BLOCKED, without repairing it).

a_rows_sample.anchor: The method illustrated in Swar Gyan is not actually dhatu extraction in the classical Sanskrit grammatical sense. It is primarily orthographic decomposition / compositional extraction. ... exactly the kind of pre-processing layer we could use before applying statistical or machine-learning methods.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit source-fidelity correction: Swar Gyan teaches orthographic decomposition (character/matra/conjunct construction) as a deterministic pre-processing layer, not dhatu extraction itself, which additionally requires morphology, lexical knowledge, grammar, derivational history, semantic compatibility and contextual disambiguation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: W = A1 A2 ... An where each Ai is an akshara unit, itself decomposable into consonant + vowel + matra + virama/halant + conjunct structure. This gives us a deterministic feature extractor.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a word as a sequence of akshara units each decomposed into consonant/vowel/matra/virama/conjunct structure, giving a deterministic feature extractor to feed downstream statistical models.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P(D | W,C) proportional to P(W | D,C) P(D | C) ... Instead of Root = root-gam, we can have: root-gam 0.91, root-gai 0.05, other 0.04. That is much more appropriate for KnowledgeOS.
a_rows_sample.statement: Bayesian dhatu-inference model P(Dhatu|Word,Context) yielding a probability distribution over candidate roots rather than a single deterministic answer, described as more epistemically appropriate for KnowledgeOS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A Conditional Random Field (CRF) would be a very natural classical statistical approach. ... gachchhati -> [gachchh][ti] -> [gachchh] root/stem candidate, [ti] verbal ending.
a_rows_sample.statement: CRF/HMM sequence-labeling proposed for morphological segmentation (character sequence -> ROOT/TRANSFORM/SUFFIX labels), worked through a concrete example segmenting a Sanskrit verb form.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Can we discover families of words without telling the algorithm their roots? ... clustering should produce candidates, not authoritative roots.
a_rows_sample.statement: Unsupervised clustering of morphologically-related word forms (gachchhati/agachchhat/gamishyati/gatah/gamanam) proposed to discover latent root families, explicitly bounded as producing candidates only, never authoritative roots.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Model A: surface word -> dhatu ... Model D: akshara + morphology + context + semantic features -> dhatu. Then measure: accuracy, top-1/top-5 accuracy, precision, recall, F1, calibration, uncertainty, error by morphological class. This would tell us whether the Swar Gyan/Paninian decomposition actually contributes predictive information.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formal four-model ablation experiment isolating whether akshara decomposition, phonology/morphology, and context/semantics each contribute measurable predictive value for dhatu recovery, with a full evaluation-metric list.

a_rows_sample.anchor: statistical model -> CANDIDATE -> NOT AUTHORITY. The ML model should propose. The deterministic linguistic/knowledge system should validate. ... Probabilistic inference should not silently become authoritative knowledge.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the batch's recurring propose-vs-validate boundary in this linguistic context: statistical models propose candidate dhatus; a deterministic linguistic/knowledge system validates them, never the reverse.

a_rows_sample.anchor: What structural features remain invariant across the transformation family? ... The dhatu becomes a latent structural center, rather than merely a dictionary lookup.
a_rows_sample.statement: Topological reframing: a dhatu (e.g. root kri, generating karoti/krita/karana/karya) is modeled as a latent structural center of a graph of surface-form transformations, analyzable via graph clustering/community detection/embeddings/centrality/manifold analysis rather than treated as a static dictionary lookup.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Give the algorithm only: Unicode characters + character positions + word boundaries + document/page boundaries. Then ask: Can the structure of the language be rediscovered statistically? ... Does the independently discovered statistical structure correspond to traditional dhatu structure?
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a deliberately label-blind experiment: give the algorithm only raw characters/positions/boundaries, let it discover latent word families statistically (frequency/co-occurrence/transition matrices -> clustering -> latent units), then compare the independently discovered structure against traditional dhatu theory as a hypothesis test, rather than assuming dhatu labels from the start.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Now we have three powerful operations. Dhatu / linguistic lens: What is the structural meaning expressed by the language? Critical-thinking lens: What claims, evidence, assumptions and inferences are actually justified? Zero lens: What remains after removing language, rhetoric, terminology and representation? So: Text -> SemanticStructure -> EpistemicStructure -> InvariantStructure. That is starting to look like an actual Knowledge Extraction Engine.
a_rows_sample.statement: Combines three research lenses into a single pipeline: the Dhatu/linguistic lens (structural meaning expressed by language), the critical-thinking lens (which claims/evidence/assumptions/inferences are actually justified), and the Zero lens (what remains after removing language/rhetoric/terminology/representation), yielding Text -> SemanticStructure -> EpistemicStructure -> InvariantStructure, described as an actual 'Knowledge Extraction Engine'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: yogartha / yogarudhartha / rudhartha = intrinsic / contextual / conventional meaning; word frequency != meaning
b_rows_sample.statement: The three-layer semantic model, named the strongest contribution of the Sanskrit-grammar lens: an anti-collapse lesson directly targeting LLM word-frequency-as-meaning failures.

b_rows_sample.anchor: semantic sandhi: context compatibility rules, meaning alignment rules, conflict resolution rules (A+B transform by rules at the boundary, never simple concatenation)
b_rows_sample.statement: A knowledge-composition mechanism analogous to Sanskrit's sound-combination rules, proposed to feed the typed epistemic graph's composition rules and the Verification Gate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: transformation history as a first-class knowledge-object structure: origin + transformation rule + new expression + semantic continuity
b_rows_sample.statement: The concrete storage shape for the Escher invariant-preserving-transformation target, derived from the dhatu-root-to-derived-word lineage pattern.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the eight-case epistemic grammar (Who? Does what? Using what? For whom? From where? Belongs to whom? In which context?) as a relationship ontology
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes Sanskrit's grammatical case system as a richer relationship vocabulary for the typed epistemic graph than a bare node-edge label set.

b_rows_sample.anchor: guna/vrddhi maturation ladder: Observation -> Information -> Knowledge -> Understanding -> Wisdom; growth != replacement
b_rows_sample.statement: Maps Sanskrit's controlled-amplification vowel transformations to a knowledge-maturity ladder where growth preserves identity while raising expression level.

b_rows_sample.anchor: refinement: not 'word order does not matter' but 'meaning should be reconstructed from invariant relationships'
b_rows_sample.statement: The HPA explicitly corrects the folk claim about Sanskrit word-order freedom before drawing the architectural lesson, modeling a discipline of not overclaiming from a linguistic fact.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS is not a language model; it is a meaning-preservation and meaning-transformation system.
b_rows_sample.statement: A re-derivation of the admitted character stance from the fifth (linguistic/grammatical) derivation route, contrasting LLM's Expression->Probability->Expression with KnowledgeOS's Meaning Root->Context->Evidence->Reasoning Rules->Expression.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Pāṇini's Aṣṭādhyāyī is a 2,500-year-old precedent for computational semantic representation that is order-independent and relationship-first (deterministic production rules, recursive application, precedence-based conflict resolution, meta-linguistic notation).
b_rows_sample.statement: External-research finding (citing linguistics/CS literature) offered as strong evidence that Karaka-based, permutation-invariant semantic representation is not a novel invention but has a long computational-linguistics precedent (PERIN, 2020 CoNLL shared-task winner).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Karaka theory: eight semantic roles (Karta/Karma/Karana/Sampradana/Apadana/Adhikarana/Sambandha/Sambodhana) mapped to Actor/Object/Instrument/Beneficiary/Source/Context/Relationship/Address
b_rows_sample.statement: A concrete semantic-role-labeling scheme proposed as a strong candidate mechanism (ARTHA-MECH-001), citing real Sanskrit-NLP literature.

b_rows_sample.anchor: case-to-relationship mapping table (nominative=Who/what asserts?; accusative=What is affected?; instrumental=Through what evidence/tool?; dative=For whom/purpose?; ablative=From where/source?; genitive=Ownership/provenance; locative=Context; vocative=Intended recipient)
b_rows_sample.statement: The original (v1) worked mapping of the eight Sanskrit grammatical cases onto knowledge-relationship roles, later reused verbatim in the v2 deepening and the formal reviews.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sanskrit Grammar Lens = Semantic Integrity & Transformation Lens; among all lenses so far, Sanskrit grammar is one of the closest analogues to the internal language of KnowledgeOS itself.
b_rows_sample.statement: The author's own closing classification, later quoted verbatim in the formal review (S0290).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Human expression -> Lexical recognition -> Candidate interpretations -> Contextual/governance interpretation -> Canonical domain act -> Deterministic execution ... The Kernel should consume an already-resolved domain candidate; it should not solve linguistic ambiguity.
b_rows_sample.statement: Sanskrit/compiler lens critique offers a compiler-analogy pipeline (human expression -> lexical recognition -> candidate interpretations -> contextual/governance interpretation -> canonical domain act -> deterministic execution) mapped to front-end (interpretation) / semantic boundary (meaning candidate) / domain core (constitutionally valid transition) / runtime layer (execution), yielding the principle that the Kernel consumes an already-resolved domain candidate and does not itself resolve linguistic ambiguity -- offered as possibly a better model than 'Kernel = admission boundary' alone.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate interpretation != Knowledge. ... CandidateKnowledge + EvidenceReferences + Justification + Context -> Kernel domain decision ... not: raw expression -> Kernel -> meaning
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends the Sanskrit-compiler 'Expression != Meaning' lens to 'Candidate interpretation != Knowledge', concluding the Kernel should not care how a candidate was produced and its input should be a structured CandidateKnowledge+EvidenceReferences+Justification+Context bundle, never raw expression -- preserving the existing Expression<->Meaning boundary and P5's finding that semantic mechanisms remain replaceable providers.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 4. Paninian / Sanskrit Grammar Lens -- Generate Structure from Rules ... Can expression be transformed deterministically into structured representation through explicit rules? ... A deterministic semantic compiler can exist outside the Kernel.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Paninian/Sanskrit-grammar lens (distinct from Vani: can expression be transformed deterministically into structured representation via explicit rules -- Expression -> morphological/syntactic analysis -> semantic roles -> structured candidate), concluding the architectural lesson is not to build Sanskrit into the Kernel but that a deterministic semantic compiler may exist outside it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Don't interpret a token in isolation. Determine its role and relationship within the whole expression. ... Sanskrit cases encode relations such as actor, object, means, source, ownership and context. ... EVENT: Approval. ACTOR: Architect. OBJECT: Nexus Upgrade. BASIS/INSTRUMENT: Security Assessment.
b_rows_sample.statement: Borrows from Sanskrit case grammar the principle 'don't interpret a token in isolation, determine its role and relationship within the whole expression' -- Sanskrit cases encode relations like actor, object, means, source, ownership, context. Worked example: 'The architect approved the Nexus upgrade based on the security assessment' parses (unlike a flat tokenizer) into EVENT=Approval, ACTOR=Architect, OBJECT=Nexus Upgrade, BASIS/INSTRUMENT=Security Assessment.

b_rows_sample.anchor: we should NOT copy Sanskrit grammar literally. ... it proposes extracting architectural principles such as: root-based semantics; explicit relationships; generative transformation rules; separation of meaning and expression. ... our architecture should not be: KnowledgeOS -> Sanskrit grammar. It should be: Sanskrit grammar -> architectural lens -> semantic parsing principles -> KnowledgeOS semantic compiler.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit warning against literally adopting Sanskrit grammar into KnowledgeOS: the value is in extracted architectural principles (root-based semantics, explicit relationships, generative transformation rules, separation of meaning and expression), never the grammar itself as an implementation. The correct chain is Sanskrit grammar -> architectural lens -> semantic parsing principles -> KnowledgeOS semantic compiler, never a direct KnowledgeOS -> Sanskrit grammar dependency.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Expression != Meaning ... the uploaded research explicitly identifies this as a central principle. ... we need a transformation: Expression -> MeaningStructure and only then: MeaningStructure -> Dimensions + Values + Relations. ... Expression -- semantic rules --> State structure and later: State structure -- expression rules --> Expression.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies the single most valuable Sanskrit-derived idea as Expression != Meaning, requiring a two-stage transformation Expression -> MeaningStructure -> Dimensions+Values+Relations; inverting the Paninian rule-based-transformation analogy gives a bidirectional pair: Expression --semantic rules--> State structure, and State structure --expression rules--> Expression.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sanskrit grammar can help us determine: What role does this expression play? It cannot by itself determine: Whether the statement is true. ... Semantic parsing != Epistemic validation. This distinction is critical.
b_rows_sample.statement: States a critical limit of the grammar lens: it can determine what role an expression plays (grammar can parse 'Nexus runs version 3.85' perfectly) but cannot by itself determine whether the statement is true -- truth still requires Evidence->Source->Observation->Validation->Truth/uncertainty. Formalizes Semantic parsing != Epistemic validation as a critical, never-to-be-conflated distinction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Ignored(M) = no observed response. Rejected(M) = negative response. Challenged(M) = counter-signal. Unobserved(M) = receiver state unavailable. Ambiguous(M) = multiple interpretations remain. Zero(M) = removal preserves the contracted result. These are not interchangeable. Especially: Ignored != Zer
a_rows_sample.statement: Names six distinct, non-interchangeable communication-response states (Ignored, Rejected, Challenged, Unobserved, Ambiguous, Zero), explicitly asserting Ignored != Zero and Rejected != Zero as an important new proposed test of the Zero framework's discipline.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Adding Zero / Neutrality is actually a very important refinement ... The stable neutral reference point from which knowledge can be observed, compared, transformed, and corrected without being corrupted by the observer or the transformation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Raw brainstorming draft introducing Zero/Neutrality as an eighth lens extending the Vedic extraction: Zero is not 'nothing' but the non-distorting ground/reference frame connecting the Vedic lens, Navya-Nyāya, Kashmir Śaivism, Vedānta, and TMS/AGM into one deeper architectural pattern.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero should not become a new constitutional article ... Role: Explains why the existing 8 dimensions must exist. Not: New dimension. Not: Kernel object. Not: Implementation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues, per-dimension (Identity, Context, Evidence, Contradiction, Transformation, Agent), that Zero already resolves to existing kernel confirmations, and proposes the classification 'Foundational Meta-Principle' rather than a new dimension or kernel object.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero is correctly placed outside the kernel, otherwise it would create exactly the kind of collapse KnowledgeOS is designed to prevent.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the HPA's Zero analysis as an architecture-track (not research-track) refinement, arguing Zero must remain outside the kernel — a meta-principle admitted as a twelfth law would re-open the kernel it is meant to protect.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero function (HPA) | Reference Architecture instantiation | Resolution ... Zero is therefore not a missing component — it is the property of the boundary design.
b_rows_sample.statement: Shows Zero is already distributed across the frozen Reference Architecture's kernel services (Verification Gate=neutral admission, Contradiction Registry=neutral suspension, Dimension Registry=comparison baseline, Identity+History=continuity, Decision Interlock+Projection+Agency=perspective without collapse, Authority Service=authority separation) rather than being a missing component.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero is not another rule. It is the architectural attitude behind all rules.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the meta-level claim that Zero names the anti-collapse property the whole boundary design instantiates, with an explicit boundary warning: naming a property is not creating a component — it must remain a framing, never a twelfth article.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS is a constitutional epistemic system that preserves the relationship between the Knower, the Known, and the evolution of understanding while maintaining a neutral reference point that prevents identity, evidence, context, and reasoning from collapsing into each other.
b_rows_sample.statement: Records the HPA's candidate character refinement enriching the UM-33 formulation with a neutral-reference clause; explicitly NOT adopted — head 43 stands until formal ratification (which occurs later in S0254).

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS SHALL maintain a neutral epistemic reference condition that prevents identity, evidence, authority, context, reasoning, agency, and transformation from collapsing into one another.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formally designates Zero as Z-KOS-001 (Neutral Epistemic Reference Principle, Type: Foundational Meta-Principle — not Kernel, not Dimension, not Invariant), opening a new Z-KOS-xxx meta-principle namespace distinct from the invariant register (unchanged at 25+4).

type_signature.domain: epistemic dimensions (identity, evidence, authority, context, reasoning, agency, transformation)

b_rows_sample.anchor: Representation → Identity | Document becomes knowledge ... Agent → Reality | Opinion becomes truth
b_rows_sample.statement: States the 'category collapse' insight: Zero's strongest contribution is that every major KnowledgeOS failure mode is a specific collapse (Representation→Identity, Authority→Truth, Probability→Truth, Similarity→Identity, Observation→Inference, Transformation→Replacement, Contradiction→Error, Agent→Reality) — eight named collapses Zero forbids.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Everything is relative to Zero could accidentally create abstract absolutism · hidden truth authority · a philosophical kernel
b_rows_sample.statement: States the P5 warning that Zero must not become too powerful: Zero does not tell us what is true, it only preserves the conditions under which truth can be investigated — the guard preventing Z-KOS-001 from becoming a hidden ninth kernel law.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS builds a constitutional epistemic structure around a neutral reference principle: Zero. Zero does not define truth; it preserves the separation, continuity, and accountability required for truth discovery.
b_rows_sample.statement: Records the HPA's ratified character expression with the Zero clause — recorded here as ratified, but this reading is itself superseded shortly after in S0255, which holds the character PROPOSED pending formal ratification.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero has reached the correct architectural maturity level: it is not a new kernel concept, but it explains the reason the kernel has its boundaries.
b_rows_sample.statement: HPA synthesis confirming Zero's classification (Foundational Meta-Principle) and stating the strongest outcome: Zero did not enlarge KnowledgeOS — it made the architecture smaller and clearer.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero is not another rule. It is the architectural attitude behind all rules ... Zero was not missing — it was distributed across the architecture.
b_rows_sample.statement: Re-affirms the finding that Zero ≠ component, Zero = property of the boundaries; presents the six-mechanism correspondence table (neutral admission→Verification Gate, neutral suspension→Contradiction Registry, reference frame→Dimension Registry, identity continuity→Identity+History, perspective without collapse→Decision Interlock+Projection+Agency, authority separation→Authority Service).

b_rows_sample.anchor: do not make Zero a kernel article. Why? Because then Zero would become the very thing it prevents: Article 12 — Everything must follow Zero ⇒ Zero becomes authority
b_rows_sample.statement: Re-affirms the governance constraint that Zero must not become a kernel article, with an explicit self-referential danger example (a hypothetical Article 12 turning Zero itself into an authority, which is precisely what Zero forbids).

b_rows_sample.anchor: This remains a character statement, not a kernel rule. The uploaded record correctly keeps it proposed until formal ratification.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the prior record's status reading: the earlier Z-KOS-001 ratification (S0254) treated the character formulation as ratified, but the HPA now holds it explicitly PROPOSED until a separate formal-ratification act; adds 'transformation' to the collapse list as the preferred variant.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge = Identity + Context + Evidence + Reasoning + Agent + Transformation + Time + Uncertainty
b_rows_sample.statement: Refines the twelve-lens convergence pattern by adding 'Uncertainty' as an eighth term (sourced from Zero's neutral pre-judgement state), already carried by the existing Negative-State Model — a confirmation, not new content.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS is not a system that stores truth. It is a system that prevents the conditions required for truth discovery from being corrupted. Zero is the name for that prevention.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the sharpest architectural conclusion of the whole Zero research trajectory, consistent with head 43 and the BD-4 justified-epistemic-state distinction; a character-level conclusion, not a kernel rule.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero: The Quranic equivalent is close to Al-Ḥaqq. The stable truth/reference ... This resonates with your Zero principle.
b_rows_sample.statement: Notes the resonance between Al-Ḥaqq (stable neutral-reality reference, as opposed to human opinion) and the already-developed Zero principle — an independent re-derivation of Zero from a second tradition family.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Witness Consciousness / Zero Lens ... Events change, Knowledge states change, Reference remains. This is exactly your Zero idea.
b_rows_sample.statement: Maps the witness-consciousness concept (observer remains stable while thoughts/events change) directly onto the Zero principle as an independent re-derivation from a different Vedāntic angle.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A trustworthy knowledge system must not only accumulate knowledge; it must reduce the distortions that prevent knowledge from being correctly understood.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the most valuable Moksha extraction as a meta-goal framing routing to the Zero principle, explicitly not becoming another kernel dimension.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS is not a machine that knows. KnowledgeOS is a system that protects the possibility of knowing.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the final architectural insight of the Moksha synthesis, a character-consistent variant of head 43 and the Zero conclusion, strengthening Z-KOS-001 ('Zero = the state where distortion is minimized') without adding a new dimension.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels share the notation 'Zero'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Take P which is epistemically well-supported but administratively rejected. ... Epistemic and Governance status must be tested as orthogonal dimensions.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes testing (not yet establishing) that EpistemicStatus and GovernanceStatus are orthogonal dimensions, illustrated by a proposition that is epistemically Supported yet administratively Rejected, and by an Epistemically-Unknown proposition coexisting with GovernanceStatus=AcceptedForInvestigation; if such states are meaningful, one scalar status cannot represent both dimensions without information loss.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EMPIRICAL CONFIRMATION of ARC D's separation -- and the separation was ALREADY RUNNING, schema-enforced, before the theory derived it ... NEITHER axis is the theory's Sigma ... There is NO field in the running system that records whether a claim is SUPPORTED BY EVIDENCE.
b_rows_sample.statement: EXP-12 counts (status, authority) combinations across the 40 EKP cards and finds more distinct pairs than either axis alone has values, empirically confirming the two axes vary independently (matching the schema's own stated independence); however neither axis is the theory's Sigma (epistemic support), so the running system implements Lifecycle x SourceTrust but not Lifecycle x SourceTrust x EpistemicSupport.

b_rows_sample.anchor: draft <=> provisional is a perfect biconditional: 13 of 13 in each direction. ... On the running estate the two dimensions are deterministically linked on the draft axis. The declaration is unfalsified as a PERMISSION and unexercised as a FACT -- so it is NOT independent evidence for Sigma perp Gamma.
b_rows_sample.statement: Measuring (status,authority) pairs across all 39 frontmatter-bearing EKP documents finds only six of forty possible cells occupied, with a perfect biconditional between status=draft and authority=provisional (13/13 each direction), directly contradicting the schema comment's claim that status is independent of authority: on the running estate the two dimensions are deterministically linked on the draft axis, so the independence declaration is unfalsified as a permission but unexercised (and empirically false) as a fact, and is therefore not independent evidence for Sigma-perp-Gamma; additionally 93 of 132 markdown files under docs/knowledge/ carry no frontmatter at all, constituting a real running instance of the 'not assessed' state the theory says it cannot express.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The running system has TWO of the five axes ... and ZERO of the evidence, supersession-as-state, validity, or asked axes as ENFORCED concepts. No field records whether a claim is supported by evidence; no lint rule mentions evidence. ... Against the theory: Sigma has never been tested by reality. It has no instance.
b_rows_sample.statement: Finding SG-7: measuring the real EKP finds only two axes implemented (status as a lifecycle/governance-process axis with 4 distinct values across 38 documents; authority as a source-trust axis with 4 values; 7 observed joint pairs confirming independence), and zero of the five theoretical Sigma axes (evidence, supersession-as-state, validity, asked) as enforced concepts -- no field records evidential support, no lint rule (of 16 listed identifiers) mentions evidence; concludes Sigma has never been tested by reality (no instance) while the EKP itself has no mechanism at all for epistemic status, so a factually-refuted document with status=approved/authority=authoritative has no way to record that fact.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'epistemic-vs-governance-status-orthogonality' POSSIBLY relates to 'sigma-lifecycle-sourcetrust-separation' (batch B0041).
