a_rows_sample.anchor: Manas = state-processing ... Buddhi = discrimination
a_rows_sample.statement: From the senses->mind->intelligence->soul hierarchy (Soul > Buddhi > Manas > Indriya > Objects): refines KnowledgeOS Kernel ~ Manas+Buddhi operational system (not simply Kernel=Mind), since Manas (dynamic internal workspace/state coordinator: receives observations, holds candidate interpretations, combines signals, maintains attention, carries temporary state, presents alternatives to Buddhi) and Buddhi (discrimination/decision operator: admissible? supported? contradictory? relevant? permitted? justified? should this transition occur?) perform different functions. Gives control loop W_t->O_t->M_t->B_t->A_t->K_{t+1}.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Kernel must distinguish operation from operator
a_rows_sample.statement: From 3.27's false-agency verse ('I am the doer' bewilderment; actions carried out through the modes of nature): proposes 'Kernel must distinguish operation from operator' -- the system must not confuse 'I produced this result' with 'this operation produced this result under these conditions'. Enormous implications identified for provenance, attribution, auditability, reproducibility, causality, and responsibility, connecting to existing provenance/identity work.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Buddhi(x) \neq Buddhi(x\mid \text{unexamined attachment})
a_rows_sample.statement: From 3.34/3.40-42 (attachment/aversion as stumbling blocks operating through senses/mind/intelligence to cover knowledge): proposes a candidate kernel safety invariant Buddhi(x) != Buddhi(x|unexamined attachment), operationally Discern(x) -> CheckBias(x) -> Qualify(x) -> Decide(x). Explicitly notes Chapter 3 does not prove the Qualify operator, only gives philosophical motivation for why a discrimination stage must exist (corroboration != derivation).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero(K_t) = Missingness + Distortion ... Z_t=(G_t,D_t)
a_rows_sample.statement: Major potential refinement to Zero: distinguishes Problem A ignorance (K_t lacks x) from Problem B corruption (x in K_t but x is distorted, misclassified, attached, contradictory, or wrongly interpreted). Proposes Zero(K_t) = Missingness + Distortion, possibly Z_t=(G_t,D_t) where G_t=knowledge gaps and D_t=epistemic distortions -- explicitly flagged as needing to be tested against the existing Zero corpus before adoption, not assumed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Operation\ applicability \subseteq Type(OperationContext)
a_rows_sample.statement: From 3.35's Svadharma (better one's own duty imperfectly than another's perfectly): proposes Operation applicability subset Type(OperationContext) -- an operation is not valid merely because it can technically be executed; it must be valid for the current role/context/state (Operation+Context+Capability+State -> Admissibility), connecting to the existing Admissible concept. From 3.26, proposes progressive-not-destructive knowledge transformation: detect misconception -> introduce evidence -> discriminate -> reconcile -> transition, rather than delete-and-replace, compatible with provenance/lineage/supersession/contradiction/observation/state-transition modeling.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \mathbb K_t = ( M_t, B_t, K_t, \Sigma_t, G_t, D_t, \Gamma_t )
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a 12-operator candidate catalogue (Receive, Attend, Compare, Discern_B, Accept, Reject, Hold, Transform, Act, Observe-consequence, Reconcile, Purify) and a candidate kernel state (fraktur K)_t=(M_t,B_t,K_t,Sigma_t,G_t,D_t,Gamma_t) [Manas/working state, Buddhi/discrimination state, knowledge state, epistemic dimensions, detected gaps, detected distortions, operational mode/guna]. Gives transition algebra (fraktur K)_t --Omega--> O_t --M--> M_{t+1} --B--> B_{t+1} --Q--> Q_t --A--> a_t --delta--> K_{t+1}, noting Qualify's natural position between Buddhi and Action ('Perceive->Think->Discriminate->Qualify->Act') but explicitly leaving whether Qualify deserves this exact formal role OPEN, consistent with Steps 285-287.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Kernel integrity is an epistemic property ... not merely a software-security property.
a_rows_sample.statement: From the raga(desire)->anger->illusion->covered-knowledge chain (desire called an enemy that covers knowledge): builds a KnowledgeOS threat model indriya->manas->buddhi->knowledge corruption, concluding Kernel integrity is an epistemic property, not merely a software-security property -- proposed as potentially one of the foundational concepts of the theory.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Cross-chapter Kernel Reconciliation ... What is the smallest formally sufficient KnowledgeOS kernel
a_rows_sample.statement: Recommends not canonizing any Chapter-3 finding, and instead performing a 'Cross-chapter Kernel Reconciliation' over Chapters 3-18: a formal matrix Gita concept -> KnowledgeOS hypothesis -> existing corpus object -> existing operator -> missing operator -> mathematical property -> falsification test. Poses the key research question: what is the smallest formally sufficient KnowledgeOS kernel capable of performing Manas-processing, Buddhi-discrimination, state transition, purification, and action under changing guna modes -- framed as moving from philosophical reflection to formal kernel construction while respecting that correspondence cannot itself create a canonical primitive.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Jñāna : (K_t,\;Doubt_t) \rightarrow (K_{t+1},\;Doubt_{t+1})
b_rows_sample.statement: From the closing verses (knowledge as a weapon that cuts doubt arising from ignorance): models Jnana not as a primitive/object but as a transformation operator J:(K_t,Doubt_t)->(K_{t+1},Doubt_{t+1}), with intended effect Doubt_{t+1}<Doubt_t under appropriate conditions -- reinforcing the earlier Jnana~delta interpretation over Jnana=Knowledge. Also formalizes Ajnana->Samsaya->Jnana->Buddhi->Karma as a candidate kernel cycle: ignorance->doubt->investigation->knowledge->discrimination->decision->action->new observation->updated K_t.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero \neq Doubt ... "I don't know X." -> Zero ... "I have two conflicting claims about X." -> Samsaya
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly separates five concepts previously at risk of conflation: Zero (detection of missing/absent knowledge, 'I don't know X'); Samsaya/doubt (unresolved epistemic uncertainty, 'I have two conflicting claims about X'); Ajnana (lack/absence of understanding); Jnana (knowledge/transformation that resolves or transforms uncertainty, 'evidence establishes claim A'); Buddhi (discrimination/decision capability, 'therefore accept A'). Zero != Doubt is proposed as an excellent candidate for formalization.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t=(X_t,\Sigma_t,\Pi_t,\Gamma_t,\Delta_t)
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes KnowledgeOS is not fundamentally a set (beyond K_t subset K): a five-component knowledge state K_t=(X_t,Sigma_t,Pi_t,Gamma_t,Delta_t) where X_t=represented knowledge content, Sigma_t=epistemic quality/state dimensions, Pi_t=provenance, Gamma_t=context/constraints, Delta_t=detected gaps/uncertainties, with kernel transitions K_{t+1}=F(K_t,O_t,B_t,A_t) -- assessed as a much richer mathematical object than K_t subset K alone.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Content equality? ... Epistemic equality? ... Provenance-sensitive equality? ... Behavioural equality?
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly connects Chapter 4's doubt/knowledge/lineage material to the Step 287 open equality problem K_1 equiv K_2, posing four distinct candidate readings: content equality (X_1=X_2); epistemic equality (Sigma_1=Sigma_2); provenance-sensitive equality ((X_1,Pi_1) cong_lambda (X_2,Pi_2)); behavioural equality (delta(K_1,o)=delta(K_2,o) for all o). States plainly that Chapter 4 gives philosophical motivation for asking this question but does not provide the mathematical answer -- Step 287's OPEN status remains correct.

Constructs a five-operator formal algebra: Omega:W->O (observe), Q:O->E (qualify), J:ExK->K' (know/transform), B:K'xC->D (discriminate), A:D->W' (act), with explicit composition K_{t+1}=J(Q(Omega(W_t)),K_t), D_t=B(K_{t+1},C_t), W_{t+1}=A(D_t,W_t). Proposes working kernel definition Kernel=(K_t,Omega,Q,J,B,A,Delta,Sigma,Pi) with central transition K_t --Omega,Q--> E_t --J--> K'_t --B--> D_t --A--> W_{t+1} --Omega--> K_{t+1}, explicitly non-canonical pending formal validation. Frames Chapter 4's strongest contribution as a theory of what the kernel DOES with knowledge (Knowledge->discrimination->decision->action->new state), not another primitive.

b_rows_sample.anchor: freeze a KERNEL-CANDIDATE-v1 consisting of only \{K_t,\;Zero,\;Sa\d{m}śaya,\;Jñāna,\;Buddhi,\;Decision,\;Action\}
b_rows_sample.statement: Recommends, before simulating the whole Gita-KnowledgeOS system, freezing a minimal KERNEL-CANDIDATE-v1 = {K_t, Zero, Samsaya, Jnana, Buddhi, Decision, Action} and mathematically testing operators J, B, A, Omega, Q for closure, typing, identity, composition, reversibility, monotonicity, and information loss -- explicit caution that the source's religious claims must not be converted into technical claims by analogy alone; the strongest candidates are those independently derivable from KnowledgeOS per Step 286. Chapter 4 generates and corroborates hypotheses; it does not ratify the kernel.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'hpa-gita-chapter3-manas-buddhi-hierarchy-distortion-model' POSSIBLY relates to 'hpa-gita-chapter4-doubt-jnana-transformation-operator' (batch B0054). Note: Rereads Gita Chapter 3 (Karma-yoga) after Chapters 4-18, deriving mechanisms for constructing/simulating the kernel rather than treating it as analogy. Introduces the hierarchy Soul>Buddhi>Manas>Indriya>Objects, refining Kernel~Mind into Kernel~Manas+Buddhi operational system (two distinct functions, Manas=state-processing, Buddhi=discrimination). Gives a control-loop model W_t->O_t->M_t->B_t->A_t->K_{t+1}. From the false-agency verse (3.27), proposes 'Kernel must distinguish operation from operator' -- the system must not confuse 'I produced this result' with 'this operation produced this result under these conditions', with strong implications for provenance/attribution/auditability. Proposes a kernel safety invariant Buddhi(x) != Buddhi(x|unexamined attachment), i.e. Discern->CheckBias->Qualify->Decide, explicitly not proof of the Qualify operator, only motivation. Major refinement: Zero(K_t) = Missingness + Distortion, Z_t=(G_t,D_t) (ignorance vs corruption of already-present but distorted knowledge) -- flagged as requiring a corpus test before adoption. Gives Svadharma->Operation applicability subset Type(OperationContext), connecting to the existing Admissible concept. Proposes progressive-not-destructive knowledge transformation (detect misconception->introduce evidence->discriminate->reconcile->transition, not delete-and-replace). Gives a 12-operator candidate catalogue (Receive,Attend,Compare,Discern_B,Accept,Reject,Hold,Transform,Act,Observe-consequence,Reconcile,Purify) and a candidate kernel state (fraktur K)_t=(M_t,B_t,K_t,Sigma_t,G_t,D_t,Gamma_t) with transition algebra (fraktur K)_t-Omega->O_t-M->M_{t+1}-B->B_{t+1}-Q->Q_t-A->a_t-delta->K_{t+1}. Closes proposing a Cross-chapter Kernel Reconciliation matrix (Gita concept->hypothesis->existing corpus object->existing operator->missing operator->mathematical property->falsification test).

a_rows_sample.anchor:
Identity
eq Name
eq State
eq Representation. ... How can KnowledgeOS know that the 'Nexus' observed yesterday is the same domain/system entity as the 'Nexus' discussed today after migration?
a_rows_sample.statement: Opens Step 195: everything so far assumed a known identity for the tracked entity, but in distributed systems names change, systems are replaced, repositories fork, services are renamed, AI agents are recreated, and knowledge is copied; poses Identity!=Name!=State!=Representation and proposes deriving an Identity-Continuity Model connecting to the Chapter 2 continuity lens and DDD's identity-vs-attributes distinction.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
Identity
eq Name
eq State
eq Representation
b_rows_sample.statement: Core Step 195 distinction: an entity's Identity, its Name, its State, and its Representation(s) are four separate things; StateChange does not imply IdentityChange (worked example: NexusSystem's version changing from 3.69 to 3.70 does not change its identity).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Name is an attribute of an identity, not necessarily the identity itself.
b_rows_sample.statement: A system's hostname changing (nexus3.dgverlag.de -> nexus-prod.dg.de) does not necessarily change the underlying entity; Name(x,t)=n_t is an attribute of Identity(x)=i, not the identity itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Representation\rightarrow Entity is a mapping that itself requires evidence.
b_rows_sample.statement: The same entity may appear as many different representations (CMDB, DNS, monitoring, firewall, KnowledgeOS, Git, Jira, docs); worked example (CMDB:Nexus, DNS:nexus3.dgverlag.de, IP, container, repo, KnowledgeOS:Nexus) shows the question of whether these are six entities or one entity with six representations cannot be answered from names alone -- Representation->Entity is itself an evidence-requiring mapping.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Relationship claims are themselves knowledge claims.
b_rows_sample.statement: RefersTo(R_i,x) relations carry their own epistemic status (e.g. RefersTo(CMDB:Nexus,x)=Confirmed vs RefersTo(DNS:...,x)=Likely), restating the earlier principle that relationship claims are themselves knowledge claims, applied specifically to identity reference.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ID(x)=constant while: Attributes(x,t) may vary. ... TechnicalIdentity \neq DomainIdentity.
b_rows_sample.statement: Recommends a stable identity key distinct from mutable attributes (Name, Location, Version, Configuration, Owner); separately warns that a technical ID (e.g. a database UUID) is not automatically a domain identity -- if a record is deleted and recreated under a new UUID, the domain may or may not regard it as the same business entity; the correct question is what makes an entity the same entity in the domain, not what the database schema says.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Identity \rightarrow Continuity \rightarrow Lineage \rightarrow State \rightarrow Evidence \rightarrow Knowledge \rightarrow Decision \rightarrow Action. ... needs identity-aware, temporally versioned, provenance-preserving transitions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 195 verdict: the architecture cannot safely be a simple CRUD model of 'things and their current status'; it requires identity-aware, temporally versioned, provenance-preserving transitions, restating the full forward chain Identity->Continuity->Lineage->State->Evidence->Knowledge->Decision->Action and the reverse observation chain Reality->Observation->Representation->IdentityAssessment->Knowledge.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels share the notation 'Identity != Name != State != Representation'

a_rows_sample.anchor: If identity is wrong, everything downstream can be wrong. ... Nexus / Nexus Repository / Nexus3 / nexus3.dgverlag.de / the artifact repository / the old Nexus server ... Same name\neq Same entity ... Different name\neq Different entity. This becomes a fundamental KnowledgeOS principle.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the fundamental principle SameName≠SameEntity and DifferentName≠DifferentEntity, illustrated with six differently-named references possibly denoting the same Nexus system, and warns that identity errors propagate downstream through Comparison→Conflict→EvidenceAggregation→Inference→Discrepancy.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Three things must be separated ... Representation r ... Entity x ... Proposition P(x). Representation\neq Entity\neq Proposition
a_rows_sample.statement: Separates Representation (textual expression r), Entity (the referent x), and Proposition (a statement P(x) about that entity) as three distinct concepts.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DDD interpretation ... Identity — which domain object is this? Value — what does it represent? Context — where does this identity have meaning? Aggregate — what consistency boundary governs it? Reference — how do we locate it? ... KnowledgeEntity with a stable identity independent of how it happens
a_rows_sample.statement: Maps identity to five DDD concepts (Identity/Value/Context/Aggregate/Reference), introducing a KnowledgeEntity domain concept with stable identity independent of naming.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Canonical identity ... ID(x) ... EntityId: system:nexus:production ... multiple representations can resolve to it ... if sufficient evidence establishes Resolve(r_i)=x.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a canonical entity identifier ID(x) (e.g. system:nexus:production) to which multiple surface representations may resolve given sufficient evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Resolution is not string matching ... Normalize("Nexus3")=Normalize("nexus3") and conclude identity. That is unsafe. Instead EntityResolution = f(Representation,Context,Evidence,IdentityRules). The output should itself have an epistemic status.
a_rows_sample.statement: Warns that string-normalization matching is unsafe for entity resolution, defining EntityResolution=f(Representation,Context,Evidence,IdentityRules) with an epistemic status on the output rather than a boolean.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Entity resolution is an inference ... Nexus3 is running on nexus3.dgverlag.de. We infer Entity("Nexus3")=Entity("nexus3.dgverlag.de"). But this is not necessarily directly observed. ... IdentityAssertion with evidence and provenance.
a_rows_sample.statement: Connects entity resolution to Step 10's inference machinery: identity claims are themselves inferences, not direct observations, and must be represented as an IdentityAssertion carrying evidence and provenance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Identity assertion ... I_A=(r,x,S,Ctx,\Pi,\tau) ... "Nexus3" \equiv system:nexus:production. But KnowledgeOS should know why it believes that.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines IdentityAssertion I_A=(representation,entity,Support,Context,Provenance,Validity) so KnowledgeOS always records why an identity claim is believed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Identity is contextual ... Nexus means the Nexus product in one context ... the production deployment in another context. Meaning(Nexus,C_1)\neq Meaning(Nexus,C_2). Identity is interpreted within context. We should never create a universal global identity merely from a name.
a_rows_sample.statement: States identity is interpreted within context (Meaning(Nexus,C1)≠Meaning(Nexus,C2)) — a universal global identity must never be created merely from a name.

a_rows_sample.anchor:
Product versus instance ... NexusProduct versus NexusInstance_{Production} ... Software
eq Deployment
eq Container
eq Host
eq Service
eq Endpoint. A DDD model must preserve these distinctions.
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Product from Instance and six further layered concepts (Software/Deployment/Container/Host/Service/Endpoint) that a DDD model must preserve separately.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Entity identity can be hierarchical ... x_{product}, x_{deployment}, x_{host} ... DeploymentOf(x_{deployment},x_{product}) RunsOn(x_{deployment},x_{host}) ExposedAt(x_{deployment},endpoint). Thus identity is not just a flat lookup. It is a semantic graph. ... Entity graph G_X=(\mathcal X,\mathcal R_
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a hierarchical Entity graph G_X=(X,R_X) with typed relations (DeploymentOf, RunsOn, ExposedAt) linking product/deployment/host/endpoint layers, arguing identity is a semantic graph, not a flat lookup.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Now semantic equivalence ... Version(Nexus)=3.69 and Nexus is running release 3.69 ... may be semantically equivalent. But Nexus was version 3.69 in 2024 is not equivalent to P_1 if P_1 is intended to describe the current state. ... Define semantic equivalence P_1\equiv_C P_2 ... The context subscri
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines context-relative semantic equivalence P1≡_C P2, warning that without the context subscript equivalence becomes dangerously absolute, illustrated by a temporally-scoped proposition that is not equivalent to a current-state one.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Equivalence is not identity ... A_1: Nexus=3.69 from a document. A_2: Nexus=3.69 from an API. They may express the same proposition P(A_1)\equiv P(A_2). But they remain separate assertions because their evidence; provenance; acquisition time; source; epistemic state are different. EquivalentProposit
a_rows_sample.statement: States EquivalentProposition ≠ SameAssertion: two assertions expressing the same proposition from different sources remain distinct assertion objects because their evidence/provenance/acquisition differ — essential for correct evidence aggregation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Duplicate evidence problem ... If B was copied from A, we must not count A+B as two independent pieces of evidence. Therefore semantic equivalence alone is insufficient. We also need EvidenceDependency and SourceIndependence. This connects Step 12 directly to Step 11.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms semantic equivalence alone is insufficient for evidence counting; EvidenceDependency and SourceIndependence must also be checked (connecting to Step 11), so copied duplicate documents are not double-counted.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Four different relationships ... Same x_1=x_2 ... Equivalent P_1\equiv P_2 ... Related P_1\sim P_2 ... Contradictory P_1\bowtie P_2 ... Distinct: No established semantic relationship.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines four (five including Distinct) proposition/entity relationship kinds: Same, Equivalent, Related, Contradictory, Distinct.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Contradiction now becomes much more precise ... Conflict= f(EntityResolution,SemanticComparison,Context,TemporalScope,ConflictRule). This is much stronger than simply comparing strings.
a_rows_sample.statement: Refines Conflict detection as a function of EntityResolution, SemanticComparison, Context, TemporalScope, and ConflictRule together, rather than simple string comparison.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Example ... Nexus3.dgverlag.de=3.69 and ProductionNexus=3.70. Before declaring conflict, KnowledgeOS must establish Entity(nexus3.dgverlag.de)=Entity(ProductionNexus)? and Environment(P_1)=Environment(P_2)? and Time(P_1)=Time(P_2)? Only then can it evaluate 3.69\neq3.70. This is precisely why identi
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example showing entity/environment/temporal identity must all be established before a version discrepancy can be declared a conflict — identity resolution is upstream of contradiction detection.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Entity resolution has uncertainty ... We should never force identity resolution into Same/NotSame too early. ResolutionStatus could include Unknown, Candidate, LikelySame, ConfirmedSame, LikelyDifferent, ConfirmedDifferent, Contested. This is another multidimensional epistemic object.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a seven-value ResolutionStatus enum (Unknown/Candidate/LikelySame/ConfirmedSame/LikelyDifferent/ConfirmedDifferent/Contested) instead of a premature boolean Same/NotSame.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate identity ... an LLM ... proposes Entity("repository server")=Entity("Nexus production"). We record CandidateIdentity. We do not immediately merge them. This prevents one of the most dangerous AI failure modes: semantic hallucination becoming structural identity.
a_rows_sample.statement: Names and guards against a specific AI failure mode — 'semantic hallucination becoming structural identity' — by recording LLM-proposed identity as CandidateIdentity rather than merging immediately.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Identity merge is a high-impact operation ... Merging them changes potentially huge parts of the graph. Merge(x_1,x_2) should be governed by an explicit policy. It should not be an ordinary side effect of an LLM extraction. ... Identity merge and provenance ... original identities; evidence; provena
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires entity Merge(x1,x2) be a policy-governed, auditable operation preserving original identities/evidence/provenance/contexts/timestamps/decision authority/reason — never an ordinary side effect of LLM extraction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Identity split ... Later evidence establishes they are distinct. We need Split(x)\rightarrow x_1,x_2 with historical provenance. Split\neq Delete. This is belief revision applied to entity identity.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the reverse Split(x)→x1,x2 operation with historical provenance preserved (Split≠Delete), applying belief-revision principles to entity identity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A common mistake is to say A_1,A_2\Rightarrow A_3 therefore A_3 has "the same confidence" as A_1,A_2. That is generally false. The epistemic quality of a derived proposition depends on what kind of inference produced it, what premises it depends on, how those premises depend on one another, and what
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns against assuming a derived proposition inherits its premises' confidence wholesale; its epistemic quality depends on the inference kind, premise dependencies, and the inference rule's own uncertainty.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The fundamental problem ... A_1=Strong and A_2=Weak. A_3=A_1\land A_2 ... It cannot simply inherit Strong. Nor should we arbitrarily assign Weak. ... \Sigma_{derived} = Propagate_\rho(\Sigma_{premises},Rule,Method,Dependency,Context)
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Σ_derived=Propagate_ρ(Σ_premises,Rule,Method,Dependency,Context) as the general propagation function, illustrated by a conjunction of a Strong and a Weak premise where neither naive inheritance is correct.

b_rows_sample.anchor: First distinction: uncertainty has different origins ... Premise uncertainty U_{premise} ... Inference uncertainty U_{inference} ... Model uncertainty U_{model} ... Measurement uncertainty U_{measurement} ... Semantic uncertainty U_{semantic} ... Context uncertainty U_{context} ... Uncertainty\neq o
b_rows_sample.statement: Enumerates six distinct uncertainty origins — premise, inference, model, measurement, semantic, context — establishing Uncertainty ≠ one universal quantity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This confirms our multidimensional model ... U_A=(U_{source},U_{measurement},U_{semantic},U_{inference},U_{model},U_{context}) ... more rigorous than U_A=0.3. A scalar may later be derived if a policy needs one.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a six-dimension uncertainty vector U_A, more rigorous than a bare scalar U_A=0.3, from which a policy-specific scalar may later be derived.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Dependency graph ... G_D=(V,E_D) ... A1, A2 → A3 → A5 ... Deps(A_3)=\{A_1,A_2\} and Deps(A_5)=\{A_3\}. Therefore uncertainty can propagate through the graph.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a derivation dependency graph G_D=(V,E_D) with Deps(A) giving direct premise sets, through which uncertainty can propagate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: But propagation depends on the inference method ... y=2x ... \sigma_y=2\sigma_x=0.2 ... a mathematical propagation rule. But now consider ... x is probably caused by y ... an abductive inference. Its uncertainty cannot be propagated using the same formula. PropagationFunction depends on InferenceMet
b_rows_sample.statement: Shows via a linear-uncertainty-propagation example (y=2x, σ_y=2σ_x) contrasted with an abductive inference that the propagation function itself depends on the inference method, not a single universal formula.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Deterministic derivation ... A_1\vdash Q ... the derivation itself does not introduce statistical uncertainty. However, the premises may still have epistemic uncertainty. Deterministic rule \not\Rightarrow uncertain premises. The rule may be certain while its inputs are not.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes rule certainty from premise certainty: a deterministic derivation rule does not itself add uncertainty, but its premises may still be epistemically uncertain — Deterministic rule ⇏ uncertain premises.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Statistical inference ... \hat\theta=10.2 with SE(\hat\theta)=0.4. The uncertainty belongs to the statistical inference. KnowledgeOS must preserve Estimate=10.2 and Uncertainty=0.4 rather than reducing the output to 10.2.
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires KnowledgeOS to preserve a statistical estimate together with its standard error (e.g. 10.2 ± 0.4) rather than collapsing to the point estimate alone.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Correlated evidence ... E_2=Copy(E_1), then Information(E_2\mid E_1)\approx0. Dependency structure must participate in uncertainty/support propagation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates that strongly correlated/copied evidence adds near-zero additional information, so dependency structure must participate in uncertainty/support propagation, not be treated as independent.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Unknown dependency ... a conservative policy might produce Support_{combined}\leq Support_{assuming independence}. But that inequality is policy-dependent, not a universal mathematical theorem. The kernel should preserve Dependency=Unknown. The assessment calculus decides what to do.
b_rows_sample.statement: Notes a conservative policy may cap combined support below the independence assumption when dependency is unknown, but this inequality is policy-dependent, not a universal theorem — the kernel only preserves Dependency=Unknown.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The most important statistical distinction ... P(A)=0.9 and P(B)=0.9 ... If independent P(A\land B)=0.81. If perfectly dependent P(A\land B)=0.9. Marginal confidence does not determine joint confidence. This is a major reason KnowledgeOS cannot use naive confidence multiplication.
b_rows_sample.statement: Uses two 0.9-confidence propositions to show joint confidence ranges from 0.81 (independent) to 0.9 (perfectly dependent) — marginal confidence does not determine joint confidence, ruling out naive confidence multiplication.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Statistical propagation needs a model ... Y=f(X_1,\ldots,X_n) ... Var(Y)\approx J\Sigma_XJ^T ... Covariance matters. This maps beautifully to our evidence-dependency model.
b_rows_sample.statement: Notes formal statistical uncertainty propagation Var(Y)≈JΣ_XJ^T requires the full covariance matrix, mapping naturally onto the evidence-dependency model — covariance matters, not just marginal uncertainties.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS should therefore preserve dependency, not just scores ... A1 confidence = 0.9, A2 confidence = 0.9 ... instead A1, A2, Dependency(A1,A2) = Independent / Dependent / Unknown. Then a calculus can determine the appropriate combination. This is one of the strongest architectural consequences
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues KnowledgeOS must store per-pair Dependency status alongside confidence scores rather than bare scores alone, called one of the strongest architectural consequences of the theory.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Derived knowledge should retain its dependency graph ... A_3=f(A_1,A_2). Basis(A_3)=\{A_1,A_2\}. If A_1 is retracted, we do not automatically retract A_3. Instead Reassess(A_3). This follows directly from Step 9.
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires derived assertions retain their basis (Basis(A3)={A1,A2}), so retracting one premise triggers Reassess, not automatic retraction — following directly from Step 9's dependency-propagation invariant.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Support propagation ... S_3=PropagateSupport_\rho(S_1,S_2,R,D,C) ... S_3=\min(S_1,S_2) ... S_3=S_1\times S_2 ... S_3=f(S_1,S_2,D). There is no universal formula.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines abstract support propagation S_3=PropagateSupport_ρ(S1,S2,R,D,C), showing min, product, and dependency-adjusted formulas as different rule-specific instances — no universal formula.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Uncertainty propagation ... U_3=PropagateUncertainty_\rho(U_1,U_2,R,D,C) ... The kernel stores uncertainty semantics; the calculus performs uncertainty propagation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines U_3=PropagateUncertainty_ρ(U1,U2,R,D,C) analogously to support propagation, with the architecture rule that the kernel stores uncertainty semantics while the calculus performs the actual propagation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A useful distinction: epistemic versus aleatory uncertainty ... Aleatory uncertainty Intrinsic variability/randomness ... Epistemic uncertainty Uncertainty caused by lack of knowledge ... We don't know which version is deployed. KnowledgeOS primarily deals with epistemic uncertainty, but may also en
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes aleatory uncertainty (intrinsic randomness, e.g. X~N(μ,σ²)) from epistemic uncertainty (lack of knowledge, e.g. unknown deployed version), noting KnowledgeOS primarily deals with the latter but should not collapse the two when both are relevant.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Example: infrastructure ... Backup configured ... Restore test succeeded ... Backup is operationally recoverable. A_1,A_2\Rightarrow A_3. But suppose A_2 is missing. Then A_1 alone may support Configured but not OperationallyRecoverable. Missing premise \Rightarrow Derived proposition remains unreso
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked backup-recoverability example showing that a missing premise (no restore test) leaves the derived proposition unresolved rather than falsely supported.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This gives us a concept of inference sufficiency ... Complete(R,\Gamma) meaning all required premises are available at the required epistemic level. Complete(R,\Gamma)=False \Rightarrow A_3 cannot be deductively derived. An LLM may still hypothesize A_3, but it must not label it as deterministic der
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines inference-sufficiency predicate Complete(R,Γ): if false, A3 cannot be deductively derived, though an LLM may hypothesize it as long as it is never mislabeled deterministic derivation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Partial derivation ... Candidate(A_3) and MissingPremise(A_2). This directly generates a discrepancy \Delta_{missing premise}. Lord can then search for evidence for A_2. So inference becomes another mechanism for gap discovery. Inference \rightarrow MissingPremise \rightarrow Discrepancy \rightarrow
b_rows_sample.statement: Shows a missing premise generates a Candidate(A3)+MissingPremise(A2) state that becomes a discrepancy Lord can act on, establishing the feedback loop Inference→MissingPremise→Discrepancy→EvidenceAcquisition — inference as another gap-discovery mechanism, i.e. KnowledgeOS can infer what it needs to know in order to infer what it wants to know.

a_aliases: Step 12: Identity, Entity Resolution, and Semantic Equivalence
b_aliases: Step 11: Uncertainty Propagation and Derived Knowledge

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'identity-entity-resolution-semantic-equivalence' POSSIBLY relates to 'uncertainty-propagation-derived-knowledge' (batch B0021). Note: S0866's Step 12: separates Representation/Entity/Proposition; defines KnowledgeEntity, canonical ID(x), entity graph G_X, IdentityAssertion as an evidence-based inference; defines context-relative semantic equivalence and EquivalentProposition!=SameAssertion; names 'semantic hallucination becoming structural identity' as a guarded-against AI failure mode; defines auditable Merge/Split, four separated operations (Extraction/Normalization/IdentityResolution/Validation), an ontology Omega with versioning, non-full-decidability of equivalence, and ID1-ID14 invariants; hands off to Step 13 (sufficiency/completeness/readiness for purpose).

a_rows_sample.anchor:
this is where KnowledgeOS could otherwise make its most dangerous mistake: confusing a generated statement with a logically derived statement. ... A_1,\ldots,A_n\vdash_ho A_{n+1} ... Deduction
eq Induction
eq Abduction
eq Calculation
eq Interpretation
a_rows_sample.statement: Frames Step 10's central danger as confusing a generated statement with a logically derived one, requiring the entailment notation A1,...,An⊢_ρ A_{n+1} to accommodate five distinct inference kinds.

a_rows_sample.anchor: First fundamental distinction ... Derivation \Gamma\vdash_\rho P ... Inference \Gamma\xRightarrow{\rho}P ... Generation LLM(\Gamma)\rightarrow P ... These are not equivalent. LLM(\Gamma)\rightarrow P \not\Rightarrow \Gamma\vdash P. This is one of the most important KnowledgeOS invariants.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the core invariant LLM(Γ)→P ⇏ Γ⊢P, distinguishing Derivation (formal rule-following), Inference (probabilistic/defeasible), and Generation (AI-produced statement) as non-equivalent.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The KnowledgeOS Derivation Object ... D=(P,\Gamma,R,M,\Pi,\Sigma,\tau) ... every derived proposition can answer: How did you get this?
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Derivation object D=(P,Premises,Rule,Method,Provenance,ResultingState,Validity) so every derived proposition can answer 'how did you get this?'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Provenance becomes mathematical ... A_1,A_2\vdash A=C ... D1 Conclusion: A = C ... Premises: A1, A2 ... Rule: Transitivity ... Method: Deduction ... DerivedKnowledge = Rule + Premises + Derivation not merely A = C.
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked transitivity-derivation example showing DerivedKnowledge must record Rule+Premises+Derivation, never just the bare conclusion.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Five major inference families ... \mathcal M=\{Deduction,Induction,Abduction,Calculation,Interpretation\}
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the five-member inference-method family M={Deduction, Induction, Abduction, Calculation, Interpretation}.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Deduction ... Production(x)\rightarrow RequiresBackup(x) therefore RequiresBackup(Nexus). This can be deterministic. ... Deductive inference has a crucial condition: the rule itself must be known and valid. KnowledgeOS therefore needs RuleRegistry. r=(Premises,Conclusion,Context,Version,Authority).
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Deduction as the strongest deterministic form (worked with a Production⇒RequiresBackup rule), requiring a RuleRegistry with rules r=(Premises,Conclusion,Context,Version,Authority) so Γ⊢_r P is computable — connecting to rules/ADRs/manifestos/governance as sources of explicit inference rules.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Calculation ... Revenue=1000, Cost=700, Profit=300 ... f(1000,700)=300. The result is not an LLM opinion. It is ComputedEvidence with a deterministic provenance chain. ... Mathematical calculation ... C=\sqrt{A^2+B^2}=5. Computation \rightarrow Evidence \rightarrow DerivedAssertion.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Calculation as deterministic derivation via a formula (revenue-cost example, Pythagorean example), producing ComputedEvidence with a deterministic provenance chain — Computation→Evidence→DerivedAssertion.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Induction ... Nexus_1=3.69, Nexus_2=3.69, Nexus_3=3.69 ... Nexus_{all}=3.69. But that does not follow deductively. Induction produces support, not logical certainty. ... Acquisition=Induced.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Induction (generalizing from repeated observations, e.g. three Nexus instances all reading 3.69) as producing support, not logical certainty, tagged Acquisition=Induced.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Statistical inference ... \hat\theta=\frac{1}{n}\sum_iX_i ... confidence intervals, posterior distributions, hypothesis tests ... P(\theta\in I) has semantics defined by the statistical method. StatisticalInference\neq DeductiveTruth.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms StatisticalInference ≠ DeductiveTruth: statistical estimates/intervals have semantics defined by the statistical method, not deductive certainty.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Abduction ... Nexus unavailable. Possible explanations: E1 container stopped, E2 network failure, E3 DNS failure, E4 database failure. KnowledgeOS may rank E_1,E_2,E_3,E_4. But Observation\not\Rightarrow Explanation. Therefore abduction produces Hypotheses rather than facts. ... Hypothesis\neq Asser
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Abduction (ranking candidate explanations, e.g. four causes of Nexus unavailability) as producing Hypotheses, not facts — Hypothesis ≠ AssertionOfFact, connecting to the earlier Candidate→Supported→Accepted lifecycle.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Interpretation ... This ADR implies that the architecture board intended X. This is not necessarily deduction. It may involve semantic interpretation; contextual understanding; domain knowledge; human intent. LLM(D,C)\rightarrow I but I=Interpretation not I=Fact. It should carry explicit provenance:
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Interpretation (e.g. inferring an ADR's intent) as distinct from deduction, requiring the result be tagged I=Interpretation, never I=Fact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Analogy ... This architecture resembles the previously approved pattern. That can be useful for Lord. But Similarity\neqIdentity. Therefore analogy generates a candidate inference, not a deterministic fact.
a_rows_sample.statement: Adds Analogy as a sixth method (similarity-based pattern matching useful to Lord), producing only a candidate inference since Similarity≠Identity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: LLM inference ... LLM(D)\rightarrow P. D_{LLM}=(P,\{D\},LLM,GenerativeInference,\Pi,\Sigma,\tau). This means: An LLM generated proposition P from document D. It does not mean D\vdash P.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally places LLM output as its own GenerativeInference method producing D_LLM=(P,{D},LLM,GenerativeInference,Π,Σ,τ), never equated with D⊢P.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This solves the AI problem ... The LLM can perform extraction; classification; summarization; interpretation; hypothesis generation; semantic matching; candidate rule discovery; candidate relationship discovery. But KnowledgeOS distinguishes AI Output from Deterministic Derivation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Lists eight legitimate LLM uses (extraction, classification, summarization, interpretation, hypothesis generation, semantic matching, candidate rule/relationship discovery) while insisting AI Output is always kept distinct from Deterministic Derivation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AI output itself becomes evidence ... e_{LLM} \rightarrow EvidenceAssessment. Its provenance says DerivedFrom(D). LLM output can be evidence, but it is not automatically independent evidence.
a_rows_sample.statement: States LLM output can itself become evidence e_LLM feeding EvidenceAssessment with provenance DerivedFrom(D), but is not automatically independent evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Dependency propagation ... D\rightarrow LLM_1\rightarrow P_1 and then P_1\rightarrow LLM_2\rightarrow P_2. The second output does not become two independent confirmations. The provenance graph preserves D\rightarrow P_1\rightarrow P_2. This connects Step 10 directly to our evidence dependency axioms
a_rows_sample.statement: Traces a two-hop LLM chain (Document→LLM1→P1→LLM2→P2) showing the second output must not be counted as two independent confirmations, connecting to the evidence dependency axioms.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Inference provenance graph ... G_D=(V,E_D) ... nodes include evidence; assertions; rules; calculations; inference results. Edges represent supports; derives-from; contradicts; transforms; supersedes. Then KnowledgeOS can answer: Why does this assertion exist? by traversing P\leftarrow D\leftarrow \G
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines an inference-provenance graph G_D=(V,E_D) with typed node kinds (evidence/assertions/rules/calculations/inference results) and typed edges (supports/derives-from/contradicts/transforms/supersedes), traversable to answer 'why does this assertion exist?'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Rule types ... Logical rule P,Q\vdash R ... Mathematical rule f(x)=y ... Statistical rule X\sim Distribution ... Domain rule Production software requires owner. ... Governance rule Architecture-relevant change requires architecture review. ... Policy rule Two independent sources required for accepta
a_rows_sample.statement: Classifies six rule types (Logical, Mathematical, Statistical, Domain, Governance, Policy) that must not be confused with one another.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Rule provenance ... Rule=(ID,Premises,Conclusion,Scope,Version,Authority,EffectiveTime) ... Suppose an architecture rule changes in 2027. Historical conclusions derived under the old rule must remain reconstructible.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Rule=(ID,Premises,Conclusion,Scope,Version,Authority,EffectiveTime), required so historical conclusions remain reconstructible under the rule version active when derived.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Monotonic versus non-monotonic inference ... Monotonic reasoning ... adding knowledge does not invalidate P. Non-monotonic reasoning ... Adding knowledge may invalidate a previous conclusion. Real-world KnowledgeOS absolutely requires non-monotonic reasoning. ... No evidence that Nexus is internet-f
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues KnowledgeOS absolutely requires non-monotonic reasoning (a default 'probably internal' conclusion overturned by later firewall evidence), connecting to Step 9's belief revision.

b_rows_sample.anchor: An Observation is a recorded representation of something perceived, measured, detected, or otherwise encountered without automatically asserting its interpretation. O = (subject, method, value, time, context). Observation ≠ Interpretation. ... An observation must not silently contain an unmarked conclusion. ... An LLM frequently transforms: 'I found X' into: 'Therefore Y.' KnowledgeOS should preserve that boundary.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Observation = (subject, method, value, time, context) as a recorded representation without automatic interpretation, distinguished from Interpretation and further from Claim (three epistemic levels illustrated by 'Nexus process is listening on port 8081' vs 'Nexus is reachable by application clients' vs 'Nexus architecture permits direct application access'). States the invariant that an observation must not silently contain an unmarked conclusion, warning this is especially important for AI-generated material, which frequently collapses 'I found X' into 'Therefore Y.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: An Inquiry is an intentional epistemic activity directed toward answering a question or resolving uncertainty. I = (question, subject, scope, context, objective). ... Task ≠ Inquiry ... although an Inquiry can generate Tasks. ... Inquiry ⇒ Question/Object. A generic 'Analyze this.' is insufficiently specified unless the intended question can be recovered.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Inquiry = (question, subject, scope, context, objective) as an intentional epistemic activity ('determine something'), distinct from a Task ('do something'), though an Inquiry can generate Tasks (Task != Inquiry). Invariant: Inquiry implies Question/Object -- a generic instruction like 'Analyze this' is insufficiently specified unless its intended question can be recovered.

b_rows_sample.anchor: An observation becomes Evidence relative to an inquiry or claim. Evidence is contextual. E = (O, I, relevance, provenance, integrity). ... Evidence must preserve enough provenance to answer: Where did this come from? At minimum: Source(E) and Method(E). ... Evidence ≠ Proof unless the domain and method justify that terminology. We should use proof sparingly in the book.
b_rows_sample.statement: Evidence E = (Observation, Inquiry, relevance, provenance, integrity) is contextual -- an observation becomes evidence only relative to a specific inquiry/claim, and the same observation can be evidence for multiple inquiries. Minimum required provenance fields: Source(E), Method(E) (and for technical evidence, Time(E), Subject(E)). Distinguishes Evidence from mathematical Proof (Proof => Theorem under a formal system): engineering evidence is generally not equivalent to proof, and 'proof' should be used sparingly.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A governed representation of a claim or proposition whose source, context, validity and epistemic status are sufficiently known for the intended use. K = (claim, source, context, validity, status). ... Evidence supports Knowledge. but: Evidence ≢ Knowledge. ... Knowledge may have states such as: PROPOSED SUPPORTED CONFIRMED CONTESTED SUPERSEDED EXPIRED UNKNOWN ... K1 -- superseded by --> K2. Current truth ≠ Historical truth.
b_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge K = (claim, source, context, validity, status) is 'a governed representation of a claim or proposition whose source, context, validity and epistemic status are sufficiently known for the intended use'; Evidence supports Knowledge but Evidence is not identical to Knowledge. Candidate (non-final) knowledge-status enumeration: PROPOSED, SUPPORTED, CONFIRMED, CONTESTED, SUPERSEDED, EXPIRED, UNKNOWN. Superseded knowledge (K1 superseded-by K2) must not be erased, giving Current truth != Historical truth.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A Determination is a conclusion reached from specified knowledge/evidence under a defined context and method. D = f(K,E,C,M) ... A determination must be explainable. ... 'The AI said so' is not sufficient as a durable determination. ... VerificationResult → supports → Determination. But: VerificationResult ≠ Determination.
b_rows_sample.statement: Determination D=f(K,E,C,M) (knowledge, evidence, context, method) is a conclusion stronger than a casual opinion; invariant that a determination must be explainable via Determination -> Inputs+Method+Context, so 'the AI said so' cannot serve as a durable determination -- the system must be able to answer 'why did we reach this conclusion?' A deterministic VerificationResult (e.g. PASS) supports a Determination but is not identical to it (VerificationResult != Determination); a human/agent determination such as 'the implementation conforms to rule R' is a separate epistemic act built on top of the verification result.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A Decision is an authoritative selection among alternatives, made by an authorized decision-maker or mechanism within a defined governance context. Decision = (choice, authority, scope, context, time). ... Determination ≠ Decision ... Decision ⇒ Authority. ... Recommendation ≠ Decision. An AI may say: 'I recommend rejecting the architecture change.' That is a recommendation. It does not become an authoritative decision merely because the system generated it.
b_rows_sample.statement: Decision = (choice, authority, scope, context, time), an authoritative selection among alternatives made by an authorized decision-maker/mechanism within a governance context; a determination may inform but does not automatically become a decision (Determination != Decision); a decision requires identifiable authority (Decision => Authority, 'who or what had the right to decide?'); an AI recommendation is explicitly not a decision merely because the system generated it (Recommendation != Decision).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Authorization answers: Is this actor permitted to perform this operation under these conditions? Auth = f(actor, action, resource, policy, context, time). ... Decision ≠ Authorization. A governance body can decide that something should happen while an execution system separately authorizes a particular actor to perform it. ... Execute(a) ⇒ ValidAuthorization(a) unless an explicitly defined exception applies. ... Action ≠ Execution ... Execution(Action) produces observable effects.
b_rows_sample.statement: Authorization Auth=f(actor,action,resource,policy,context,time) answers whether a specific actor may perform a specific operation under specific conditions; Decision != Authorization (a governance decision that something should happen is separate from an execution system authorizing a particular actor). Invariant: Execute(a) => ValidAuthorization(a) unless an explicit exception applies. Action ('upgrade Nexus') != Execution ('podman pull ...', the mechanism); Execution(Action) produces observable effects, and Action->Execution->Observation closes the loop.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We started with nouns: Knowledge Evidence Decision Action and initially they looked like possible domain objects. But through the semantic analysis, we discovered that the more fundamental architecture is actually defined by relationships and invariants: supports derivedFrom determines authorizes executes supersedes contradicts observes. ... The domain is not merely: Objects. It is: Objects + Relationships + Invariants + Time + Authority.
b_rows_sample.statement: Major DDD observation: what began as candidate domain-object nouns (Knowledge, Evidence, Decision, Action) turned out, under semantic analysis, to be more fundamentally characterized by named relationships (supports, derivedFrom, determines, authorizes, executes, supersedes, contradicts, observes) and invariants; the domain is therefore relation-centric -- Objects + Relationships + Invariants + Time + Authority -- rather than a plain object model, judged 'much closer to the actual problem KnowledgeOS is trying to solve.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: I1: Observation ≠ Interpretation I2: Evidence ≠ Knowledge I3: Determination ≠ Decision I4: Decision ≠ Authorization I5: Authorization ≠ Execution I6: Unknown ≠ False I7: Provenance ≠ Lineage I8: Memory ≠ Historical Continuity I9: Recommendation ≠ Decision I10: Evidence must be traceable to its source. These should become candidates for the KnowledgeOS semantic constitution.
b_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates a candidate ten-invariant set (I1-I10: Observation!=Interpretation, Evidence!=Knowledge, Determination!=Decision, Decision!=Authorization, Authorization!=Execution, Unknown!=False, Provenance!=Lineage, Memory!=Historical Continuity, Recommendation!=Decision, Evidence must be traceable to its source), explicitly proposed as candidates for a future 'KnowledgeOS semantic constitution' -- not yet ratified.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We have not yet decided: exact bounded contexts; exact aggregates; database schema; event model; API structure; graph technology; microservices; class hierarchy; whether Wisdom deserves its own model; exact implementation of epistemic states. Those decisions belong later. ... Which invariants require a bounded context, which require an aggregate, which require a policy, and which are merely semantic relationships? ... Semantic Contract → Invariant → Consistency Boundary → DDD Boundary.
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 161 explicitly restrains scope: it has not decided exact bounded contexts, aggregates, database schema, event model, API structure, graph technology, microservices, class hierarchy, whether Wisdom deserves its own model, or the exact implementation of epistemic states -- deferred to later steps. Proposes Step 162 (Invariant and Boundary Derivation) to ask, per invariant, whether it requires a bounded context, an aggregate, a policy, or is merely a semantic relationship, via the pipeline Semantic Contract -> Invariant -> Consistency Boundary -> DDD Boundary.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels share the notation 'I1..I10'

a_rows_sample.anchor: INV-ATTR-2/G-2: separation is Declared, NOT attestable. No mechanism can establish who performed an act; assurance rests entirely on where the human starts the session.
a_rows_sample.statement: Finding F-4: role separation between producer, verifier, and approver is Declared, not attestable (INV-ATTR-2/G-2); no mechanism in the estate can establish who actually performed an act, so assurance rests entirely on where the human starts a session -- a capability described as C-5, separation attestation, with no owner today.

a_rows_sample.anchor: this is the first recorded instance of it failing in the FALSE-BAR direction. INV-ATTR-2 anticipated that a process could wrongly claim independence; this event shows the same mechanism can make a process wrongly claim to be barred
a_rows_sample.statement: INV-ATTR-2 ('separation is declared, not attestable') is extended by observed evidence to a second failure direction: not only can a process wrongly claim independence (the failure the invariant was framed against), but the same unverified-self-declaration property can make a process wrongly claim to BE barred, harming an assignment rather than assurance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The platform cannot attest a specified session execution. identity binding must NOT be placed inside C-10's authoritative state, because C-10 cannot establish it. It is C-5-shaped
a_rows_sample.statement: The sharpest finding in the D3 prep: a C-10 receipt's binding to a specific session execution can never be stronger than what INV-ATTR-1/INV-ATTR-2 permit (self-declared, not attested), so identity binding cannot be placed inside C-10's authoritative state -- it is C-5-shaped, and C-5 owns no attestation record either.

a_rows_sample.anchor: One prohibition, three surfaces: an unresolved status may never be laundered into a resolved one.
a_rows_sample.statement: A single cross-cutting prohibition is observed recurring in three independent places in the estate's governance (independence classification, C-5 separation dimensions, D4.1 compensating controls, later a fourth at D4.3 M4): an unresolved epistemic status must never be laundered into a resolved one -- recorded as an observation bearing on, but distinct from, the canonical unifying-invariant candidate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This process is not a neutral party to this question... It has an interest in concluding that that record is worth preserving.
a_rows_sample.statement: Full process-disclosure practice: a producing process discloses its own prior participation and interest in the outcome (having authored the canonical analysis, D5, and prior governance registrations) and binds itself out of later verifying or accepting its own work (R-34/P-2).

a_rows_sample.anchor: This process is not a neutral party to this question, and the reason is specific... many of the 210 transitions and 99 grants whose durability is the subject of this ADR were recorded by this process.
a_rows_sample.statement: Full conflict-of-interest disclosure: the ADR's producer recorded many of the transitions whose durability is under analysis, has an interest in concluding the record is worth preserving, and binds itself out of approving, verifying, or accepting its own ADR.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the Governance actor was correct to refuse to decide. That refusal is actually evidence that the separation model is working.
a_rows_sample.statement: The PO/ARB's own observation, recorded as OBSERVED evidence: a producer bar held under direct pressure to breach it, twice, without an exception being requested, is evidence that the separation-of-authority model is functioning; the registering process explicitly draws no conclusion about C-5 (separation attestation) ownership from it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the S4b lane's registered executionContext names the producer as claude-code-session:5e1dd9ee. The plan 3817eb2b was produced by claude-code-session:1c8b041b.
a_rows_sample.statement: INFO-2: a provenance discrepancy exists in the governance record itself (not the plan) — the plan discloses its own producer correctly, but the lane's registered executionContext names a different process as producer; reconciling this is left as a Governance act.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C-12's principle — author ≠ independent reviewer, not author ≠ every prior reviewer — would make it authoring-eligible again, and repeated authoring remains a QUALITY RISK rather than an independence failure.
a_rows_sample.statement: Clarifies an eligibility rule already precedented in the chain: the exclusion rule is 'author ≠ independent reviewer', not 'author ≠ every prior reviewer who ever touched this artifact' — a process that authored earlier amendments remains eligible to author a later, different correction, though the repetition itself is recorded as a quality risk rather than an independence failure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Independence — the seven criteria, all required ... distinct process/session identity ... is not a continuation/compaction/fork/resume lineage of a barred producer
a_rows_sample.statement: States a seven-criterion independence test (process identity, non-authorship of the artifact/prior corrections/prior verifications, non-lineage from a barred producer, non-inherited working context) with the rule that a different session ID alone is insufficient; if lineage cannot be established the classification must be NOT ATTESTED, never PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Independence is not one property ... Role independence ... Authority independence ... Access independence ... Organizational independence ... Financial independence ... Technical independence ... Temporal independence ... Cognitive independence
a_rows_sample.statement: Decomposes 'independence' into eight distinct dimensions and a six-level evidence-strength ladder (self-declaration through independent external assessment), concluding a platform can prove some dimensions (recorded identity difference, access-enforced separation) but not others (no collusion, no cognitive bias, organizational independence) from metadata alone.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A reviewer checking only the two names it was handed would have PASSED this gate and proceeded ... this is exactly why the same commission forbids hand-copied grant lists: the chat-supplied exclusion set was narrower than the governed one.
a_rows_sample.statement: Demonstrates the failure mode of trusting a prompt-supplied exclusion list rather than the governed record: the chat-supplied set of two barred names missed a fourth clause that fires on a registered grant covering the same performer under a different role in this same chain.

a_rows_sample.anchor: a REGISTERED act that is not live is a FALSE RECORD — and here it would falsely assert that an independent reviewer is at work on the gate that exists to guarantee independence.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the converse of the estate's 'a live but unregistered act still counts as missing' rule: a registered-but-not-live START is a false record, which is the worse failure direction on the one gate whose purpose is guaranteeing independence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 'Fresh' is satisfied in the sense the record can test — no prior participation. It cannot mean 'no knowledge of the estate': this session read MEMORY.md and CONTEXT.md at startup via the repository's SessionStart hook, which is disclosed here rather than left to be discovered.
a_rows_sample.statement: Narrows what 'fresh' can mean under the record's own tests: no prior participation is provable; absence of any estate knowledge is not, and unavoidable bootstrap reading is disclosed rather than concealed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: independence is not transferable: an assignment whose recorded evidence names a8ce5a39 cannot be discharged by 8a525719 without the record asserting something false about who did the work.
a_rows_sample.statement: Names a second-order independence failure distinct from personal ineligibility: a genuinely independent process cannot discharge a review under a workflow lane whose registered execution context names a different process, since INV-ATTR-1 means the engine itself would never detect the substitution.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I will not adopt another process's identity in order to become operable.
a_rows_sample.statement: States a refusal principle: a process must not adopt a different, already-registered process's self-declared identity merely to satisfy a commission's addressee field and become operable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: a live but unregistered act still counts as missing ... a REGISTERED act that is not live is a FALSE RECORD.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the estate's two-directional recording rule as the reason a chat-delivered commission cannot substitute for a recorded START transition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 'It is CODE provenance, never AI-process attestation: nothing here asserts who produced the artifact (EKS-07 stays unsolved; self-declared process identity is not independently attested authorship).' — scripts/lib/EngineeringKnowledge/Shared/Domain/HandoffContext.php:11–15
a_rows_sample.statement: AI processes are first-class actors (they invoke CLIs, author artifacts, and record transitions -- e.g. recordedBy:architecture on 2 HANDOFF transitions), but their identity cannot be established by any mechanism: tier-1 source states verbatim that this is code provenance, never AI-process attestation (EKS-07 unsolved); self-declared process identity, as practiced (e.g. a document declaring its producer as claude-code-session:5e1dd9ee), is explicitly marked 'self-declared and NOT attestable.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: What EKS does not do with AI processes ... No process identity ... No cross-process notification ... No agent registry ... No capability restriction. Every hook is advisory; nothing an AI process can do is prevented by EKS.
a_rows_sample.statement: EKS explicitly does not: issue/record/verify any AI-process identifier (self-declaration is the practice); notify concurrent processes of each other's actions (discovery is only by re-reading files, EKS-07); register any AI process in registry.yaml; or restrict any AI-process capability (every hook is advisory; nothing an AI process can do is prevented by EKS).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Exactly one mutation owner per work item is a mechanically enforced invariant (I-1)
a_rows_sample.statement: Grants: a grant without a humanActRef is refused by the engine ('the record never manufactures authority -- G-2/R5b'). Exactly one mutation owner per work item is mechanically enforced (I-1). Closure is a governance act (G-1): COMPLETE refuses any writer but governance/human. Producer != acceptor (R-34, INV-ATTR-2): a process cannot verify/accept its own work; separation is declared, not attestable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-4/C-7: ADDRESSED BUT NOT CLOSED ... DV-1 — the one unsafe-direction gap ... the durable copy is written twice after its last all-or-nothing verification ... and re-verified nowhere.
b_rows_sample.statement: AMD6's independent review finds a genuine safety gap (DV-1) in the durability migration plan: the durable authoritative copy is written after its last all-or-nothing verification and never re-verified before the source is removed, so Phase 7's gate could report success while the durable copy is silently incomplete.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 'the FIRST record in the authoritative store' is false under the plan's own record vocabulary ... Truth is 'first governance append after the writer switch'
b_rows_sample.statement: Names DV-3: the migration plan's acceptance criterion 17 uses an inaccurate phrase ('first record in the authoritative store', which is literally false because Phase 3 already copied records into it) and must be replaced by 'first governance append after the authority transfer.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Phase 5 remains prohibited ... DV-1 is the critical one because it creates an unsafe path to Phase 7.
b_rows_sample.statement: Prescribes the next lawful sequence after the DV-1..DV-7 findings: register/route a new Architecture correction commission only (not a Governance decision document), then Architecture authors the fix, then a fresh independent Architecture review, then Governance's bounded review, then PO/ARB; Phase 5 must not execute until DV-1 is repaired and reviewed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The durability migration chain (AMD3→AMD6) is literally the test corpus the assurance checker is being built to back-test against, and the checker's job list is literally the migration's own mandated pre-delivery verification.
b_rows_sample.statement: Finds that the two seemingly separate work items (cost-optimization/deterministic-assurance, and the durability migration) already share the same evidence base and back-test corpus, so integration is a sequencing/authority problem rather than a new architecture problem; the checker must remain warn-only through Phase 1 to avoid itself becoming a governance object requiring authority.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DV-1 = UNSAFE ... Business: Migration must not start yet because there is still a real risk of losing governance evidence.' Not: Migration is almost finished.
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked counterexample showing what an incorrect over-simplified business translation would say versus the correct uncertainty-preserving translation of the DV-1 durability finding.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Decision status is graded, not monolithic: ADR artifact = PROPOSED ('recommends an architecture and decides nothing'); a separate PO/ARB DECISION ACT (2026-08-19) = DECIDED: D1 = B′ adopted, D2 = R-CONFLICT adopt, D3 = existing placement governance.
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes that decision status must be read as a graded record: an ADR document being PROPOSED does not contradict a separate PO/ARB decision act having already DECIDED specific numbered items from it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: D9 | Separation: source of execution vs evidence of execution vs authoritative decision record (B′ relocation, R-CONFLICT) | DECIDED (PO/ARB 2026-08-19, D1–D2) — recorded, not re-decided here
b_rows_sample.statement: Reconciliation-document claim register entry D9: the three-way separation and B′/R-CONFLICT decisions are recorded here as already DECIDED by a separate PO/ARB act, never re-decided by this reconciliation document itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1 RE-HASH ... 1b RECONCILE/DISPOSE DELTA ... 2 READERS ... 3 THE WRITER ← THE AUTHORITY-TRANSFER INSTANT ... 4 RUNTIME DEMOTION MARKER ... 5 STAGING MARKER RETRACTION
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the single canonical Phase-5 slot sequence (1, 1b, 2, 3, 4, 5) with slot 1b's three outcomes (no delta/continue, reconcilable delta/continue, unreconcilable delta/freeze-violation-STOP), replacing two previously-competing enumerations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A MOVE is refused because it would LAUNDER THE QUARANTINE — a post-demotion record lies OUTSIDE the enumeration by definition, so moving it out HIDES the quarantined evidence, makes the source SPURIOUSLY SATISFY criterion 12.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects an earlier, inverted justification for forbidding a quarantined record's relocation (previously reasoned as 'would alter the demoted store'); the true reason is that moving it would make a failing Phase-7 comparison spuriously pass.

b_rows_sample.anchor: OPEN-M7 — quarantine disposition — the disposer AND the path ... The one open item that can block the migration's COMPLETION indefinitely.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies that the workflow mechanism has an act class for disposing a quarantine (a governance act) but literally no DISPOSE transition type, so an undisposed quarantine can block migration completion indefinitely by design, not by oversight.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A quarantine is a DOMAIN STATE with a business consequence, not a directory condition. The block is not a tooling limitation to engineer away — it is the aggregate refusing an invalid transition.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes quarantine-blocking-completion as a DDD invariant (an aggregate refusing an invalid state transition) rather than a filesystem/tooling limitation to be worked around.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the switch-over record is the FIRST GOVERNANCE APPEND AFTER THE AUTHORITY TRANSFER (⛔ superseded wording: 'that store's first record' — false, not merely imprecise: Phase 3 has already copied governance records into that store.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the acceptance-criterion phrase describing the authoritative store's identifying record: it must read 'first governance append after the authority transfer', not 'that store's first record', because prior copied records already exist there.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the grant count moved 110 → 114 since AMD5, and it is C-4's premise observed live: those four grants are AMD6's OWN commission, appended by P-1 into the corpus the migration freezes and hashes.
b_rows_sample.statement: A self-referential observation: the ongoing governance work authorizing this very amendment is itself appended to the corpus the migration plan proposes to freeze, meaning a literal freeze would have had to prohibit the act that authorized the amendment.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ELIGIBILITY OUTCOME AS RECORDED: bc1b47ef - AUTHORING ELIGIBLE, REVIEWING BARRED, ACCEPTING BARRED ... A FRESH INDEPENDENT ARCHITECTURE PROCESS - REVIEWING ... REQUIRED.
b_rows_sample.statement: A registered grant explicitly restores a producer's authoring eligibility while permanently barring it from reviewing or accepting its own amendment (AMD6), which the reviewer here reads directly from the record rather than inferring.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A reviewer checking only the two names it was handed would have PASSED this gate and proceeded ... this is exactly why the same commission forbids hand-copied grant lists: the chat-supplied exclusion set was narrower than the governed one.
b_rows_sample.statement: Demonstrates the failure mode of trusting a prompt-supplied exclusion list rather than the governed record: the chat-supplied set of two barred names missed a fourth clause that fires on a registered grant covering the same performer under a different role in this same chain.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1 PO/ARB starts a FRESH Architecture session ... 2 that session DECLARES its own identity ... 3 GOVERNANCE ... appends REGISTER ... then HANDOFF ... 4 START recorded with THIS PO/ARB act as its humanAct ... 5 the fresh reviewer consumes G-…-DV-CORRECTION-READING-ORDER as its index
b_rows_sample.statement: Prescribes the exact five-step lawful sequence that would unblock the deadlocked reviewer-appointment problem without a barred process appointing its own judge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: THE REVIEWER MUST BE A FRESH INDEPENDENT ARCHITECTURE PROCESS ... Satisfied on the measurement in §2.2: this is a process with no registered role in the chain.
b_rows_sample.statement: Demonstrates the independence-verification method in practice: enumerate every process occurrence across all transitions and grants in the aggregate plus a whole-repository grep, and treat zero occurrences as the only admissible basis for eligibility.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the reviewer must not be its own registrar — the same reason bc1b47ef refused to appoint its own judge, applied to the other end of the same edge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends the 'a barred process must not appoint its own judge' principle to its symmetric case: an eligible candidate reviewer must also not register/hand-off its own assignment, since separation is the entire point of the lane.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the eligibility set keeps narrowing — every candidate reviewer that declares eligibility and is then not started adds one more name to it.
b_rows_sample.statement: Observes a structural risk pattern: repeatedly declaring and abandoning candidate reviewers without recording a START permanently shrinks the pool of processes still eligible to review, since each attempt itself becomes a disqualifying prior-participation fact.

b_rows_sample.anchor: independence is not transferable: an assignment whose recorded evidence names a8ce5a39 cannot be discharged by 8a525719 without the record asserting something false about who did the work.
b_rows_sample.statement: Names a second-order independence failure distinct from personal ineligibility: a genuinely independent process cannot discharge a review under a workflow lane whose registered execution context names a different process, since INV-ATTR-1 means the engine itself would never detect the substitution.
