a_rows_sample.statement: Registers a cosmetic naming observation (O-1): the protocol's 'HANDOFF' filename segment overlaps EKS-07's coordination vocabulary even though the scope language already disambiguates it; recommends the existing scope language be kept and a clearer title be considered.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ADOPTED AS OPERATIONAL PRACTICE ... The protocol does NOT: create authority · assign ownership · create workflow transitions · create humanAct · start sessions · approve artifacts · replace Governance · implement EKS-07
a_rows_sample.statement: Records the verbatim human PO/ARB decision adopting the Session Completion & Handoff Protocol as ADOPTED OPERATIONAL PRACTICE, with an explicit enumerated NOT-list of what the protocol does not do.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ⛔ .claude and .codex are NOT updated yet. Agents may follow a protocol only after Governance has accepted it. No implicit adoption without governance registration.
a_rows_sample.statement: States a sequencing constraint deferring agent-template deployment (.claude/.codex) until after explicit Governance acceptance, preventing implicit adoption.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Governance records this decision; it did not make it. ... this registering session is also the protocol's producer. This registration records the human act; it does not constitute — and cannot substitute for — producer acceptance of its own work (R-34/P-2).
a_rows_sample.statement: Discloses that the session registering the PO/ARB's adoption decision is also the protocol's own producer, and explicitly states that registering a human decision is not the same act as producer acceptance of one's own work.

a_rows_sample.anchor: V1 | F1 distinguishes capability from authorization | PASS ... V2 | F3 references the real End-of-Commission checklist | PASS ... V6 | No broken cross-references / orphaned sections | PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Runs a six-item verification matrix (V1-V6) against the protocol's v1.1 controlled revision (F1/F3), each check citing specific line numbers and cross-corroborating against workflow-state.php and the End-of-Commission checklist; verdict CONFORMANT.

a_rows_sample.anchor: agent templates ... 'now permitted' ... is the producer's own, self-declared judgment — no explicit acceptance record appears in this commit.
a_rows_sample.statement: Registers one non-blocking observation: the protocol's own next-steps line asserts agent-template deployment is 'now permitted' post-adoption, but this reading is the producer's self-declared judgment rather than an explicit recorded Governance-acceptance act; recommended to be treated as still gated pending an explicit registration.

a_rows_sample.anchor: After a governed session finishes, the human should not need to reverse-engineer the next responsible actor.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the protocol's one-line thesis and defines the mandatory twelve-field Session Completion Report structure (Work Item, Current Role, Session Identity, Completed Work, Evidence Produced, Current State, Remaining Obligations, Recommended Next Actor, Reason, Human Decision Required, Can Current Session Continue, Continuation Reason).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Independent Reviewer | a review | Governance | Reviewer cannot accept its own review ... Any role | no declared next actor fits | PO/ARB | no declared actor — decision authority escalates to the human
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines deterministic actor-recommendation rules (fixed mappings from completing-role+completed-obligation to next actor) plus four constraint rules: no inventing roles, the independence/producer-bar rule, the authority rule (only PO/ARB decides/approves), and that a recommendation assigns nothing.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ⚡ Amendment v1.1 — Continuation Assessment (F1: capability ≠ authorization) ... answering YES is a capability statement, never an authorization statement.
a_rows_sample.statement: Applies the v1.1 F1 amendment distinguishing operational-continuity capability from authorization: 'Can Current Session Continue: YES' never means ownership granted, authority transferred, workflow started, human decision completed, or artifact acceptance granted — authorization remains controlled by workflow state, Governance decisions, humanAct requirements, and ownership rules.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This protocol consumes workflow information. It does NOT replace — and does NOT add to — the workflow engine. | The protocol answers 'Who should act?' | The workflow engine decides 'Who is allowed to act?'
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the boundary between the protocol and the workflow engine: the protocol consumes Current State and active-grant context, authors none of it, and never passes ownership (ownership passes only on START per G-3).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Relationship to Existing Completion Controls (amendment v1.1 — F3) ... This protocol does not replace existing completion checklists ... a complement (consume/relate — ES-005.4, never a second) — never a parallel completion process.
a_rows_sample.statement: Applies the v1.1 F3 amendment explicitly cross-referencing the End-of-Commission checklist ('has the session completed its obligations?') as a complementary, never duplicate, discipline to this protocol's 'who should act next?' question, per ES-005.4.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Rel(kos, ai, "Bootstraps and constrains AI sessions") Rel(ai, kos, "Executes assigned work under grants")
b_rows_sample.statement: The KnowledgeOS system bootstraps and constrains AI sessions, and the AI/Agent Runtime executes assigned work under grants -- a two-directional relation between the governed platform and executing AI sessions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Component(workflow, "Workflow Engine", "Governed workflow", "Grants, assignments, handoffs, mutation ownership and transitions")
b_rows_sample.statement: The Workflow Engine component is defined as owning grants, assignments, handoffs, mutation ownership and transitions -- the governed-workflow mechanism later referred to throughout the batch as BC-7 / the workflow-state engine.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Rel(review, verification, "Routes independent verification")
b_rows_sample.statement: A Review Engine component is proposed whose role is to route independent verification and preserve role separation, distinct from the Verification Engine component itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ContainerDb(estate, "Knowledge / Workflow Estate", "Git + governed records", "Architecture artifacts, ADRs, reports, workflow JSON, source and tests")
b_rows_sample.statement: A single durable 'Knowledge / Workflow Estate' store (git + governed records) is proposed as the persistence layer for architecture artifacts, ADRs, reports, workflow JSON, source and tests.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The architecture lane S4 was HANDED_OFF at seq 5 and NEVER returned to ACTIVE
b_rows_sample.statement: Programmatic check of the workflow record shows the architecture lane producing Amendment 1 held mutation ownership at HANDOFF but never received a START/CONTINUATION afterward, meaning Amendment 1 was produced by a lane not verifiably ACTIVE on the record -- distinguished from whether its claims are independently assessable (they are).

b_rows_sample.anchor: every invariant BC-7 owns is MECHANICALLY enforced; almost every invariant outside BC-7 is DECLARED ONLY. INFERRED: the platform's assurance is strong exactly where it is executable and weak exactly where it is prose -- and a role model is prose.
b_rows_sample.statement: The discovery's core structural result: BC-7's invariants (I-1 single mutation owner, I-2 HANDOFF+human START, I-3 sticky STOPPED, G-1 closure is a governance act, G-2 single writer for the Authority State) are all mechanically enforced, while almost every invariant outside BC-7 (R-34 producer!=acceptor, INV-ATTR-2 separation, AIP-11 frozen-artifact supersession, AIP-14 Product Primacy) is declared only, with no enforcement mechanism.

b_rows_sample.anchor: this verification lane has no START on the record, so this report is produced off-record, the second occurrence at the "Verification #3" slot in this estate.
b_rows_sample.statement: Finding X-2: this verification's own workflow lane has no recorded START, meaning the report is produced off-record -- the second occurrence of the same lifecycle-gap pattern at a 'Verification #3' slot across this estate, classified as a platform gap (bearing on C-10/knowledge-distribution and G-3) rather than a defect of Correction #2.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Correction #2 finished its work and said so in the artifact, but its lane never handed off -- it still held mutation ownership when this act arrived.
b_rows_sample.statement: A recurring delivery/record gap pattern is recorded: an artifact states it is delivered, but the lane that produced it never performed the corresponding HANDOFF transition, so the workflow record lags the actual work; Governance performs the handoff now rather than back-dating it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: X-2 is a live blocker ... the work item's mutationOwner is None: seq 14 handed off to a lane that then never STARTed, so ownership was released and never taken up. Consequently no lane can hand off
b_rows_sample.statement: A workflow lane that is HANDED_OFF to but never STARTed leaves mutationOwner as None, mechanically blocking every subsequent lane's handoff (Inv C requires the current mutation owner to hand off) -- a live, measured blocker rather than a theoretical one, confirmed by probing a scratch copy of the record.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Option A -- transcribing the missing START -- is not available to Governance. A transcription records a human act that was given. No such act exists in this lane's record, and Governance may not supply one.
b_rows_sample.statement: Governance determines it cannot itself transcribe a missing human START act, because a transcription records a fact (that a human act occurred) which only the PO/ARB can supply; Governance instead retains the report as evidence produced off-record, leaving option A open to the PO/ARB at any time.

b_rows_sample.anchor: restoring append-only history is itself a history edit, two lanes were writing this file the same day, and a restoration performed without authority would repeat the very defect it repairs.
b_rows_sample.statement: Governance declines to restore 73 deleted lines from an append-only session log, reasoning that restoring append-only history is itself a history-edit and could repeat the defect it would fix; it instead recommends preserving current history with an explicit recovery-commit pointer.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The record is not broken. It is exactly ONE HUMAN ACT short.
b_rows_sample.statement: Diagnosis: the entire workflow chain is blocked by exactly one missing human START act; once the PO/ARB affirms it occurred, Governance transcribes the START (preserving on the record's face that the artifact predates the transition) and the blocked handoff chain unblocks in one move.

b_rows_sample.anchor: There is an important distinction between the role model and the workflow state machine. The roles tell us who may act; the lifecycle tells us what happens and in what order.
b_rows_sample.statement: A foundational distinction is drawn between the role model (who may act) and the workflow state machine (what happens and in what order), presented as two separate but related layers of the governed AI engineering lifecycle.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A deliverable being produced is not the same thing as its lifecycle being closed.
b_rows_sample.statement: A critical rule surfaced from the BC-7 history: a deliverable being produced (content exists) is not the same thing as its lifecycle being closed (the governed record reflects it) -- the earliest statement in this batch of the delivery/record gap pattern that recurs dozens of times in later documents.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A lane cannot hand off work the record does not show it ever started. ... Governance will not manufacture the START, and will not record the bootstrap form from: null
b_rows_sample.statement: Governance refuses a directed HANDOFF because the predecessor lane, though it produced a delivered artifact, was never STARTed on the record and therefore holds no mutation ownership; refuses both manufacturing a START and using a null-predecessor bootstrap form, because either would falsely assert something about the record.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the START sits at seq 25, later in the log than the work it authorized. This is recorded deliberately and is not an error to be tidied ... no historical ordering is invented
b_rows_sample.statement: A governance transcription convention is established: when a human act is confirmed after the fact, its transition is recorded at its true (later) sequence position, not back-dated to appear before the work it authorized -- the record states explicitly that the artifact predates the transcription.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A later act is not automatically a supersession. Act B may be an amendment superseding Act A, a re-issue that crossed with it, or a duplicate. ... Until Governance disposes, a0b61305 remains the recorded DECIDED text
b_rows_sample.statement: A general governance principle: a later act arriving on an already-DECIDED slot is not automatically read as superseding it; until Governance explicitly disposes of the relationship (amendment, re-issue, or duplicate), the earlier recorded DECIDED text remains authoritative.

b_rows_sample.anchor: acts and records have crossed four times -- seq-16 and seq-22 transcriptions, the seq-21 producer designation, the S4b missing START, and now two D1 acts.
b_rows_sample.statement: A cumulative pattern is named explicitly: the record and the governed acts on this work item have crossed (diverged and required reconciliation) four separate times, treated as a recurring structural pattern each disposed individually by Governance rather than absorbed silently.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Handing off from S5 would set S5 to HANDED_OFF, misrepresenting an OUTSTANDING verification as concluded. ... a lane with no recorded handoff can never legally START. ... Registering an assignment now would create a permanently unreachable lane.
b_rows_sample.statement: Governance declines to register a new workflow lane for D5, because the current mutation owner (S5, an outstanding/refused verification) would need to hand off, which would misrepresent that verification as concluded; instead D5 proceeds as a PO/ARB-directed act, deferring the lane-creation question until S5's disposition is settled.

b_rows_sample.anchor: HANDED_OFF means the lane RELEASED MUTATION OWNERSHIP. It does NOT mean the verification was performed. a lane that refused on independence now reads, in the state column, indistinguishably from lanes that finished their work.
b_rows_sample.statement: A workflow-engine state-vocabulary risk is named: the HANDED_OFF state denotes only that mutation ownership was released, not that any verification, consumption, or acceptance occurred -- so a lane that refused on independence grounds becomes indistinguishable, in the raw state column, from a lane that actually finished its work, requiring explicit clarification for any later reader.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Never infer ontology directly from representation without establishing the intended semantic interpretation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Records Williamson's constraint (Modal Logic as Metaphysics): never infer ontology directly from representation without establishing the intended semantic interpretation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: How do we compare competing conceptual systems without prematurely declaring one of them the truth?
a_rows_sample.statement: Records Williamson's comparison-of-competing-conceptual-systems question and notes it is precisely the condition this extraction itself is in (eight Kernel formulations, six Knowledge genera, four incompatible relation classifications, no adjudication authority); the implied answer (compare without declaring) matches S1-F013's UNRESOLVED verdict and this extraction's own preserve-don't-reconcile discipline.

b_rows_sample.anchor: TRUE != BELIEVED != KNOWN / ASSERTED != ACCEPTED != TRUE / CONFIDENCE != TRUTH / UNKNOWN != FALSE ... Absence of knowledge must not be represented as falsehood.
b_rows_sample.statement: Williamson's contribution: knowledge is not whatever an agent believes, has epistemic requirements and intrinsic limits; motivates an explicit state vocabulary (UNKNOWN, ABSENT, INSUFFICIENT, QUESTIONABLE, CONFLICTED, REJECTED, VALIDATED, SUPERSEDED, WITHDRAWN) with the exact governed vocabulary left as a domain-law question.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS must never silently turn "supported" or "probable" into "known."
b_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge is factive: a factive attitude can only be directed toward truths; Williamson treats knowing as the most general factive stative attitude, distinct from believed(P)/supported(P)/probable(P)/asserted(P), all of which 'may be false' while known(P) is factive. This should be a Kernel-level safeguard: never silently convert 'supported' or 'probable' into 'known'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Williamson rejects the assumption that knowledge can be completely separated into an internal mental part and an external-world part... he explicitly describes knowledge as broad
b_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge is broad: K_A(P) depends not only on A's internal representation but on the external world, context, object of knowledge, and relevant environment. This revises the earlier Agent->projection->Knowledge Space model: the agent does not invent the space, the agent's knowledge is constitutively connected to the space (KNOWLEDGE SPACE Ω -> external world/social reality/semantic structures -> participant/agent -> capacity+access -> epistemic state).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Capacity is not knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: A Williamson-inspired correction to the earlier 'knowledge might be a capacity to write information and define its scope' idea: capacity is not knowledge. A system can have high representation capacity (an LLM generating text, a database storing petabytes) without knowing anything. Instead: capacity determines what a participant can potentially represent/investigate/distinguish/communicate; knowledge is a factive epistemic relation/state involving the participant and the external target (CAPACITY -> access/observation/reasoning -> epistemic state -> KNOWLEDGE).

b_rows_sample.anchor: He argues for the **primeness** of knowledge and warns against decomposing it into composite conditions when doing so loses explanatory generality.
b_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge may be prime (non-composite): a maximally detailed decomposition can make an explanation worse by destroying useful generalization. This strengthens the earlier Merricks 'non-redundant work' principle (a candidate primitive deserves first-class status if removing it destroys non-redundant capability) into two tests: the Reduction test ('Can X be reconstructed?') and the Primeness test ('Does treating X as a composite destroy explanatory/general structure?').

b_rows_sample.anchor: Williamson argues that people are not always in a position to know whether they know something. He calls the mistaken assumption that important mental conditions are cognitively transparent **luminosity** and argues against it.
b_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge is not luminous (anti-luminosity): KnowledgeOS cannot assume a participant can perfectly report the state of its own knowledge. 'Agent says I know P' is itself an assertion requiring evaluation; 'Agent says I don't know P' does not necessarily prove P is outside its epistemic capacity. This is a major correction to the previous model of UNKNOWN, requiring KnowledgeOS to distinguish KNOWLEDGE / KNOWLEDGE ABOUT KNOWLEDGE (K_A(K_A(P))) / SELF-ASSESSMENT / EXTERNAL ASSESSMENT / COMPUTATIONAL ESTIMATE as non-equivalent layers, with the second not automatically following from the first.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The agent's **self-report of knowledge** is therefore an object of analysis, not a privileged oracle.
b_rows_sample.statement: For an AI agent claiming 'I know that the architecture decision is valid', KnowledgeOS should be able to represent P, the AI's claim knows(P), the supporting evidence, an external assessment (e.g. 'insufficient'), and the actual status ('unresolved') separately — the agent's self-report of knowledge is an object of analysis, not a privileged oracle.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Williamson's Chapter 5 investigates margins and "close possibilities."
b_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge has a margin: an agent may know P under ordinary circumstances but not under arbitrary tiny variations, so knowledge is not simply a point (TRUE) but can have a 'neighbourhood of epistemic safety'. Proposed quantity M(P,A,C) represents the size/structure of the range of relevant variations under which the knowledge attribution remains stable (not a final formula) — high margin means knowledge remains stable under nearby changes, low margin means small changes may destroy knowledge. This connects the topological lens to epistemology: 'What kinds of changes would invalidate the knowledge attribution?'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Williamson discusses contextual variation in epistemic standards but does not reduce truth/knowledge to arbitrary subjective standards.
b_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge is contextual but not arbitrarily relative: different epistemic contexts (S_t^A, S_t^B, S_t^G) can differ in their knowledge attributions, but this does not mean 'everything is equally true' — different knowledge attributions still point to the same underlying Knowledge Space, supporting the idea that different participants are oriented toward the same infinite space.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Williamson separates causal basis from evidential basis.
b_rows_sample.statement: Cause of belief is not the same as evidence for belief: a perceptual process can be probabilistically caused by the environment without the resulting evidence itself being probabilistic in the same way. This is a non-collapse rule — KnowledgeOS must preserve both relationships (causal basis, evidential basis) separately.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Williamson's Chapters 9–10 develop the idea that **knowledge itself can function as evidence**, and he explicitly identifies one's evidence with what one knows within his framework.
b_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge can be evidence (E=K): observation -> knowledge -> evidence for another proposition -> new knowledge, a recursive structure where the Knowledge Space is not simply 'evidence -> knowledge' but can contain 'knowledge -> evidence -> inference -> knowledge', making knowledge a participating element in reasoning, not merely a final storage state.

b_rows_sample.anchor: He explicitly shows that evidential probability 1 should not be treated as absolute certainty, and that treating evidence as permanently probability-1 creates an implausible monotonicity problem. New evidence can undermine something previously regarded as evidence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Evidential probability 1 must not be treated as absolute certainty; treating evidence as permanently probability-1 creates an implausible monotonicity problem since new evidence can undermine something previously regarded as evidence. This validates Gärdenfors's distinction between historical evidence and permanently-unquestionable evidence: KnowledgeOS evidence history should be immutable, but epistemic status may be revised.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Williamson's Chapter 11 argues for a **knowledge account of assertion**: the connection between knowing and asserting is not accidental.
b_rows_sample.statement: Assertion is downstream from knowledge (knowledge account of assertion): the earlier model 'knowledge -> language' is refined to KNOWLEDGE -> warrant to assert -> ASSERTION -> language/communication. The sentence itself is not the knowledge; the assertion act is a consequence of an epistemic state and a communicative norm, close to Searle's distinction between descriptive and constitutive/performative language.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ### K-INV-01 — Factivity cannot be silently violated
b_rows_sample.statement: Seven proposed Kernel invariants: K-INV-01 Factivity cannot be silently violated (a record labelled 'knowledge' cannot silently mean merely belief/claim); K-INV-02 Representation is not knowledge (storage alone confers no epistemic status); K-INV-03 Knowledge attribution is contextual (must identify participant, scope/context, time); K-INV-04 Self-report is not self-proof ('I know P' is not sufficient proof P is known); K-INV-05 Evidence can be revisable (historical evidence records remain, interpretation can change); K-INV-06 Knowledge history is reconstructible (a current projection must be traceable to its inputs/transformations); K-INV-07 No assumption of epistemic transparency (the system must permit 'I don't know that I don't know P' and incomplete metaknowledge generally).

b_rows_sample.anchor: ### Kernel should preserve
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposed Kernel boundary (inside/outside/above): Inside Kernel — identity, participant, context, boundary, time, representation provenance, observation/source, proposition/content reference, knowledge attribution, epistemic transition, evidence/history, relationships, conflict, revision/supersession, question/inquiry, assessment history, regime reference. Outside Kernel — words, sentences, documents, embeddings, LLMs, vector databases, specific statistical models, possible-world machinery, Bayesian machinery, Pramāṇa implementation, Pāṇinian grammar, topic taxonomy, UI, search algorithm, explanation algorithm. Above the Kernel — knowledge projections, topics, answers, explanations, reports, architecture views, governance views, AI-agent views. Knowledge is present in the Kernel not as Truth+Belief+Evidence but as a KNOWLEDGE ATTRIBUTION (participant -> knows -> proposition -> context/time/boundary/regime), respecting primeness while remaining operational.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The Kernel should not silently overwrite this into: P = KNOWLEDGE
b_rows_sample.statement: The Kernel should NOT decide whether P is 'knowledge' universally. Example: for P='System X is secure', KnowledgeOS may preserve 'Alice claims to know P', 'Audit A provides evidence E', 'Regime R assesses P', 'Verification V says unresolved', 'Bob says not proven' as a KnowledgeAttribution(participant, proposition, context, time, regime, provenance) without collapsing to P=KNOWLEDGE, allowing different epistemologies/regimes to coexist and evaluate independently.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Stop trying to construct "knowledge" bottom-up from representations.
b_rows_sample.statement: The biggest insight: stop trying to construct knowledge bottom-up from representations (words->sentences->propositions->evidence->truth->knowledge is conceptually backwards). Instead: Infinite Knowledge Space -> Knowledge relation/state, which can be represented, asserted, justified, serve as evidence, influence action, or be revised/lost. Representation is a downstream expression of a knowledge-bearing state, not what creates knowledge. This also re-interprets the earlier S_t=P(Ω|A,B,L,U,R,t,H) formula: it is not 'the state of Knowledge itself' but 'a projected epistemic representation of knowledge at t', and K_t^A(P) becomes a knowledge attribution 'Agent A knows P at time t under the relevant context/regime.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: We should not seek: KnowledgeScore ∈ [0,1] as the first objective. Instead quantify **properties of knowledge**
b_rows_sample.statement: Reject a universal KnowledgeScore ∈ [0,1]; instead quantify properties of knowledge Q(K,P,C,t) = (Evidence, Reliability, Margin, Coverage, Consistency, Relevance, Provenance, Stability). Candidate measurable properties: knowledge margin (how much nearby change before attribution fails), evidence contribution (removing evidence e, how much epistemic support changes — Williamson compares total-evidence hypothesis support against support after removing one item), explanatory value (how much knowing P improves prediction/explanation via probability/correlation), knowledge stability (how often an attribution is revised/lost under new evidence), projection coverage (how much declared scope has actually been represented).

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS must be able to represent uncertainty about its own epistemic boundary.
b_rows_sample.statement: Do not try to make the Kernel completely transparent to itself (anti-luminosity applied to the system itself); a system claiming to know exactly what it knows and does not know makes an extremely strong assumption. KnowledgeOS must represent uncertainty about its own epistemic boundary via states: KNOWN, UNKNOWN, UNKNOWN WHETHER KNOWN, DISPUTED, OUTSIDE CURRENT MODEL, UNASSESSED — with 'unknown whether known' being particularly important.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The Knowledge Space is an unbounded space of reality, meaning, institutional structures, events, relations and propositions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Final synthesis: 'The Knowledge Space is an unbounded space of reality, meaning, institutional structures, events, relations and propositions. Persons, machines and organizations have limited capacities and therefore form bounded, contextual, time-dependent projections of that space. Knowledge is a factive relation/state within such a projection—not merely information, representation, belief, evidence or truth alone. KnowledgeOS preserves the identities, contexts, provenance, temporal histories, epistemic transitions and knowledge attributions necessary for those projections to be reconstructed and evaluated under different regimes.' Capstone principle: KnowledgeOS must not confuse the projection with the space, the representation with the knowledge, or the epistemic assessment with reality — supported by McGinn, Floridi, Dretske, Fagin, Gärdenfors, Searle, and Williamson jointly.

b_notations: Timothy Williamson, Knowledge and Its Limits
